title: Why I abandoned law for acting – Femi Adebayo
summary: Femi Adebayo left litigation in 2005, saying acting offered greater financial rewards and fulfilment. His father had hoped he would pursue law.
body:
Nollywood actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo says he left legal practice in 2005 to pursue acting and film production, drawn by the work’s financial rewards and the greater fulfilment it brought him. He discussed the decision in an interview on the Afrobeats podcast, published on Saturday, reflecting on his career and his upbringing in an entertainment family.

Adebayo was called to the Nigerian Bar in 2003 and spent about two years practising litigation. He said he appeared in court and handled cases before deciding to leave law. Acting, which began as a hobby, had become the work he felt more passionate about, he explained, and he found it made him happier than the career he had studied for.

He said his father, veteran actor Adebayo Salami, known as Oga Bello, initially welcomed his choice to study law. Salami had wanted to become a lawyer himself but, according to his son, lacked the financial resources to pursue legal studies. Adebayo said his father’s reaction to his eventual departure from law was mixed: he was glad his son was following him into acting, but had also hoped to see him continue in the profession he had once wanted for himself.

Adebayo said his father later became grateful for the path he chose. His work has since extended across several parts of filmmaking, including acting, producing, writing and directing. His account describes a transition from a short period in litigation to a full-time career in entertainment, shaped by both personal interest and the practical rewards he saw in the industry.

title: Police Arrest Two Suspects For Staging Abduction In Ebonyi
summary: Police in Ebonyi arrested two people accused of staging a kidnapping to seek ₦30 million. The alleged victim’s father reported the abduction on October 31.
body:
Police in Ebonyi State have arrested two suspects over an alleged plot to stage a kidnapping and demand money. The case began at about 10:30 p.m. on October 31, 2026, when the father of one of the suspects contacted the police control room to report that his son had been abducted from his hostel in Ikwo Local Government Area.

Police spokesperson SP Joshua Ukandu said the father had received view-once videos and voice notes showing his son bound and apparently held captive. The people claiming to be the abductors demanded ₦30 million and threatened to kill the young man if the money was not paid.

Ukandu said police launched an intelligence-led investigation into the reported abduction. After sustained surveillance and discreet inquiries, officers arrested the two suspects on the night of November 5, 2026, as they came out of the room where they had been hiding, he said. The statement did not provide further details about the suspects or indicate whether charges had been filed.

Ebonyi State Commissioner of Police CP Hope Urunwa Okafor warned against staging kidnappings or making false abduction claims. She said such schemes cause serious distress to families and divert police resources from genuine security threats, adding that the conduct is a criminal offence punishable under the law.

title: US Air Force captain arrested in Japan
summary: Japanese police arrested a 27-year-old US Air Force captain on suspicion of drunk driving in Okinawa. Whether he breached a US military curfew is unclear.
body:
Japanese police arrested a 27-year-old US Air Force captain on suspicion of drunk driving in Okinawa on Saturday. A prefectural police spokesman said the man was driving in Okinawa City at about 3:09 a.m. The captain was assigned to Kadena Air Base, according to a report by Kyodo News.

Police said it was unclear whether the captain had violated a curfew imposed by US officials. The base did not immediately provide comment.

The arrest came a week after Japan and the United States agreed on measures to prevent crimes by US service members in Okinawa. The agreement followed public anger over a murder allegedly involving an American Marine.

About 54,000 US military personnel are stationed in Japan, most of them in Okinawa. US officials had also announced an extension of a curfew for lower-ranking service members through December 7 and a ban on all service members drinking alcohol outside their homes between midnight and 5 a.m.

title: 2027: Aaro Meta urges Kwara South APC to back Danladi
summary: Aaro Meta urged Kwara South APC members to back Yakubu Salihu Danladi for 2027, citing fairness among the state’s three senatorial districts. It also called for party unity.
body:
Political group Aaro Meta has urged aggrieved All Progressives Congress members in Kwara South to reconcile and support the party’s governorship candidate, Kwara State House of Assembly Speaker Yakubu Salihu Danladi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group also endorsed a candidate from Kwara North, saying political power should be shared fairly among the state’s three senatorial districts.

Coordinator Adebayo S. Daramola made the appeal on Friday at a News Keg event organised by the Nigeria Union of Journalists’ Correspondents’ Chapel in Ilorin. He said Aaro Meta had supported the 2018 O to Ge movement, which contributed to the APC-led government taking office in 2019, and argued that sustaining the party’s electoral prospects required unity and fairness.

The group recalled that it backed an APC candidate from Kwara Central in the 2019 governorship election despite being based in Kwara South. That candidate, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, won the election and secured a second term in 2023. Aaro Meta said Kwara South should show similar political accommodation by supporting Danladi, rather than allowing divisions over preferred aspirants to weaken the party.

Aaro Meta said Kwara South had produced a governor for eight years since 1999, while Kwara Central would have accounted for 20 years in office by the end of AbdulRazaq’s tenure in May 2027. It appealed particularly to dissatisfied APC members and the G-15 political bloc to work for Danladi and other party candidates, warning that internal disputes could give opposition parties an advantage.

The group also praised President Bola Tinubu and Governor AbdulRazaq for efforts to address banditry and kidnapping, saying insecurity in Kwara South had declined. It identified the Oro Forest corridor, from Oro-Ago and Oreke Road towards Egbe, Okoloke and Lade, as a continuing concern. It described military bases in Oro-Ago and Babanla, and the 184 Battalion in Omu-Aran, as strategic to tackling the threat.

title: Who Gets To Compete?
summary: Campaigns are advancing and opposition talks continue. Violence, legal uncertainty and INEC’s preparations are testing access and confidence in the 2027 vote.
body:
Who Gets To Compete?

As campaigns gather pace and opposition figures discuss cooperation, questions about access, legal certainty and confidence in the vote are becoming central to the contest. Recent events have ranged from Peter Obi’s visit to a community affected by violence to an APC mobilisation rally and public questions about the electoral commission’s preparations. Together, they highlight that competing for votes also depends on candidates being able to organise and citizens being able to participate safely.

A reported attack on an NDC town hall gathering in Oregun, Lagos, left participants injured, according to reporting from the scene, and a suspect was arrested. The NDC alleged political responsibility, while the Lagos APC denied sponsoring the incident. The available reporting did not establish independent evidence linking the attackers to a political party. An investigation must determine who was responsible; meanwhile, political meetings should be accessible without fear of assault. Intimidation can deter attendees, volunteers and venues, affecting the conditions in which candidates compete.

Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde confirmed active discussions involving Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, saying any decision should consider evidence, manifestos, past performance and public sentiment. He did not announce an agreement or endorse a candidate. Separately, INEC chairman Joash Amupitan said the commission would comply with binding court decisions concerning Atiku’s participation and noted that it faces more than 300 pending cases. The ADC says it has appealed a November 5 ruling and sought a stay of execution; the material available does not establish that a stay has been granted. The dispute remains unresolved in the information provided.

Obi visited people affected by the June 2025 attack in Yelwata, announced support for orphaned children’s education and a borehole, and held a town hall in Makurdi with running mate Rabiu Kwankwaso. In Akure, Vice-President Kashim Shettima represented President Bola Tinubu at an APC rally, calling for unity and mobilisation. The campaign set a target of 1.2 million votes in Ondo, an aspiration rather than a forecast. Rally activity and organisation do not establish how voters will decide.

INEC has announced a nationwide mock accreditation exercise for November 28 to test accreditation and electronic result transmission. Amupitan said the commission had procured additional BVAS devices and reduced the maximum number of voters assigned to each machine from 1,250 to 850. The exercise’s effectiveness remains to be tested; transparent findings on performance, problems and corrective steps would help voters assess the commission’s assurances. No fresh, credible polling in the material reviewed establishes a national shift. The standard for the coming weeks is whether lawful contenders can be heard, citizens can participate without intimidation and votes can be counted credibly.

title: Tinubu Hails Bakassi Seaport, Says Project Will Create Jobs, Boost Trade
summary: President Bola Tinubu said the Bakassi Deep Seaport will widen Nigeria’s trade routes and create jobs. The project is designed to ease pressure on Lagos ports.
body:
Tinubu Hails Bakassi Seaport, Says Project Will Create Jobs, Boost Trade

President Bola Tinubu has described the groundbreaking of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State as a step towards diversifying Nigeria’s economy, expanding trade and creating jobs. Vice President Kashim Shettima represented him at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday, November 13, 2026. Tinubu commended Governor Bassey Otu and the state’s residents for advancing a project first conceived in 2014.

Designed with a 20-metre draft, the port is intended to receive large vessels that currently bypass Nigerian ports. A planned 260-kilometre superhighway would connect it to markets across the country. Tinubu said the facility would complement Lagos, which handles more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade, by easing congestion and reducing the country’s reliance on a single maritime gateway. He said Nigeria handles only a fraction of regional cargo trade despite the importance of sea transport to commerce.

Tinubu credited Otu with helping to address institutional and financial obstacles, including efforts to secure a $3.5 billion financing arrangement with Afreximbank and formalise the project’s Public-Private Partnership framework in February 2025. Otu said the groundbreaking followed years of political, administrative, legal and environmental challenges. He cited an initial funding approval of $2.27 billion, federal approval for the project and preparatory work including environmental, hydrographic, geotechnical and geophysical studies.

Otu said the port could support employment and business in logistics, shipping, fishing, tourism and shipbuilding. Selected Cross River residents are receiving specialised training for construction and operational roles, he said. The governor also pointed to a corridor linking the state’s airport, seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway as a route for cargo and investment, and invited maritime-sector investors to consider opportunities in the state.

Marine and Blue Economy Minister Gboyega Oyetola pledged his ministry’s support for a modern, efficient and environmentally sustainable port. He said the project could improve market access and create industrial and employment opportunities, with benefits extending beyond Cross River. Tinubu urged residents to protect the project from political interference and described it as an investment for future generations.

title: Lagos NDC meeting attack threatens democracy — APM candidate
summary: Lagos APM candidate Prince Laja Adeoye condemned an attack that disrupted an NDC town hall in Ikeja. He called for arrests and protection of political gatherings.
body:
Lagos State governorship candidate Prince Laja Adeoye of the Action Peoples Movement has condemned an attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress supporters at a town hall meeting in Ikeja, calling the disruption a threat to democracy. The meeting was held on Thursday at Classique Event Centre in Oregun.

Adeoye said disrupting the gathering infringed on citizens’ rights to assemble and express political views. He warned that attacks on opposition events could increase political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also said the incident was especially concerning in Lagos, which he described as a traditional centre of political activity.

The APM candidate urged the Lagos State Police Command to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible, regardless of their political affiliation or status. He cautioned that failing to hold perpetrators accountable could encourage similar incidents elsewhere. Adeoye also raised concerns about the safety of voters, candidates and journalists during the campaign period, citing reports that a journalist covering the meeting was attacked and had working equipment taken.

Adeoye commended NDC supporters for not retaliating and called on political leaders and parties to discourage violence and focus campaigns on issues. He urged INEC, security agencies and other stakeholders to work together to ensure fair conditions for all parties, and called on the National Peace Committee and civil society organisations to promote peaceful political engagement. He also sympathised with people reportedly injured in the attack and urged the NDC to continue its campaign. Adeoye said the APM remained committed to peaceful, credible and transparent elections and respect for the rule of law.

title: Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians over immigration offences – Report
summary: Malaysian authorities arrested 112 African nationals in immigration operations from January through October 31, including 53 Nigerians. Most were detained for lacking valid permits.
body:
Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians in immigration operations

Malaysia’s Immigration Department arrested 112 African nationals in enforcement operations conducted across the country between January and October 31, according to figures disclosed by department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban. Nigerians made up the largest group, with 53 arrests, followed by 13 Ugandans, 10 Kenyans and eight Ghanaians.

The remaining arrests included six each from Somalia and Tanzania, four from Senegal, three from Algeria, and two each from Burkina Faso, Togo and The Gambia. One person each from Guinea, Zimbabwe and Libya was also detained.

Shaaban said the most common offence was entering or staying in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. That offence accounted for 85 arrests, including 47 Nigerians. A further 23 people were detained for overstaying under Section 15(1)(c), while three were arrested for breaching the conditions of their immigration passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. One Nigerian was also arrested over alleged possession of forged documents under Section 56(1)(l) of the Act.

Authorities separately arrested an Algerian employer under Section 55B of the Act for allegedly employing foreign workers without valid passes. Shaaban said enforcement operations were intended to address undocumented migration and take action against employers who employ or accommodate foreign nationals without proper immigration documents. The report did not identify the Nigerians arrested or specify where they were apprehended.

title: Best performing money market funds in Nigeria as of October 2026
summary: First Ally led Nigeria’s money market funds in October with a 21.17% year-to-date yield. Sector assets rose 5.05% to N6.90 trillion.
body:
First Ally Money Market Fund retained the top position in Nigeria’s money market fund rankings in October 2026, recording a year-to-date yield of 21.17%. The sector’s net asset value reached N6.90 trillion as of October 30, up 5.05% from N6.56 trillion in September. It comprised 50 funds following the addition of Custodian Money Market Fund and represented 68.31% of the N10.09 trillion mutual fund market.

DLM Money Market Fund placed second with a 20.47% yield, followed by Coronation at 20.31%, RT Briscoe Savings & Investment Fund at 20.19%, Page at 19.53% and Custodian at 19.52%. CardinalStone recorded 19.38%, Zedcrest 19.12%, Apel Wealth 18.98% and STL 18.93% to complete the top 10. STL narrowly held the final place, finishing 0.01 percentage point ahead of the fund ranked 11th, Comercio Partners.

Yields at the top of the table generally eased during the month: six of the seven funds that remained in the top 10 recorded lower year-to-date yields than in September. The top-10 entry threshold also declined, from 19.01% to 18.93%. CardinalStone was the exception, rising 0.07 percentage point to 19.38%. Custodian and Zedcrest entered the top 10, while Page returned after last appearing in August. First Ally’s yield fell from 21.43% in September, but it remained ahead of DLM by 0.70 percentage point.

Money market funds continue to attract retail and institutional investors seeking liquid options focused on capital preservation. Their returns remained attractive even as fixed-income yields moderated following the Central Bank of Nigeria’s September reduction of the Monetary Policy Rate from 26.5% to 23%. On the reported year-to-date figures, a hypothetical N5 million investment in First Ally at the start of the year would have generated about N1,058,500 in returns by October. Coronation was the largest fund in the top 10, with N126.28 billion in assets, while RT Briscoe was the smallest, with N736.06 million.

title: Atiku wanted me as running mate in 2023 – Makinde
summary: Seyi Makinde says Atiku Abubakar asked him to be running mate in 2023, but he declined, citing limited experience. He also discussed the PDP, governance and security.
body:
Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde says former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar approached him to be his running mate in the 2023 presidential election. Makinde said he declined because he had spent only three years as governor and felt he lacked enough experience in public service to take on the role. He discussed the offer and other aspects of his political career in an interview.

Makinde also spoke about the G5 governors’ opposition to Atiku’s 2023 bid and the continuing crisis in the Peoples Democratic Party. He said he was the only member of the G5 who had since left the party. He defended his faction’s decision to expel former Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike, saying it was intended to enable the PDP to contest the election, even with a weakened structure. Makinde also questioned the state of democracy, citing disputes over the nullification of candidates less than 80 days before a national election.

Responding to claims by the Oyo State All Progressives Congress that he had neglected governance for political activity, Makinde said state administration was continuing. He pointed to his presentation of the 2027 budget estimates to the State House of Assembly and his state-of-the-state address. He also said his preferred successor, former commissioner Bimbo Adekanbi, should develop his own political identity, and rejected the description of himself as a political godfather.

On security, Makinde backed decentralised decision-making and state police, arguing that states should be able to tailor responses to local conditions. He said safeguards would be needed to address concerns that state policing could be used oppressively. Referring to kidnappings of pupils and teachers in Oyo and Borno states, he said Oyo had secured the release of those abducted, though the incident involved casualties. Makinde said a judicial panel had submitted its report on the Oyo incident and that a government white paper was due within the week.

title: Beside Adamawa Government House, school battles decay, thirst
summary: Dougirei Secondary School in Yola lacks reliable water, safe classrooms and basic learning facilities. Parents and staff are urging Adamawa officials to address the problems.
body:
Beside Adamawa Government House, school battles decay and thirst

Dougirei Secondary School, in Yola North Local Government Area, is less than 100 metres behind the Adamawa State Government House. Yet pupils and staff face deteriorating classrooms, insufficient desks and chairs, no functional water supply and a shortage of other basic facilities. During a visit, teachers and some students were seen working under trees, while the staff room shared by the junior and senior sections was described as too cramped for personnel.

Classroom ceilings are falling apart, raising concerns about safety. The school has no working water supply, leaving its toilets closed and students to use nearby bushes. It also lacks an examination hall: students sitting external examinations, including WAEC and NECO, have had to do so outdoors, using stones as seats. Staff said science subjects are taught without a laboratory, limiting opportunities for practical lessons. Some teachers bring mats to use as seats and work surfaces.

Flooding adds to the difficulties during the rainy season. Water discharged through drainage pipes from Government House is reportedly channelled into the school grounds, sometimes disrupting lessons and prompting the management to suspend activities over safety concerns. Parents-Teachers Association chairman Alhaji Mohammed Usman said he had written several times to the Ministry of Education without receiving a satisfactory response.

The school’s condition has prompted questions about how the state’s education priorities are being implemented. The administration has introduced free education and school feeding in boarding schools and has announced plans for model secondary schools across the state’s 21 local government areas. Budget figures cited in the report show education allocations of N17.32bn in 2020, N24bn in 2021, N17.3bn in 2022, N26.8bn in 2023, N15.603bn in 2024, N40.41bn in 2025 and N40.63bn in 2026. Stakeholders are calling for greater transparency over how the funding is used and for action on basic school infrastructure. The education commissioner was unavailable for comment, and calls had not been returned by the time the report was filed.

title: Lagos taskforce raids Cele, Itire, Ilasamaja, arrests 3 suspected drug peddlers
summary: Lagos State Taskforce raids in Cele, Itire and Ilasamaja led to three arrests over alleged drug sales. The suspects pleaded not guilty in court.
body:
The Lagos State Taskforce says it has arrested three people in raids on suspected criminal hideouts in Cele, Itire, Ilasamaja and other parts of the state. The operation was led by the agency’s chairman, Chief Superintendent of Police Adetayo Akerele, and targeted locations identified as hotspots for drug activity and public disturbances.

The agency alleges the suspects sold and distributed marijuana, Colorado and Indian hemp to adults, underage people and street urchins around Cele Bus Stop, Itire and Ilasamaja. It said the activity had reportedly contributed to public disturbances, street fights, cult-related activity and youth violence in the affected communities.

The suspects were identified as Bello Musa, 18, and Abubakar Musa, 27, both of Adebayo Street, Cele-Ijesha, and Agboola Fuad, 24, of Sewage Street, Abaranje, Ijegun. According to the taskforce, they have been arraigned on three counts relating to possession and sale of illicit drugs, inciting members of the public against officers carrying out lawful duties, and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace. All three pleaded not guilty. The case was adjourned until December 9, 2026, for further proceedings.

During the operation in Itire, Akerele thanked a whistleblower and residents for their cooperation. He said public participation and timely sharing of information helped identify and remove suspected criminal elements from communities. Speaking at the agency’s headquarters in Bolade, Oshodi, he urged residents to report suspicious activity and work with law enforcement.

Akerele also warned young people against drug activity, street violence and cultism, and urged them to avoid associations that could expose them to criminality. He said the taskforce would continue enforcement against drug peddling, environmental nuisances and other criminal activity, and warned that those who violate applicable laws would face legal consequences.

title: US Congress Steps Up Scrutiny Of Trump, Nvidia After Huang Exit
summary: Lawmakers are seeking answers about the Trump administration’s knowledge of Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China. The inquiry also covers chip exports.
body:
US lawmakers from both parties are calling for answers about what the Trump administration knew of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman suspected by US intelligence of working for China. The scrutiny intensified Thursday after Nvidia’s board announced Huang’s immediate departure as chief executive. China has denied the allegations against the woman, Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed; the two are not related. Jensen Huang acknowledged the affair on Sunday.

The controversy has renewed debate over US sales of advanced chips to China. Jensen Huang had advocated looser export rules, while lawmakers are also questioning Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to restrict sales. Reports have said President Donald Trump was informed of the suspicions last year and that Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May. Trump said Monday that the FBI was looking into the affair and that Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Congress should seek answers from Huang and Nvidia about possible risks to national security. He also questioned what the administration did after learning of the relationship, including whether officials were told not to investigate, and what Trump knew when he invited Huang aboard Air Force One for a state visit to China in May. Senate Republican leader John Thune said a congressional investigation would make sense given the national security stakes.

Three Republican House committee chairmen have said they want to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18. Democratic lawmakers are also preparing to examine the matter: the top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees wrote to Lutnick Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s approval and taxation of chip exports to Chinese firms linked to China’s government and military. They accused Lutnick and Trump of overlooking a national security threat despite reportedly being informed of the suspicions.

Democrats may also examine potential conflicts of interest. Nvidia has said its reported $25 million pledge toward a White House ballroom project was unrelated to its business interests; the pledge reportedly came months after chip sales to China resumed. The calls for scrutiny come days before Trump is due to travel to China.

title: FG hands Port Harcourt airport to private operator for 30 years
summary: Nigeria has granted Port Harcourt Airport Company a 30-year concession for the Port Harcourt airport. The government says the deal aims to improve operations and attract investment.
body:
The Federal Government has granted Port Harcourt Airport Company Ltd. a 30-year concession to operate the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Aviation and Aerospace Development Minister Festus Keyamo announced the agreement at a signing ceremony in Abuja on Thursday. He said the arrangement had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council.

Keyamo said the concession was intended to ease the cost of running airports that operate at a loss and attract private investment. The government currently uses profits from major airports to support less profitable facilities, he said. Airport expenses include staff, electricity and diesel for generators, while the government has limited resources to develop commercial services beyond passenger and aircraft operations. Private participation, he added, could improve efficiency and help airports generate more revenue.

The minister said earlier administrations had tried to concession the Port Harcourt airport but faced resistance from aviation unions and lengthy legal disputes. The current administration engaged with unions to address workers’ concerns and safeguard their welfare, he said. Speaking for the concessionaire, R28 Holdings Group Executive Eyo Asuquo said the deal would create jobs rather than lead to job losses. He also pledged substantial infrastructure investment, with the aim of bringing the airport up to standards comparable to facilities in Europe and the United States.

The government has also received concession proposals for Benin Airport and Yola International Airport. The Port Harcourt agreement follows the formal concession of Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Enugu, signed on January 21, 2026. The deals are part of the government’s effort to bring private investment into aviation, improve infrastructure and operations, and reduce the financial burden of managing public airports.

title: ‘His Support Base Still Strong’, Doherty Says Obi Can Repeat 2023 Feat In Lagos
summary: Funso Doherty says Peter Obi retains strong support in Lagos and could repeat his 2023 result. His remarks followed an attack that disrupted an NDC town hall.
body:
Funso Doherty, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Lagos, says Peter Obi retains the support needed to repeat his 2023 performance in the state. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Doherty rejected the suggestion that Obi’s move from the Labour Party to the NDC would weaken his appeal, arguing that voters are drawn to his political outlook rather than his party label.

Doherty said Obi’s reception remained strong and warned that politicians who dismissed his influence could misjudge the public mood. He pointed to the response of NDC supporters during an attack on the party’s town hall meeting as evidence that the enthusiasm seen during Obi’s 2023 campaign had not faded.

The meeting at Classic Event Place in Oregun, Ikeja, was disrupted before Obi and other party figures arrived. Suspected political thugs, reportedly carrying cutlasses, cudgels and stones, allegedly vandalised property and damaged vehicles at the venue. Supporters confronted the attackers, throwing chairs as they tried to drive them away, before security operatives intervened. The gathering later went ahead, with Obi, Victor Umeh and activist Aisha Yesufu among those attending. Doherty condemned the incident as unprovoked and unnecessary, and praised supporters who resisted it.

In the 2023 presidential election, Obi finished third nationally but won Lagos, receiving 582,454 votes against 572,606 for Bola Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate. The APC has governed Lagos for 27 years, and Tinubu, a former state governor, has had substantial political influence there. Obi is seeking the presidency again in 2027, this time as the NDC candidate. Doherty said he believes the opposition can defeat the APC in Lagos, arguing that the party’s long-standing dominance is not insurmountable.

title: FG reviews 932 laws, drops 269 obsolete enactments
summary: The Federal Government reviewed 932 enactments and 731 subsidiary laws for the proposed 2025 compilation. Officials gave differing totals for laws retained and excluded.
body:
The Federal Government has completed a review of 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations for a proposed 2025 edition of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria. At the report’s presentation in Abuja, Attorney General of the Federation Lateef Fagbemi said 663 enactments and their relevant subsidiary legislation were identified for inclusion, while 269 were classified as obsolete, spent or repealed.

Committee chairman Olawale Fapohunda gave a slightly different breakdown: he said 664 enactments and accompanying subsidiary legislation had been cleared for inclusion, with 268 dropped. The figures were presented at the same event. The committee also submitted draft copies of the proposed edition, arranged in 20 volumes, to Fagbemi for consideration and further executive action.

The review follows the last official consolidation of federal laws in 2004. Fagbemi said the intervening years had brought legislative, constitutional, institutional and technological changes, as well as new laws and amendments, making an updated and accessible collection necessary. He said the report would be presented to President Bola Tinubu for transmission to the National Assembly for legislative consideration.

Fapohunda said the committee used 14 thematic working groups and digital collaboration tools to review and harmonise the legislation. Its work also identified matters needing further attention, including outdated statutory language, cross-references and chapter numbers, inconsistencies in the sequencing of Acts, and fines and fees that no longer reflect current economic conditions. The committee recommended guidance for ministries, departments and agencies on reviewing their laws, a centralised repository of federal legislation, and a continuing process for updating the laws so another lengthy gap between consolidations can be avoided.

title: DMO raises N5.06 billion from November savings bonds, down 17.4%
summary: The DMO allotted N5.06 billion in November FGN Savings Bonds, 17.4% less than October’s N6.12 billion. Subscription numbers also fell, despite higher rates.
body:
The Debt Management Office (DMO) allotted N5.06 billion through its November 2026 Federal Government of Nigeria Savings Bond offer, down 17.4% from the N6.12 billion allotted in October. The November total was about N1.06 billion lower, and the number of subscriptions received also declined.

The allotment comprised N746.01 million in the two-year bond and N4.31 billion in the three-year instrument. The offer was open from November 2 to 6 and settled on November 11. Annual interest rates were 13.25% for the two-year bond and 14.25% for the three-year bond.

The lower November allotment came despite an increase in the rates offered on both tenors. The available results do not specify how many subscriptions were received or give a breakdown of the change in participation. They do show that less was allocated to investors through the retail bond offer than in October.

FGN Savings Bonds are among the government’s domestic borrowing instruments. The DMO also manages larger FGN bond issuances; in June 2026, it announced an approximately N4 trillion auction plan for the third quarter. The November results follow a period of higher allotments in the retail government securities market during the first nine months of 2026.

title: EFCC appeals judgement lifting forfeiture order on $912,550 linked to ex-Warri refinery MD
summary: The EFCC has appealed a ruling that lifted an interim forfeiture order on $912,550 linked to former Warri refinery MD Jimoh Yisawu. The criminal case is separate.
body:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has appealed a Federal High Court ruling that rejected its bid to permanently forfeit $912,550 and other assets linked to Jimoh Olasunkanmi Yisawu, a former managing director of the Warri Refining and Petrochemical Company. Judge James Omotosho ruled on Monday that the commission had not proved the assets were proceeds of crime, lifted an interim forfeiture order on the funds and dismissed its application for final forfeiture. The EFCC said it filed a notice of appeal at the Court of Appeal in Abuja on Tuesday.

In its appeal, the commission argues that the judge failed to evaluate and properly weigh evidence about Yisawu’s income and financial transactions. It says the evidence showed that he gave $912,550 in cash to bureau de change operators Samaila Bala and Rasheed Yusuf between 2021 and 2025 for conversion to naira, with an equivalent value of more than N1.5 billion. The EFCC contends that Yisawu did not explain how he converted his lawful earnings into the foreign currency.

The commission also points to Yisawu’s declared cash and bank balances of N647,205.36 and $12,779.26 as of 17 September 2020, and says his salaries and allowances from October 2020 to September 2023 totalled N114,548,024.48. It further alleges that the dealers indirectly paid N282,542,000 towards developing two properties sought for forfeiture, and that Bala paid N65,860,000 to Cordros Securities Limited for treasury bills in three instalments in February 2024. The EFCC says these payments were not linked to Yisawu’s lawful earnings.

The EFCC is asking the appeal court to overturn the ruling and order final forfeiture of the funds and properties to the federal government. Yisawu, who worked for the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation for 32 years before leaving in September 2023, told the lower court that he acquired the properties between 2015 and 2020 using earnings and loans. The forfeiture proceedings are separate from a criminal case in which he pleaded not guilty to eight money-laundering charges involving N1.339 billion. The EFCC’s allegations in both matters remain allegations; the appeal concerns the forfeiture ruling.

title: Russia’s Ambassador to US, Alexander Darchiev, dies at 66
summary: Russia says Ambassador to the United States Alexander Darchiev has died at 66. The Foreign Ministry announced his death but gave no details about the circumstances.
body:
Russia’s Foreign Ministry has announced the death of Alexander Darchiev, the country’s ambassador to the United States. He was 66. The ministry gave no details about the circumstances of his death, describing him in a tribute as an outstanding diplomat, an experienced leader and a kind colleague.

Darchiev was appointed to the Washington post in March 2025, shortly after Donald Trump returned to power. Before that, he served as Russia’s ambassador to Canada from 2021 to 2024.

A specialist in relations between Russia and the United States, Darchiev led the Foreign Ministry’s North America Department from 2014 to 2020. His appointment to Washington came as relations between Russia and Western countries were strained over Moscow’s military offensive in Ukraine.

After Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Darchiev described the military action as a necessary measure. The Foreign Ministry’s announcement did not provide further information about his death.

title: Nigeria 2027 Election Watch: The Battle For The Ballot Deepens As Parties Lose Candidates, Gain Defectors And Confront The Courts
summary: Party defections, candidate withdrawals and court disputes are reshaping preparations for Nigeria’s 2027 elections. Peace Committee findings also raise concerns about violence and misinformation.
body:
Political parties preparing for Nigeria’s 2027 elections face a mix of defections, candidate changes and unresolved legal disputes. Recent developments in Sokoto, Kano, Cross River and Ogun highlight pressures on party organisation and nominations, while findings from the National Peace Committee raise concerns about the conditions for campaigning and participation.

In Sokoto, a state government statement issued on November 10 reported that PDP and ADC officials and organisers had joined the APC. The reported defectors included state executive officials and local party chairmen. Some accounts put the number of departing PDP local-government chairmen at seven, although six are clearly identified in published names. They are party officials, not elected council chairmen. The defections may affect local party structures, but do not establish that voters will follow them.

In Kano, a letter dated November 9 announced a six-month caretaker committee for the ADC, led by Musa Ungogo. The appointment comes amid earlier state-level disagreements and a national leadership dispute. On November 5, the Federal High Court invalidated decisions by the David Mark-led national executive, including the process that produced Atiku Abubakar as the party’s presidential candidate. The ADC has appealed and sought a stay of execution; neither an appellate reversal nor a granted stay has been confirmed. ADC candidates have also petitioned international missions and organisations over the judgment and delays in obtaining a certified copy. Their petition does not change the court ruling or establish that every candidate has been excluded from the ballot. The party’s nominations and INEC’s response remain matters of legal uncertainty.

In Cross River, NDC deputy governorship candidate Stella Charles Archibong withdrew from the ticket and declared support for Governor Bassey Otu’s re-election campaign through the Back to South Movement. NDC candidate John Odey said consultations were continuing. No replacement has been independently verified on INEC’s published list. In Ogun, a Federal High Court judgment scheduled for Friday, November 13, is expected to address PDP candidate Ladi Adebutu’s exclusion from INEC’s governorship list. INEC says his name was not on the party membership register it originally submitted; Adebutu and the PDP dispute the basis for his exclusion. Those are competing claims before the court, not judicial findings.

The National Peace Committee recorded 109 reported breaches of the electoral Peace Accord from August 19 to October 27, across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory. The findings include 33 reported incidents involving violence or political thuggery and 29 involving misinformation. They cover more than two months, not a single day. Together, the developments concern distinct issues: party organisation, nomination continuity, legal eligibility and the safety of political participation. None by itself demonstrates a shift in voter preferences, but resolving disputes and addressing threats to free participation will be important to public confidence in the process.

title: DSS Intercepts Arms Shipment From Niger Republic In Sokoto, Arrests Female Courier
summary: DSS operatives intercepted 21 AK-47 rifles, four machine guns and 825 magazines in Sokoto, reportedly smuggled from Niger. Separately, a woman was arrested in Zamfara.
body:
The Department of State Services (DSS) intercepted a shipment of weapons and ammunition in Dawakawa, Goronyo Local Government Area of Sokoto State. The consignment comprised 21 AK-47 rifles, four PKT machine guns and 825 magazines. A security source said the weapons had been smuggled into Nigeria from the Niger Republic and were intercepted after surveillance and intelligence gathering on suspected terrorist networks. The source placed the operation less than 70 days before the 2027 general elections.

Separately, DSS operatives arrested Hafsat Umar in Talata Mafara Local Government Area of Zamfara State earlier in the week. She was allegedly carrying 12 grenades and two ammunition belts. According to the source, intelligence indicated she had travelled to Niger State to obtain ammunition for delivery to suspected bandit leader Saidu Marafa, who was described as based in Kani Kawa, Maradun Local Government Area. The source said Umar would be charged in court.

The source said increased interceptions had led criminal groups to try other ways of transporting illegal arms, including using women and camels. The DSS has reported female-courier arrests in Zamfara, Nasarawa, Ebonyi, Taraba, Kaduna and Plateau states. Cases cited include the recovery of 202 rounds of AK-47 ammunition and three empty magazines from Aisha Mohammed in Keffi, Nasarawa State, and the arrest of two suspected couriers in Ebonyi in September 2026, when operatives recovered 14 wraps of improvised explosive device detonators.

Other reported seizures included ammunition recovered from suspects in Nasarawa and Zamfara, and an AK-47 rifle, ammunition and magazines found with two women arrested on the Wukari-Jalingo Road in Taraba State. The DSS has also recorded convictions in terrorism-related cases involving female arms couriers: the Federal High Court in Abuja sentenced Halima Abdullahi, Safiya Salihu and Halima Umar to 20 years in prison each. The security source said the service would continue intelligence-led operations against illegal arms trafficking.

title: US withdraws from U17 World Cup in Qatar over security fears
summary: The United States has reportedly withdrawn from the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar over regional security concerns. US Soccer had not confirmed the decision.
body:
The United States has withdrawn from the upcoming Under-17 World Cup in Qatar because of security concerns in the Middle East, according to US media reports. Players were reportedly told of the decision just over a week before the tournament is due to start on November 19. US Soccer had not publicly confirmed the withdrawal or responded to a request for comment.

The tournament is scheduled to feature 48 teams. The United States had been drawn in a group with Montenegro, Chile and Algeria. The reported decision comes amid a conflict that began in February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, followed by Iranian attacks on targets including Gulf countries allied with Washington. Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been accompanied by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume strikes on Iran.

The security situation has also affected other sporting events in the region. The WTA Finals, originally scheduled for Saudi Arabia, are instead being held at Indian Wells in the United States. The Formula One Grand Prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the Bahrain race was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia. Several events in Saudi Arabia have also been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks by Yemen’s Houthi forces.

The Under-17 World Cup became an annual tournament last year, and Qatar is set to host it for five consecutive years. FIFA said in 2024 that selecting one host for multiple editions would allow the tournament to use existing football infrastructure and support efficiency and sustainability. Qatar also hosted the men’s World Cup in 2022.

title: University sacks another four staff members, gives reason
summary: The Anambra university dismissed four staff over alleged misconduct, including extortion, exam manipulation, security failures and theft. Its council approved the move on November 5.
body:
Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University in Anambra State has dismissed four staff members over alleged misconduct. University spokesperson Harrison Madubueze said the Governing Council approved the dismissals at its 123rd meeting on 5 November, chaired by Pro-Chancellor Peter Onwualu.

Madubueze said the council considered a disciplinary report covering cases across the university’s departments and campuses. The alleged offences included extorting students, seeking money to alter examination results, neglecting security duties in a way that allowed a suspect in custody to escape, and stealing university property. The statement did not specify which allegations applied to each individual.

The four staff members were identified as Edward Egwuaba of the Department of Sociology; Ohakaba Romanus of the Security Department at the Uli Campus; Obinna Adams; and Vincent Okochichi of the Security Unit at the Igbariam Campus. Madubueze said the council viewed the decision as part of efforts to strengthen discipline and accountability, and to protect students, university property and the integrity of academic processes.

The dismissals follow earlier staff terminations by the university within the past year. In June, the council approved the dismissal of professors Chike Osegbue and C. C. Nwabachili, along with Ifeoma Iheukwumere and Emeka Nwabunnia, all from the Department of Microbiology. Vice-Chancellor Kate Omenugha said the earlier dismissals involved offences including sexual exploitation of students and ethical misconduct. She said Osegbue’s dismissal was not related to his participation in the vice-chancellor selection process, but to his failure to teach an assigned postgraduate course and his refusal to appear before a panel.

title: Otti urges lawyers to defend rights of vulnerable Nigerians
summary: Abia Governor Alex Otti urged lawyers to provide legal help to vulnerable Nigerians. He also outlined courthouse plans and called for stronger protection of rights.
body:
Abia State Governor Alex Otti has urged lawyers to extend legal services to people unable to afford representation, saying access to justice should take priority over financial and professional interests. He made the appeal in Umuahia while opening the 2026 Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL) Annual Conference, themed “In Public Interest: Advancing Justice, Democracy and Development.”

Otti said lawyers had a responsibility to help people who lacked the means to defend their rights. He also said his administration had found people in correctional facilities who, in its view, had committed no offences warranting continued detention. He cited the case of a person allegedly detained for supporting an opposition party and said he had directed the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice to work with the Chief Judge on securing the release of such inmates. Otti warned against using the justice system to punish people for expressing opinions or posting on social media.

The governor said the state would soon commission 10 newly constructed courthouses. He said the facilities would have renewable energy systems, digitalised court records and broadband connectivity. He also urged legal practitioners to prepare for technological changes in their profession.

In his keynote address, former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo urged lawyers to go beyond litigation and legal interpretation by advancing public interest and helping ensure democracy benefits citizens. He identified high legal costs, delays in court proceedings, judicial corruption and impunity as barriers to justice, and called for reforms that make legal services more affordable and accessible. NBA President Oyinkansola Badejo-Okunsanya also called on the section to strengthen its work on justice, democracy and development. She urged it to develop an intervention addressing the treatment of children in police custody and detention facilities, following reported deaths in custody. She asked NBA-SPIDEL to work with relevant NBA branches and human rights organisations, identify priorities and responsibilities within 30 days, and submit a progress report within 90 days.

title: I was soaked for hours before help came — 74-year-old blind man whose home was wrecked by wind storms
summary: A storm left blind 74-year-old Stephen Ogbo trapped and soaked for hours in a damaged Enugu home. Reconstruction has begun for the building’s 23 families.
body:
A rainstorm damaged the home of 74-year-old Stephen Ogbo in Ugbo Ezeji, D-Line, Abakpa Nike, in Enugu metropolis, leaving him trapped in the wreckage and soaked for hours. Blind and unable to find his way out, he was eventually led to safety by a female tenant whose name he does not know.

Ogbo said the woman found him after several hours and guided him out of the damaged building, then looked for somewhere he could shelter. He had lived in the compound for about eight years. The storm also affected the other residents: the building housed 23 families, and its roof was torn off while tenants’ belongings were damaged.

Mrs. Promise Ugochukwu, a resident and woman leader in the area, said the storm struck between 9pm and 10pm. She described the damage as devastating, saying rainwater ruined household belongings. Residents appealed for assistance as they faced the task of repairing their homes and replacing what had been lost.

Reconstruction has begun after Chief Kingsley Chizoba Nweke, the Peoples Democratic Party senatorial candidate for Enugu East, visited the residents. He said he had seen a video of their appeal and was moved to help. According to Nweke, building materials had been purchased and contractors mobilised to reinforce the structures and replace the damaged roofs so residents could return.

Nweke said the assistance was humanitarian rather than political, and that he would have helped regardless of the residents’ party affiliations. Ogbo thanked him for the intervention. For the affected families, rebuilding offers a first step toward restoring their homes; Ogbo’s escape also depended on the unnamed tenant who helped him through the storm’s aftermath.

title: NCDMB, NLNG commits US$9m to endowment of professorial research chairs in Six Nigerian universities
summary: NCDMB and NLNG launched a US$9 million research-chair programme for six universities, with US$1.5 million allocated to each. The chairs will target industry challenges.
body:
The Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB) and Nigeria LNG Limited (NLNG) have launched a US$9 million programme to establish professorial research chairs at six Nigerian universities. Each institution is to receive US$1.5 million to support a specialist chair focused on agreed industry priorities and the development of practical, commercially viable solutions.

The University of Ibadan will research natural gas processing, pollution control and environmental management. Rivers State University will focus on digital engineering, intelligent energy systems, automation and asset integrity. Modibbo Adama University will work on energy transition and the environment, while Aliko Dangote University of Science and Technology will study sustainable energy innovation and climate-resilient food systems. The University of Nigeria, Nsukka, will focus on green energy production and geoenvironmental engineering. Yakubu Gowon University, formerly the University of Abuja, will research geoscience and satellite intelligence for resilient gas infrastructure.

At the programme’s launch, NLNG Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Adeleye Falade said sustained research was needed as energy technologies and systems evolve. He identified operational efficiency, emissions management, safety, infrastructure maintenance and more sustainable industrial processes as areas where research could contribute. He also called for stronger cooperation between government, industry and universities, including through researcher exchanges, practical testing and postgraduate curriculum development.

NCDMB Executive Secretary Felix Omatsola Ogbe described the endowment as an investment in Nigeria’s research and innovation system. He said it complements the board’s research infrastructure investments, including research and development centres of excellence at six universities. The beneficiary institutions are expected to set clear research objectives, measure results, use funds prudently and work with industry partners to move findings towards application and commercialisation.

The programme also provides for minor building works and infrastructure upgrades to create suitable research centres. The universities will jointly host an information management hub to support knowledge sharing and exchanges. Proposed arrangements would allow industry professionals to contribute practical expertise while pursuing postgraduate degrees, strengthening links between academic research and industrial problem-solving. Rivers State University’s Research and Innovation Centre for Computer and Electrical Engineering is envisaged as a coordinating point for collaboration among the institutions.

title: UK coroner links school rules to teenager’s suicide
summary: A coroner found Ivybridge Community College’s discipline and a relationship breakdown contributed to Taylor Lee’s death. She plans a report on preventing future deaths.
body:
An inquest into the death of Taylor Lee, a 15-year-old from Plymouth, found that his school’s disciplinary approach and the breakdown of his relationship with his girlfriend contributed to his suicide. Area Coroner Alison Longhorn said Taylor’s experience at Ivybridge Community College had a significant impact and contributed to his death more than minimally. He died in November 2023, three weeks after returning to school following a suspension.

Taylor was a Year 11 pupil who had repeatedly described attending school as exhausting. The inquest heard that the college had introduced strict behaviour measures following increased absences after the COVID-19 pandemic. These included a bell system, six minutes to move between lessons and sanctions for lateness and other rule breaches. On one occasion, Taylor was sent for reflection after arriving 47 seconds late. After he challenged the rules and was suspended, he continued to raise concerns; the school then gave pupils an additional minute to reach lessons.

The coroner heard that Taylor had experienced low mood and self-harm, and had also struggled with bullying, mock GCSE examinations and relationships with some teachers. His family had raised concerns about the impact of the school rules. Principal Rachel Hutchinson described him as creative and said he found school routines and expectations difficult. Youth worker Richard Brooks told the inquest Taylor had become disengaged from education and recalled him describing each day as a battle.

Longhorn raised concerns that similar circumstances could arise again, noting that the college’s policies had not changed since Taylor’s death. She also identified a missed opportunity after a police officer warned the school about Taylor’s fragile mental state but received no response. The coroner said she would issue a Prevention of Future Deaths report. Hutchinson said investigations by Ofsted and Devon County Council into complaints about the policies had concluded that no further action was needed.

title: Mbah: My opponents busy shopping for shortcuts in Abuja
summary: Enugu Governor Peter Mbah accused rival 2027 contenders of seeking ways to undermine the vote. He also announced road, health and school projects in Uzo Uwani.
body:
Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah accused some potential opponents in the 2027 governorship election of seeking ways to compromise the vote instead of presenting their plans to residents. He made the remarks on Tuesday during a campaign tour of the Ogboli and Igbo-Ano Development Centres in Uzo Uwani Local Government Area, including stops in Adani and Ugbene Ajima.

Mbah said, in his view, the rivals had not presented manifestos because they lacked records and plans for the state. He alleged that they were exploring ways to manipulate voters’ choices and accused them of involvement in certificate forgery. He urged residents to reject them at the polls. The source material provided no response from the people he criticised.

The governor also said construction of the Nsukka-Adani Road and the Edem-Nrobo–Abbi-Nimbo Road would begin in earnest as the rainy season receded. He gave no further details about the timing or cost of the projects.

During the tour, Mbah visited Our Lady Health of the Sick Maternity Hospital in Adani and pledged to equip it to the standard of the state’s Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centre, including providing ultrasound equipment. He also promised a classroom block and an innovation hub for Santa Maria Nursery and Primary School, where students welcomed him.

title: UNIUYO To Graduate 22,961 Students, 214 With First Class Honours
summary: UNIUYO plans to graduate 22,961 students at its combined 31st and 32nd convocation on November 14, 2026. The cohort includes 214 first-class graduates.
body:
The University of Uyo plans to graduate 22,961 students at its 31st and 32nd combined convocation ceremonies on Saturday, November 14, 2026. The event is scheduled to take place at the university’s permanent site in Nwaniba, Akwa Ibom State. Vice-Chancellor Professor Christopher Nyong Ekong announced the figures at a media briefing ahead of the ceremony.

The graduating students include 19,217 receiving first degrees, 814 diploma recipients, 248 certificate recipients and 2,682 postgraduate graduands. Among those receiving first degrees, 214 will graduate with First Class Honours. A further 7,216 earned Second Class Upper, 10,468 Second Class Lower, 917 Third Class and 402 Pass degrees.

The university will also award honorary doctorate degrees to four Nigerians: Taraba State Governor Dr Agbu Kefas; Niger Delta Development Commission Managing Director Chief Samuel Ogbuku; Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited Chairman High Chief Government Oweizide Ekpemupolo, known as Tompolo; and Ubotex Nigeria Limited Managing Director Mr Ubong Obot. Ekong said the awards recognise their contributions to human and societal development in their respective fields.

The total of 22,961 is 10,511 higher than the 12,450 graduands at the previous combined convocation, held in November 2024—an increase of about 84.4 per cent. The number of First Class graduates is also up by 40 from the 174 recorded at that ceremony. Ekong said this would be the final time his administration combines multiple graduating sessions, adding that it intends to restore regular convocation schedules by processing and approving examination results promptly.

title: CJID announces shortlist for 2026 Excellence in Journalism Awards
summary: CJID shortlisted finalists for its 2026 West African journalism awards after receiving 424 entries from 277 journalists in nine countries. Winners are due Nov. 25 in Abuja.
body:
The Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) has announced the finalists for its 2026 annual journalism awards, recognising reporting from across West Africa. The awards received 424 entries from 277 journalists in nine countries: Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, The Gambia, Sierra Leone, Côte d’Ivoire, Liberia, Guinea and Benin. The total was 54.2 per cent higher than the 275 entries received for the 2025 edition.

Entries were screened to identify the top five in each of eight categories, then assessed by an independent regional jury. Judges considered accuracy, fairness, originality and innovation, research depth, writing quality, public significance and ethical standards before selecting the finalists. The categories are health reporting, community reporting, human rights reporting, social accountability, climate change reporting, solutions journalism, fact-checking, and sexual and gender-based violence reporting.

The jury was chaired by Hannah Ajakaiye, founding editor of FactsMatter NG. Its members were Maxime Domegni, Ajibola Amzat, Kent Mensah, Manasseh Awuni and Amaka Okoye. Ajakaiye said the entries were particularly strong in social accountability, environmental reporting and human rights. She also noted progress in solutions journalism, while identifying fact-checking and coverage of sexual and gender-based violence as areas for improvement.

The jury chose not to name an Editor of the Year because the limited number of submissions did not sufficiently meet the award’s criteria. Finalists will be recognised at a ceremony on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, at the Abuja Continental Hotel, held as part of the Media and Development Conference. Winners and runners-up in each category will be announced there.

CJID CEO Dapo Olorunyomi congratulated the finalists and thanked all entrants and the independent jury, describing the recognised work as reflecting journalism’s public-service role across the region. The 2026 awards are supported by the Royal Norwegian Embassy in Abuja and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

title: FULL LIST: US warns citizens against travel to 23 countries
summary: The US State Department has placed 23 countries under its highest travel advisory, warning Americans not to travel there. It cites local conditions and limits on US assistance.
body:
The US Department of State has warned Americans against travelling to 23 countries listed under its highest travel advisory category, Level 4: Do Not Travel. The department’s Bureau of Consular Affairs issued the warning in a Facebook post on Monday, saying the designation reflects local conditions and the US government’s limited ability to assist citizens in those destinations. It advised people not to travel to the listed countries for any reason.

The 23 countries are Afghanistan, Belarus, Burkina Faso, Burma, the Central African Republic, Chad, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti, Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Niger, North Korea, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Uganda, Ukraine and Yemen.

The State Department uses a four-level system for travel advisories. Level 1 recommends normal precautions, while Level 2 calls for increased caution. Level 3 advises travellers to reconsider their plans; Level 4 is the highest category and advises against all travel to the destinations concerned. The department said its Level 4 assessments are based on local conditions, the government’s ability to help Americans, or both.

The department urged travellers to review destination-specific information before making plans. Its advisories are available at travel.state.gov/destination.

title: Senate Pledges N100m Reward For Flamingos
summary: The Senate pledged N100 million to the Flamingos after their historic Under-17 Women’s World Cup win. It also urged greater investment in sports development.
body:
The Senate has pledged N100 million for Nigeria’s under-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, after their victory at the FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup. The team made history as the first African side to win the tournament, beating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final.

The pledge followed a motion by Sen. Abdul Ningi, chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports. He congratulated the players on their performance and commended the Nigeria Football Federation for its role in the achievement.

Lawmakers also praised President Bola Tinubu and Nigerians for supporting the team. They called on the Federal Government to provide adequate funding for sports development and said investment in young athletes would help sustain the momentum of the victory and support future champions.

title: Obi will run to Cameroon if confronted with burdens of presidency – Wike
summary: Nyesom Wike said Peter Obi lacked the capacity to lead and urged Abaji leaders to back Bola Tinubu in 2027. He also addressed power and local accountability.
body:
FCT Minister Nyesom Wike accused Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, of lacking the capacity to address Nigeria’s challenges. Speaking Tuesday at a Rainbow Coalition and Stakeholders’ Meeting in Abaji, Abuja, Wike said Obi would flee to Cameroon rather than confront the demands of the presidency. He praised President Bola Tinubu for making difficult decisions and said the country needs a leader willing to take responsibility when problems arise.

Wike urged residents and political leaders in Abaji to support Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. He challenged the area council chairman, councillors and other leaders to turn their stated support into votes in their wards, saying he would judge them by their results. He also said the FCT should match and surpass Rivers State’s electoral performance, and that he would use the same mobilisation strategy in Abuja.

The minister cautioned residents against repeating what he described as a mistake in the 2023 elections: electing representatives who, he said, did not stay in touch with their constituents or address their concerns. He asked whether the elected representative had returned to meet residents or taken action on matters affecting the FCT, and urged voters to hold political aspirants accountable for development problems in their communities.

Wike said he planned to meet FCT youths on Wednesday to discuss political mobilisation and issues affecting their participation in the coming elections. He told stakeholders that resources and arrangements for the campaign were being put in place and expressed confidence in the Rainbow Coalition’s ability to mobilise support for Tinubu. He also reiterated that he wanted Abaji’s electricity problem addressed before the 2027 elections, directing the area council chairman to intensify efforts to restore power.

title: Cartoon: Politicians’ sons can’t be thugs?
summary: A cartoon is framed around whether politicians’ sons can be thugs. The supplied material gives no details about the image or the people involved.
body:
A cartoon is presented under the question: “Politicians’ sons can’t be thugs?” The wording raises a question about whether family ties to politicians affect how the behaviour of their sons is viewed.

The supplied material does not describe the cartoon’s imagery, identify any individuals or explain the circumstances behind the question.

title: WIMAFRICA seeks greater economic power for African women
summary: WIMAFRICA’s Lagos forum will focus on finance, trade and decision-making for African women. Organisers also plan to build cross-border business and investment links.
body:
WIMAFRICA seeks greater economic power for African women

Women in Management Africa will hold its first African edition of the Women in Management global economic forum in Lagos on 10–11 November 2026. The event, at the Federal Palace Hotel, will take place under the theme “The Power Shift: Women Driving Africa’s Global Economic Influence.” Organisers say it will focus on improving women’s access to finance, markets and economic decision-making.

WIMAFRICA Chairperson Dr Ngozi Oyewole said the aim was to help women move beyond participating in economic activity and gain greater influence over business decisions, trade and resource allocation. She said African women already contribute to manufacturing, agriculture, trade and entrepreneurship, but face barriers including limited capital, infrastructure gaps, cultural restrictions and difficulties accessing land. The forum will also examine opportunities linked to the African Continental Free Trade Area, including local manufacturing, backward integration and African supply chains.

Oyewole said businesses can struggle to fulfil confirmed orders because they lack working capital to buy materials, pay staff and cover production costs before customers pay. She called on financial institutions to design products that reflect the needs of women-owned businesses, and urged government agencies and companies to widen procurement access for qualified firms and pay promptly for completed contracts. She also called for practical guidance on AfCFTA documentation and rules of origin, alongside better roads and electricity to reduce costs and losses for rural businesses, particularly those handling perishable goods.

Women in Management founder Dr Sulochana Segera said bringing the international platform to Africa was intended to connect African women with global business, trade and investment opportunities. Founded in Sri Lanka 16 years ago, the organisation has a network spanning 29 countries, she said. The partnership with Oyewole will also use WIM’s Top 50 recognition platform to highlight African women’s contributions. Segera said the Lagos gathering was intended to support business partnerships and longer-term economic cooperation, as well as recognition.

title: Tinubu acknowledges challenges facing Nigerian youths, promises more opportunities
summary: Tinubu said young Nigerians’ concerns over jobs, living costs, education and security are legitimate. He pledged to expand skills, financing and employment opportunities.
body:
President Bola Tinubu has acknowledged concerns among young Nigerians about unemployment, the cost of living, access to education, business opportunities and insecurity. Speaking at the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Youth Conference in Abuja on Monday, he said the government had a responsibility to address those expectations. His remarks were delivered by House of Representatives Speaker Tajudeen Abbas.

Tinubu said young people wanted a country where effort is rewarded, talent is recognised and opportunities do not depend on personal connections or background. He said his administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda was intended to build an economy that creates opportunities and rewards enterprise. While recognising that economic reforms had involved sacrifices, he said young people should see future opportunities become tangible improvements in their lives.

The economic pressures have been compounded by the removal of petrol subsidies and the floating of the naira, as well as disruptions to global energy and commodity markets linked to conflicts and wars. Insecurity in parts of Nigeria has also disrupted farming and commerce, displaced communities and contributed to school closures, prolonging educational disruption for millions of children.

Tinubu pointed to several government programmes aimed at widening opportunities, including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, the Three Million Technical Talent programme, YouthCred and the Nigerian Youth Academy. He said the government would work to ensure skills training leads to employment, innovation attracts investment and young entrepreneurs can continue to access financing. He also pledged support for young Nigerians seeking to succeed, regardless of their background or location.

title: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi Will Collapse Under Their Own Weight — SDP’s Adewole
summary: SDP candidate Adewole Adebayo says he expects to win a credible 2027 election, arguing rivals will falter. He also pledged action on poverty and insecurity.
body:
Social Democratic Party presidential candidate Adewole Adebayo said he was confident of winning a free, fair and credible election in 2027. He argued that President Bola Tinubu, Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi would fall under their own weight, though he said his focus was defeating poverty and insecurity rather than simply defeating political opponents.

In a television interview on Monday, Adebayo presented his manifesto, titled “Farewell to Poverty and Insecurity,” as a plan for progress and good governance that he said could improve Nigerians’ lives. He described electoral victory as persuading a majority of citizens to support the plan, rather than a contest in which opponents are defeated physically.

Adebayo said that overcoming poverty and insecurity would also require addressing what he characterised as voter ignorance, fatigue and apathy. He urged citizens not to vote based only on sentiment and challenged the belief that individual votes do not count. He said greater public engagement would help voters assess and support his proposed approach.

On security, Adebayo argued that fixing government would help resolve the country’s security challenges. He said Nigerians should no longer see terrorists within six months, citing the capacity of the Nigerian Armed Forces, and pledged to address banditry. He also promised that citizens would receive security as a “Christmas present” in 2027. The presidential election is scheduled for January 16, 2027.

title: Delta okays N1.2tn proposed 2027 budget
summary: Delta’s Executive Council has approved a proposed 2027 budget of slightly more than ₦1.2 trillion. It will be sent to the House of Assembly for consideration.
body:
Delta State’s Executive Council has approved a proposed budget of slightly more than ₦1.2 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year. The proposal is expected to be transmitted to the state House of Assembly for legislative consideration. Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information Charles Aniagwu announced the approval after a council meeting at the Government House Annex in Edjeba, Warri South Local Government Area.

Aniagwu said the budget would provide a financial framework for infrastructure projects and other development programmes planned for 2027. He identified infrastructure, education, economic empowerment, electricity and security among the administration’s priorities, and said the government aimed to produce a realistic budget that could sustain development and deliver benefits to residents.

He said the administration’s programmes are guided by its MORE Agenda: Meaningful Development, Opportunities for All, Realistic Reforms, and Enhanced Peace and Security. The government intends to distribute projects and opportunities across all 25 local government areas, Aniagwu said, including as political activity increases ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commissioner also pointed to social investment programmes intended to support small businesses, including interventions offering beneficiaries up to ₦250,000. He said the support was intended to strengthen businesses and stimulate economic activity. Construction work, he added, could provide jobs for tradespeople and suppliers of building materials.

On electricity, Aniagwu said Delta had partnered with Sapele Power to use turbines brought into the state by previous administrations but not fully deployed. The arrangement is expected to generate about 120 megawatts for injection into the national grid. The proposed budget will require legislative consideration before it can proceed through the state’s budget process.

title: Navy rescues Bayelsa commissioner, NSCDC official, 5 others from drowning
summary: The Navy and local divers rescued seven of eight passengers after a boat mishap in Bayelsa’s Brass waters. A police officer remained missing as search efforts continued.
body:
Seven people were rescued after a passenger boat suffered a mishap in waters near Abedigbene, in Bayelsa State’s Brass Local Government Area, on Thursday. The passengers included Bayelsa Commissioner for Trade, Industry and Investment Ebieri Jones, an official of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps, and five others. A police officer was still missing, according to a Navy operational report.

The boat was travelling from Yenagoa to Akassa and reportedly had eight people aboard. After receiving a distress report from a local fisherman, personnel from the Nigerian Navy’s Forward Operating Base FORMOSO, deployed at Labrador Lagosgbene Houseboat, mobilised to the scene and began search-and-rescue operations. Local divers and members of the Abedigbene fishing community assisted.

The survivors were taken to the houseboat and given first aid. Preliminary assessments found no visible injuries, the report said. On Friday, Jones and the six other survivors were taken to Yenagoa to reunite with their families. Search efforts continued for the missing police officer.
