The Navy said the operation reflected its response to emergencies and its work to protect lives and improve maritime safety in its area of responsibility. FOB FORMOSO Commanding Officer Sunday Haruna praised the personnel for their response and professionalism, and acknowledged the support of local divers and the community.

title: [VIDEO] APC National Chairman Defends Wike’s ₦10m Reward For Council That Delivers For Tinubu
summary: APC chairman Nentawe Yilwatda defended Nyesom Wike’s ₦10 million offer to councillors who deliver their wards for Tinubu in 2027. He said it was not vote buying.
body:
All Progressives Congress National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda has defended Nyesom Wike’s offer of ₦10 million to councillors who deliver their wards for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. Wike is the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory.

Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, Yilwatda said the offer did not amount to vote buying.

Wike had said councillors who deliver their wards for Tinubu’s re-election would receive the reward. The available details do not include further explanation from Yilwatda about why he considers the offer distinct from vote buying.

title: Failed bank debtors frustrating loan recovery — NDIC
summary: The NDIC says debtors’ tactics are delaying loan recovery and depositor payments. It plans tighter asset-management rules and continued work with recovery professionals.
body:
## Failed bank debtors frustrating loan recovery — NDIC

The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) says some borrowers from failed banks are hindering efforts to recover outstanding debts by concealing assets, delaying court proceedings and intimidating those pursuing repayment. Ogungbemi Theophilus, the corporation’s Director of Asset Management, raised the concern at a stakeholders’ seminar and public relations workshop in Abuja on Monday. He said the loss of a bank’s licence does not remove a borrower’s obligation to repay.

Theophilus described loan recovery as one of the most difficult parts of liquidating a bank. Delays can also reduce the value of other assets: unoccupied buildings may depreciate, equipment can deteriorate, and loans may become harder to collect. The NDIC warned that these losses can reduce the funds available to depositors and slow payment of claims.

The Asset Management Department handles loans, physical assets and investments of closed deposit money banks, primary mortgage banks and microfinance banks. It is responsible for recovering debts and selling assets to generate funds for uninsured depositors. Deposits are insured up to N5m per depositor per bank at deposit money banks, non-interest banks and mobile money operators, and up to N2m at microfinance banks, primary mortgage banks and payment service banks. The NDIC says this coverage fully protects about 99 per cent of depositors; customers with larger balances rely on liquidation dividends for amounts above the insured limits.

Theophilus said the corporation held competitive sealed-bid auctions on November 3 and 4, 2026, to sell physical assets belonging to Union Homes Savings and Loans, Heritage Bank and Resort Savings and Loans. The auctions took place in Lagos, Taraba and Adamawa states. He also cautioned that recovery costs should not exceed the value of the assets recovered, and warned professionals against insider dealing, undervaluation, collusion with buyers and diversion of proceeds.

The NDIC is developing an Asset Management Policy covering asset identification, documentation, valuation, disposal and accountability. It also plans to strengthen cooperation with auctioneers, valuers, sales agents, surveyors and other professionals. The Abuja event is part of a series of three seminars scheduled for Abuja, Enugu and Lagos to address operational challenges and improve recovery outcomes.

title: Ogun govt clarifies video of corps members sleeping in hall
summary: Ogun says corps members seen sleeping in a Sagamu camp hall were awaiting screening and hostel allocation during late-night registration. Mattresses were provided.
body:
The Ogun State Government says a viral video showing prospective corps members sleeping in a hall at the NYSC Orientation Camp in Sagamu captured a temporary arrangement during registration, not their assigned accommodation. Registration continued into the night, the government said, while NYSC officials completed credential checks and screening before allocating hostel spaces.

Kayode Akinmade, Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to Governor Dapo Abiodun, said those whose registration ran late were placed in the multipurpose hall to rest, with mattresses provided. He said registration, screening and hostel allocation are handled by NYSC officials.

Akinmade said Ogun received more than 4,300 prospective corps members in the current batch, compared with slightly more than 2,000 in previous batches, putting additional pressure on available camp facilities. He said the state provided 500 mattresses for the exercise, while the Akarigbo of Remo donated 100 and later contributed a further 200.

The government also pointed to other support for corps members. Akinmade said Abiodun recently approved a ₦50,000 welfare grant for each of the 3,050 corps members in the 2026 Batch C, Stream I, to assist with transportation. He said the state supports the scheme’s welfare while NYSC remains responsible for camp operations, and that the government would continue working to provide an enabling environment for corps members serving in Ogun.

title: Nigeria’s trade sector faces financing squeeze, profit margins slip – NESG
summary: Financing was Nigeria’s trade sector’s leading constraint in H1 2026, even as credit and cash-flow indexes expanded. Operating profitability slipped into contraction.
body:
Nigeria’s trade sector faces financing squeeze, profit margins slip – NESG

Limited access to financing was the most frequently cited constraint for businesses in Nigeria’s trade sector in the first half of 2026, according to a Nigerian Economic Summit Group report. The report examines operating conditions, business performance and expectations in the sector.

Financing ranked first among reported constraints, with a score of 12. Inadequate power supply, unclear economic policies, and the cost of commercial leases and rental property each scored 10. Financing rose from second place in 2024 to the top position, while foreign exchange availability became less prominent, which the report described as an encouraging development.

The Access to Credit Index stood at 112.0, and the Cash Flow Index was 121.9; both were in expansionary territory. However, the NESG said the availability of some credit does not guarantee businesses can secure funding at suitable costs, amounts or repayment periods to support expansion. The Operating Profit Index fell to 98.1 from 102.9 in the first half of 2025, indicating a marginal move into contraction.

The Future Investment Index was neutral at 100. Traders were optimistic about future turnover and operating conditions, but those expectations had not translated into a clear expansionary investment outlook. The report’s findings point to a gap between positive liquidity indicators and businesses’ ability to invest and sustain profitability.

The concerns come as merchandise trade grows. Nigeria’s total merchandise trade reached N41.44 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, up 5.61% from N39.24 trillion in the corresponding quarter of 2025. Trade contributed 17.89% to GDP in the first quarter of 2026. The report identifies financing access, infrastructure challenges and pressure on profits as continuing concerns despite the growth in trade activity.

title: ‘They told me not to approach the team ‘ – Obi alleges NFF officials barred him from Flamingos
summary: Peter Obi alleges NFF officials stopped him greeting the Flamingos at Abuja airport. The federation had not publicly responded at the time of reporting.
body:
Peter Obi has accused Nigeria Football Federation officials of preventing him from greeting the Flamingos, Nigeria’s victorious under-17 women’s team, at Abuja’s Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport on Monday. He said he arrived at about 7 a.m. to catch a flight to Enugu and saw the players returning from Morocco after winning the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

In a statement, Obi said he asked his Protocol Officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether he could welcome the players. He alleged that he was told NFF officials had refused and had warned they could lose their jobs if he approached the team. The NFF had not publicly responded to the allegation at the time of reporting.

Obi said the incident recalled an earlier experience at a World Cup qualifying match in Uyo on 25 March 2025. He said Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno welcomed him at the stadium, but that he was prevented from greeting the Super Eagles after the match, while other government officials were allowed to meet the players. The game against Zimbabwe ended 1-1.

He described the two incidents as evidence of what he called growing political hostility and said political differences should not lead to intimidation or discrimination. A day before the airport incident, Obi had congratulated the Flamingos on their achievement, calling it a source of national pride.

Nigeria beat Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco, to become the first African nation to win the tournament. Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scored for Nigeria before Fuki Ito pulled one back for Japan. The Flamingos recovered from an opening loss to Poland and won six straight matches, including a semi-final victory over Brazil, to claim their first title in the competition.

title: Opposition’s consensus candidate plan dead – G-100 chieftain
summary: A G-100 chieftain says opposition politicians’ refusal to compromise has ended efforts for a single 2027 presidential candidate. The group had sought a united front.
body:
Umanu Elijah, a chieftain of the G-100 political pressure group, says the prospect of a broad opposition coalition for the 2027 presidential election has effectively collapsed. He attributed the setback to politicians’ unwillingness to set aside individual ambitions and support a common candidate against President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC).

G-100 was convened by Salihu Lukman, a former Director-General of the Progressives Governors’ Forum, to help build an opposition coalition ahead of the general election. The group has argued that parties contesting separately would find it difficult to defeat the APC, given the ruling party’s political structures and electoral advantages.

As part of its effort to find common ground, G-100 held consultations with former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde and other political figures. The aim was to bring parties and influential politicians together around a shared platform and a single presidential candidate.

In a telephone interview, Elijah said the single-candidate proposal had failed because potential contenders were not making the compromises needed for an agreement. He cited ongoing campaign activity by the Allied Peoples Movement and the African Democratic Congress, among other parties, as evidence that the consensus plan was losing support. The coalition effort was intended to avoid splitting opposition votes and weakening the challenge to the APC, but Elijah’s assessment points to parties continuing their preparations independently. Attempts to obtain a response from Lukman were unsuccessful.

title: The Atiku factor, By Wole Olaoye
summary: Atiku Abubakar remains in the 2027 race after a court ruling sparked uncertainty over ADC candidates. His potential absence could reshape opposition voting in the North.
body:
The Atiku factor, By Wole Olaoye

Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar remains in contention for the 2027 presidential election, despite a court ruling that prompted claims that all 470 candidates of his party, the African Democratic Congress (ADC), had been nullified. After nearly a day of uncertainty, a pronouncement by Mohammed Kudu Haruna, the Independent National Electoral Commission’s commissioner for information, voter education and stakeholder engagement, indicated that Atiku was still on the ballot.

The episode drew allegations that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) was seeking to block Atiku, which the party denied. The commentary argues that Atiku’s electoral record makes him a significant opposition figure: in 2023 he received 6,984,520 votes, compared with President Bola Tinubu’s 8,794,726. It says a legal removal of Atiku, whether linked to the ADC’s leadership dispute or an eligibility challenge, could have political and regional consequences.

In the North, the analysis suggests, Atiku’s absence could split his support among other opposition candidates, local political structures or abstention. Rabiu Kwankwaso could become the most prominent northern opposition figure, particularly in the Northwest, while APC governors would seek to attract voters in their states. In the Northeast, where Atiku won five of six states in 2023 and received about 1.7 million votes, the commentary sees no single candidate positioned to inherit his support. It says votes could move to an opposition alliance or become less concentrated, while Borno and Yobe might lean further toward the APC.

The possible effects would vary elsewhere. In Middle Belt states, voters who previously backed Atiku could turn to Peter Obi or smaller parties, while local security concerns and politics would shape choices in other states. The analysis also warns that perceived exclusion of leading candidates could discourage turnout and deepen doubts about judicial independence, although it says there is no direct evidence for claims that the ruling party influenced the court decision. It concludes that Atiku’s continued presence makes him a major factor in the contest, while voters’ concerns about their future remain central.

title: Seven die as two trains collide in Egypt
summary: At least seven people were killed and more than 100 injured when a train struck a stationary service near Giza. Authorities ordered an investigation and suspended services.
body:
At least seven people were killed and more than 100 injured when two trains collided near Giza, derailing several carriages down an embankment. The crash occurred between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat. Emergency workers, passengers and bystanders searched the overturned and badly damaged carriages for survivors and injured people.

Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum struck the rear of a stationary service travelling from Cairo to Aswan. Health Minister Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said some injured people were being treated for broken bones and head injuries. The driver of one train was among those killed, and the public prosecutor’s office warned that the death toll could rise.

Hospitals in the affected area were placed on heightened alert. The Egyptian Red Crescent said it was providing medical care and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene. Train services between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended while cranes were brought in to remove the wreckage.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi ordered an investigation into the circumstances of the crash and said anyone found responsible for negligence should be held accountable. The collision has prompted calls for the transport minister to resign, while Saudi Arabia and Turkey expressed condolences. The accident occurred in an area with a history of deadly railway crashes. In February 2002, a fire aboard a Cairo-to-Luxor passenger train killed more than 370 people in Egypt’s deadliest train disaster.

title: No Political Will To Deal With Agberos In Lagos, Says NDC’s Funsho Doherty
summary: Funsho Doherty said weak political will and entrenched interests have hindered efforts to reform Lagos’s agbero system. He pledged to modernise transport.
body:
Funsho Doherty, the Nigeria Democratic Congress governorship candidate in Lagos State, said a lack of political will by successive administrations had allowed the agbero system to persist. He made the remarks during the Lagos Governorship Debate on Sunday, where he discussed reforming the state’s transport sector.

Agberos are transport touts who collect money from commercial bus drivers and other operators at motor parks, bus stops and on roads. They may claim to act for transport unions or park authorities. Doherty said powerful interests in the existing transport system had made it difficult for successive governments to address their activities.

He argued that meaningful reform would require a government accountable to residents rather than to groups that benefit from the current arrangement. Doherty said his administration would modernise transportation, presenting that goal as part of a broader break with the existing system.

The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, a coalition of The PUNCH, Channels Television, TVC News, TheCable and Vanguard Newspapers.

title: Idris inaugurates APC 2027 Campaign Council in Kebbi
summary: Kebbi Governor Nasir Idris has inaugurated the APC’s 2027 Campaign Council, naming former governor Saidu Dakingari as its chairman. He urged members to mobilise support.
body:
Kebbi State Governor Nasir Idris has inaugurated the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 Campaign Council at the Presidential Lodge in Birnin Kebbi. He called on members to carry out their duties with commitment, dedication and determination ahead of the general elections.

Idris described Kebbi as an APC stronghold and urged party stakeholders to return to their communities to mobilise support for the party’s candidates across all elective positions. He named former Kebbi governor and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Turkey, Saidu Usman Nasamu Dakingari, as chairman of the council.

The governor wished the council members well as they took up the assignment. APC State Chairman Abubakar Kana-Zuru commended Idris for supporting the party and helping bring about the council’s inauguration. He also urged members to remain dedicated to campaign activities and work together towards the party’s success in the elections.

Dakingari thanked Idris for the confidence placed in him and the other council members. He said the committee would work collectively and diligently to pursue the party’s objectives and secure success for the APC in the 2027 general elections.

title: Major shakeup in Nigerian Air Force, 67 senior officers redeployed
summary: Nigeria’s Air Force has reassigned 67 senior officers across commands, training institutions and security bodies. The changes aim to support military operations and institutional priorities.
body:
The Nigerian Air Force has reassigned 67 senior officers across its operational commands, training institutions and strategic defence bodies. Chief of the Air Staff Kelvin Aneke approved the appointments on 7 November. The service said the changes are intended to match officers’ experience and professional skills with its operational and institutional priorities, including support for ongoing military campaigns. All affected officers hold the rank of Air Vice Marshal and are expected to complete handover formalities by 13 November.

At NAF headquarters, Adeniran Ademuwagun was appointed chief of transformation and innovation, while Nnamdi Ananaba became chief of operations. Other appointments include Precious Amadi as chief of air intelligence, Enebong Efiom as chief of training, and John Laoye as chief of aircraft engineering.

The reshuffle also changes leadership across operational commands. Nnaemeka Ilo was appointed air officer commanding Tactical Air Command, Bashir Mamman took over Mobility Command, and Olufemi Ogunsina was named head of Logistics Command. Michael Onyebashi will lead Special Operations Command, while John Ukeh was appointed commander of the Nigerian Air Defence Corps. Garba Jibia was named deputy force commander of Operation Hadin Kai, the joint task force fighting Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province insurgents in the North-east.

Other officers are moving to roles at Defence Headquarters, the Office of the National Security Adviser, the Defence Intelligence Agency and the Defence Space Administration. Usman Abdullahi was appointed director of defence operations, while Elijah Ebiowe became deputy coordinator for national intelligence at the ONSA. Changes also extend to professional military education: PB Philips was appointed commandant of the Armed Forces Command and Staff College, and AO Akinbunwa will lead the Air Force War College. The NAF said the realignment reflects a commitment to leadership renewal, accountability and improved operational effectiveness.

title: NAF redeploys senior officers, appoints new commanders
summary: The Nigerian Air Force has announced senior postings across headquarters, commands and training institutions. The changes take effect in November 2026.
body:
The Nigerian Air Force has approved a broad round of senior appointments and postings across its headquarters, operational commands, training institutions and other defence organisations. Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Sunday Aneke approved the changes on November 7, 2026, with the postings taking effect during November. The Air Force said the realignment is intended to strengthen command effectiveness, institutional capacity and operational readiness.

At Service Headquarters, Air Vice Marshal AK Ademuwagun was named Chief of Transformation and Innovation, while AVM PN Amadi was appointed Chief of Air Intelligence and AVM NN Ananaba Chief of Operations. Other headquarters appointments include AVM EE Efiom as Chief of Training and AVM AJ Laoye as Chief of Aircraft Engineering. Command changes include AVM NI Ilo as Air Officer Commanding, Tactical Air Command; AVM BR Mamman at Mobility Command; and AVM OS Ogunsina at Logistics Command. AVM MN Onyebashi and AVM FCS Nwakara will lead Special Operations Command and Ground Training Command, respectively.

Several senior officers were assigned to education and training institutions. AVM PB Philips will command the Armed Forces Command and Staff College, AVM AO Akinbunwa the Air Force War College, and AVM OC Ubadike the Air Force Institute of Technology. AVM AI Sambo was appointed Commandant of the Nigerian Air Force College of Logistics and Management, while AVM M Yusuf will serve as Deputy Commandant of the Nigerian Defence Academy.

The postings also cover Defence Headquarters and security agencies. AVM UK Abdullahi was named Director of Defence Operations, and AVM EOE Ebiowe was posted to the Office of the National Security Adviser as Deputy Coordinator, National Intelligence. AVM DDG Pwajok will be Director of Technical Services at the Defence Intelligence Agency, while AVM I Sani becomes Deputy Chief of Defence Intelligence. At the Defence Space Administration, AVM AA Suleh was appointed Deputy Chief, with AVM OA Oyename and AVM SS Lazarus taking director roles. AVM GI Jibia was named Deputy Force Commander of Operation Hadin Kai, and AVM JI Ukeh Commander of the Nigerian Air Defence Corps.

The Air Force said the exercise supports leadership renewal, accountability and operational effectiveness. Affected officers are expected to complete handover procedures by November 13, 2026.

title: ADP crisis deepens as spokesman disputes Sani’s suspension
summary: ADP spokesman Sani Dawop rejects the reported suspension of chairman Yabagi Yusuf Sani. He says a November 4 meeting instead suspended secretary Victor Fingesi.
body:
The leadership dispute in the Action Democratic Party (ADP) has intensified after National Publicity Secretary Sani Dawop challenged the reported interim suspension of National Chairman Yabagi Yusuf Sani. National Secretary Victor Fingesi had announced the suspension over allegations of forged party documents and unauthorised interference with the Independent National Electoral Commission’s candidate nomination portal. Fingesi said the decision was approved by a majority of National Working Committee (NWC) members and communicated to INEC’s chairman. Sani declined to comment when contacted.

Dawop said the party’s leadership rejected that account and maintained that no constitutionally valid decision had been made to suspend or remove Sani. He said Sani remained the duly elected chairman following the party’s National Convention on May 29 and 30, 2026. According to Dawop, the NWC’s emergency meeting on November 4 concerned disciplinary issues involving Fingesi, including alleged insubordination and failure to follow lawful party directives.

Dawop said the meeting considered Fingesi’s responses to earlier queries and appeals for him to retract disputed statements and apologise. He said National Special Duties Secretary and Acting Deputy National Secretary Fatima Sani Muhammed moved a motion under Article 23.2(e) of the ADP constitution to suspend Fingesi from the functions of National Secretary, begin a disciplinary investigation and refer the matter to the National Executive Committee for ratification. Dawop said the motion was seconded and passed at a quorate meeting, with Fingesi and National Youth Leader Chinazam Ike among those present. He described the measure as interim, not a final finding of guilt.

Dawop said allegations against Sani, including claims of forgery, financial impropriety and interference with INEC’s portal, required verifiable evidence, investigation and a fair hearing. He called for independent inquiries into suspected unauthorised activity on the portal and preservation of electronic records, while saying those concerns did not establish wrongdoing by Sani or anyone else. He also said any financial audit should follow the party’s constitutional and financial procedures.

The spokesman warned against using party communications or letterhead to misrepresent decisions, saying the ADP could take constitutional or legal steps over communications that did so. He urged members, candidates and supporters to remain calm and focus on preparations for the 2027 general elections. Dawop’s account is that the November 4 decision concerned Fingesi, not Sani.

title: Kaduna-Kano Rail Set For December 3 Inauguration, Kano-Katsina-Maradi Project 70% Complete — APC
summary: APC-PCC says the Kaduna–Kano railway is due for inauguration on Dec. 3, 2026. The Kano–Katsina–Maradi line is reported 70% complete.
body:
The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council says the Kaduna–Kano Standard Gauge Railway is scheduled for inauguration on December 3, 2026. It reported that the 203-kilometre project is about 90 per cent complete and that the 400-kilometre Kano–Katsina–Maradi railway has reached 70 per cent completion.

In a statement signed by council spokesperson Dele Alake, the APC-PCC said both projects had advanced since President Bola Tinubu took office in 2023. It put the Kano–Katsina–Maradi project at about five per cent complete at that time, and the Kaduna–Kano line at less than 30 per cent.

The council said a Federal Government inspection team, led by Transportation Ministry Permanent Secretary Funso Adebiyi, recently reviewed the projects on the President’s directive. The inspection covered track alignment, drainage, embankment protection, stone pitching and soil stabilisation. Officials also travelled by train from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano to assess the track and passenger comfort.

According to the statement, the 190-kilometre Jaji–Kano section of the Kaduna–Kano project and a 250-kilometre section of the Kano–Maradi line are to be inaugurated on December 3. The council said the President had directed that outstanding land acquisition and compensation matters in Kaduna metropolis be resolved so work on the rail corridor between Abuja and Kano can be completed.

The Kaduna–Kano line is intended to extend the existing Abuja–Kaduna standard-gauge railway, linking Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano. The council said it would provide an alternative to road travel and support passenger and commercial movement. It said the Kano–Katsina–Maradi route is expected to strengthen cross-border transport and trade with neighbouring Niger Republic.

title: Elon Musk loses $53.9 billion in one week as net worth drops to $849.7 billion
summary: Elon Musk’s estimated fortune fell $53.9 billion, or 5.97%, in a week to $849.7 billion. He remained far ahead of the next-ranked billionaire.
body:
Elon Musk’s estimated net worth fell by $53.9 billion over seven days to $849.7 billion, according to billionaire rankings updated on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The drop was a 5.97% reduction from the approximately $903.6 billion estimate recorded a week earlier. Musk remained the world’s richest person despite the decline.

His fortune was still $471.6 billion greater than that of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, ranked second with an estimated $378.1 billion. Google co-founder Larry Page was third at $236.9 billion, followed by Sergey Brin at $218.1 billion and Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg at $209.7 billion.

Musk’s wealth is largely tied to his stakes in Tesla, SpaceX and other businesses, making its estimated value sensitive to changes in company valuations and market conditions. The latest decline came during a turbulent period for technology stocks, including companies associated with artificial intelligence, electric vehicles and space exploration.

The weekly loss follows sharp movements in the opposite direction. On October 21, Musk’s estimated fortune rose by $88 billion in a single day, reaching $1.013 trillion amid renewed investor optimism about SpaceX’s financial performance and expectations ahead of Tesla’s quarterly earnings announcement. His wealth also increased by $30.7 billion in 24 hours in August, reaching $894.9 billion as valuations across major holdings improved. The swings illustrate how quickly billionaire wealth estimates can change as the value of their business interests shifts.

title: Yoruba started home video, not Nollywood — Osuofia
summary: Nkem Owoh says Yoruba filmmakers popularised Nigerian home video, but did not start Nollywood, a name adopted later. His comments revisit a debate over the industry's roots.
body:
Veteran actor Nkem Owoh, known as Osuofia, has said Yoruba filmmakers helped popularise home-video productions in Nigeria but did not start Nollywood. He made the distinction during an interview with comedian and content creator Adebayo Abidemi, known as Bae U, after being asked about reports that he had credited Yoruba people with starting the industry.

Owoh said the name Nollywood was not in use when filmmakers began making movies. He described a process in which people discussed ideas together before eventually choosing the name. He rejected the claim that his position was that Yoruba filmmakers started Nollywood, while maintaining that they were early and influential in home video.

He cited veteran filmmaker Hubert Ogunde and Adebayo Papa as people whose work he admired, and said Yoruba productions helped make the home-video format popular. Owoh also disputed a suggestion that Ogunde was Igbo, saying the filmmaker was Yoruba.

The remarks come amid debate over the contributions of Yoruba and Igbo filmmakers to Nigerian cinema. The late actor Francis Duru had argued that Igbo entrepreneurs were central to building Nollywood, particularly through the growth of the commercial home-video market in the 1990s and early 2000s. Historical accounts also trace Yoruba filmmaking to travelling theatre groups, including those associated with Ogunde and Duro Ladipo, whose stage productions developed into film and video work before that commercial boom.

The 1992 Igbo-language film Living in Bondage, produced by Kenneth Nnebue, is associated with the rise of the modern direct-to-video market and helped popularise the format. The name Nollywood emerged later, as Nigerian films gained wider international recognition. Owoh’s comments underline the distinction between the earlier history of home-video production and the later industry identified by that name.

title: FG targets 600 farmers for N180 million interest-free loans in Niger State
summary: Federal and Niger State officials plan N300,000 interest-free loans for 600 small-scale farmers, a potential N180 million programme. Registration and verification are underway.
body:
The Federal Government and Niger State Government plan to provide N300,000 interest-free loans to 600 small-scale farmers, a potential total disbursement of N180 million. The initiative is being delivered through FarmerMoni, part of the Government Enterprise and Empowerment Programme (GEEP) under the National Social Investment Programme Agency (NSIPA).

GEEP National Programme Manager Hamza Baba announced the plan in Minna during the start of a beneficiary enumeration exercise and training for desk officers from the state’s 25 local government areas. He said the loans are intended to help farmers buy agricultural inputs, expand production and improve their livelihoods.

Each loan is repayable within one year, with repayments expected to begin six months after farming activities commence. The intervention covers crop cultivation, poultry, livestock, fisheries and aquaculture. Officials will identify, register and verify applicants to help ensure that funds go to active farmers.

Baba said GEEP would work with the All Farmers Association of Nigeria, the Agricultural Development Programme and local government officials to monitor how loans are used and repaid. Niger State Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management Ibrahim Inga said the programme would complement existing poverty-reduction efforts, while stressing the importance of transparency and reaching genuine farmers.

Special Adviser to the Governor on Social Investment Programme Hauwa Mohammed said desk officers had received tablets to record farmers’ details and farmland locations. The digital process, she said, is intended to prevent fictitious beneficiaries from obtaining loans.

title: Baze University acquires two aircraft as founder expands aviation education
summary: Baze University has acquired two aircraft from Austria for its planned aviation school in Bwari. The school will combine classroom teaching with practical flight training.
body:
Baze University in Abuja has acquired two training aircraft from Austria as it expands into aviation education. The aircraft arrived at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport on Friday and received a water cannon salute. Founding Pro-Chancellor Datti Baba-Ahmed said the purchase would strengthen aviation training capacity and help develop skilled professionals.

The aircraft are intended for Baze Aviation School, which is being developed in Bwari in the Federal Capital Territory. School coordinator Aliyu Bello said they would allow students to gain hands-on experience alongside ground-school instruction. Proposed facilities include a runway, hangar, terminal building, laboratories and simulation centres.

The National Universities Commission has approved two undergraduate programmes at the university for the 2026/2027 academic session: Aviation Management and Aerospace Engineering. Baba-Ahmed has also outlined plans to train at least 600 professionals in fields including air traffic control, air rescue and firefighting, subject to approval from relevant regulators. A planned aerodrome hub would have a runway measuring 1,800 metres by 30 metres, with an additional 15 metres.

Vice-Chancellor Abiodun Adeniyi described the acquisition as part of a wider entrepreneurial vision, saying investments in education, healthcare and aviation could build local capacity, create jobs and address national needs. He has said the university aims to become the first private university in Africa to operate its own aviation school. The university’s aviation plans add to its earlier investments in higher education and healthcare; aviation training also requires substantial funding for aircraft, infrastructure, maintenance, safety systems and regulatory compliance.

title: 2027: How PDP crisis threatens Adebutu’s Ogun gov ambition
summary: Oladipupo Adebutu’s 2027 Ogun bid is uncertain after INEC omitted him and his running mate from its candidate list. The PDP says it may seek legal redress.
body:
Oladipupo Adebutu’s bid to contest the 2027 Ogun State governorship election is in doubt after the Independent National Electoral Commission omitted him and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, from its final list of candidates. INEC said the PDP did not submit its membership register before holding valid primaries. The commission did not add the pair after the 14-day period for appeals expired. Adebutu says he is a registered party member and qualified to contest. He received 262,383 votes in the 2023 governorship election.

The dispute is rooted in a wider PDP leadership crisis, with rival groups led by Abdulrahman Mohammed and Kabiru Turaki each claiming national leadership. INEC recognises the Mohammed-led executive, while both groups held membership registration exercises within the required period. A PDP official in Ogun said Adebutu registered with the Turaki faction and was absent from the digital register submitted by the Mohammed-led group. Adebutu has said he helped organise the party’s registration exercise in Ogun, which he said enrolled more than 19,800 members, and gave his registration number as 1536.

The episode echoes a dispute before the 2019 governorship election, when rival PDP factions held separate primaries. Adebutu won one faction’s ticket, but a Federal High Court directed INEC to recognise Buruji Kashamu as the party’s candidate. Adebutu has accused the APC and its candidate, Olamilekan Adeola, of trying to weaken the opposition. He says the controversy has not slowed the PDP’s preparations and that the party has visited 12 local government areas.

PDP figures in Ogun have expressed confidence that Adebutu will still appear on the ballot, through an administrative resolution or court action. Former Ijebu East local government chairman Wale Adedayo questioned why INEC published 38 of the 40 candidates submitted by the party while excluding Adebutu and his running mate. Board of Trustees member Fasiu Bakene said the party would consider legal action if the names were not restored. The APC, meanwhile, has blamed the PDP’s internal divisions and alleged failure to follow INEC’s membership-registration rules, rejecting claims of interference.

title: [FULL LIST] Umejiaku Wins Golden Ball At U-17 Women’s World Cup
summary: Oluebube Umejiaku won the Golden Ball at the 2026 U-17 Women’s World Cup after helping Nigeria claim its first title. DPR Korea and Japan also received awards.
body:
Nigeria forward Oluebube Umejiaku has been named the adidas Golden Ball winner at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. She received the award after helping the Flamingos win their first title, defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Rabat. Umejiaku scored Nigeria’s second goal and finished the tournament with four goals.

DPR Korea’s Yu Jong-hyang won the Silver Ball, and Japan’s Fuki Ito took the Bronze Ball. Yu also received the Silver Boot. DPR Korea’s Ri Ui-gyong was awarded the Bronze Boot.

The Golden Boot went to United States forward Maddie DiMaria, the tournament’s top scorer with 12 goals. DPR Korea goalkeeper Kim Son-gyong won the Golden Glove, while Japan received the FIFA Fair Play Trophy.

title: COP31: What Nigeria, other African countries will push for at UN climate summit
summary: African negotiators will seek predictable climate finance, adaptation funding and a strong Green Climate Fund replenishment at COP31. Nigeria will negotiate through the bloc.
body:
## African negotiators set out priorities for COP31

The African Group of Negotiators (AGN) says it will press for increased and predictable climate finance at COP31, including grant-based and concessional funding and an ambitious replenishment of the Green Climate Fund (GCF). The conference is scheduled to take place in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November. Nigeria, one of the 54 countries represented by the AGN, will negotiate under the group’s umbrella. Its delegation and technical support are expected to be led by Nigeria Council on Climate Change Director General Omotenioye Majekodunmi.

AGN Chair Nana Antwi-Boasiako said African countries had developed structures to implement the Paris Agreement, including national climate targets, adaptation plans, carbon market mechanisms and transparency measures. But financing remains a major barrier to putting those commitments into practice. The group has proposed agenda items on tripling adaptation finance and replenishing the GCF. It wants COP31 discussions to clarify how the adaptation-finance decision reached at COP30 will be implemented, and for next year’s GCF replenishment to secure strong contributions.

The AGN also says developed countries must meet their existing financial obligations under Article 9 of the Paris Agreement. While the group is open to broadening the pool of contributors, Antwi-Boasiako argued that contributions from other countries must not replace developed countries’ obligations. Negotiations are divided over finance, with developing countries seeking scaled-up, predictable funding and developed countries pointing to geopolitical and domestic economic pressures.

Other priorities include a Just Transition Mechanism that addresses workers, natural-resource management, energy poverty and wider economic effects, rather than focusing only on energy. The group says the transition should not impose economic hardship or leave African countries unable to use resources needed for development. It is also seeking negotiations on climate-related trade measures, greater consultation on initiatives led by the COP Presidency, and capacity-building to support young Africans entering climate negotiations.

Türkiye will host COP31 while Australia leads the negotiations. The AGN is coordinating with African delegates and engaging other developing-country blocs to build support for its proposed agenda items before the agenda is adopted on 9 November. The group sees the conference as an opportunity to strengthen Africa’s position ahead of COP32, which Ethiopia is due to host next year.

title: VIDEO: Oluremi Tinubu cheers Flamingos during World Cup final
summary: Oluremi Tinubu cheered Nigeria’s Flamingos from her residence as they faced Japan in the U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Nigeria won 2-1 for its first title.
body:
Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, watched the Flamingos’ FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup final against Japan from her residence, cheering the team as it competed for the title. A video shared on social media showed her applauding the players and chanting, “Nigeria! Nigeria!” during the match.

The Flamingos won 2-1 at the Mohammed VI Football Complex. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring in the 39th minute, and Oluebube Umejiaku added Nigeria’s second in the 47th. Japan reduced the deficit through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but Nigeria held on to secure the victory.

The win made Nigeria the first African nation to claim the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. It also made Nigeria the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 World Cup in both the men’s and women’s categories.

The Flamingos’ route to the title included a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They went on to become the first team in the competition’s history to lose its opening game and still win the tournament.

title: Trump orders Justice Department probe of Democrats seeking impeachment
summary: Trump says he has directed the Justice Department to investigate Democrats’ impeachment threats, calling them extortion. Democrats have pledged inquiries into his administration.
body:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that he had directed the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration. In a post on Truth Social, he called the threats extortion, said no impeachable acts had occurred and argued that those responsible should face accountability, including imprisonment.

The order follows Tuesday’s midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Democrats have pledged investigations into Trump and senior administration officials, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Their control of committees in both chambers gives them the power to summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings.

Potential subjects for scrutiny include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving Elon Musk, federal agency cuts, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Democrats have also indicated interest in how files concerning Jeffrey Epstein, a notorious sex offender, were handled. The administration could resist requests for testimony or documents, setting up possible court battles.

Democrats could pursue a third impeachment of Trump, although party leaders have not committed to doing so. The House can impeach a president by a simple majority, but removal requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate, a threshold far beyond the party’s numbers, according to the supplied material.

title: Central Africa Government Calls Planned Fuel Protest ‘Illegal’
summary: Central African Republic officials say a planned opposition march over fuel prices is illegal. Organisers demand lower prices and the release of four arrested civil society officials.
body:
Central Africa Government Calls Planned Fuel Protest ‘Illegal’

The Central African Republic government warned on Saturday that it would not permit a planned opposition protest over rising fuel prices. Government spokesman Evariste Ngamana said the organisers would not be able to march next Friday because the demonstration would be illegal. He said the government would not allow disorder and that rules must be respected.

The Republican Bloc for the Defence of the Constitution (BRDC) called for the protest. The group also organised a shutdown of the capital, Bangui, on October 12. Four senior civil society officials were arrested and jailed following that action. The BRDC is demanding their immediate and unconditional release, as well as a reduction in fuel prices to below 1,000 CFA francs ($1.70) per litre.

A fuel price increase at the start of October has prompted widespread discontent. The latest hike raised the price of petrol to 1,150 CFA francs per litre and diesel to 1,400 CFA francs. The Central African Republic is among the world’s poorest countries, and its reliance on imported fuel makes supplies vulnerable to security and logistical problems. Shortages often lead people to turn to the black market.

The government describes the BRDC as “illegitimate and illegal”. Ngamana said officials were not afraid of the planned march, while stressing that the country was governed by the rule of law. The government had not indicated what action it would take to prevent the protest.

title: Plateau assures corps members of safety, donates N6m at orientation ceremony
summary: Plateau Governor Caleb Mutfwang pledged support for corps members’ safety and welfare at an orientation ceremony. He and a ministry official donated N6m.
body:
Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang has assured National Youth Service Corps members serving in the state that his administration will work with security agencies to protect them and support their welfare. He gave the assurance at the opening and swearing-in ceremony for the 2026 Batch C Stream II orientation course on Saturday at the NYSC Temporary Orientation Camp in Doi-Du, Jos South Local Government Area.

Represented at the ceremony by Youth and Sports Development Commissioner Miaphen, who chairs the state’s NYSC Governing Board, Mutfwang said the protection of corps members remained a priority. He said the state government was working with security agencies and other stakeholders to strengthen security, and urged corps members to stay alert and follow security guidelines during their service year.

The governor also called on the new corps members to contribute to national development through community service and to promote unity by respecting Nigeria’s ethnic, religious and cultural diversity, as well as the customs of their host communities. He donated N5m to welcome them to Plateau State and support the orientation exercise.

Miaphen separately donated N1m on behalf of the Ministry of Youth and Sports Development, recognising the NYSC Plateau State Dance Troupe’s performance at the ceremony. State NYSC Coordinator Jonathan Yavala urged corps members to uphold the dignity of the NYSC uniform and show discipline, tolerance, humility, respect and patriotism. He also encouraged active participation in the orientation course, relationship-building across cultural boundaries and the use of their skills and experience to address challenges in their host communities.

title: Police bullet kills girl, injures another in Lagos
summary: A Lagos police officer has been detained after his firearm struck two girls during an operation in Ajegunle. One died and the other is stable as an inquiry proceeds.
body:
A police officer has been detained after his firearm struck two girls during an operation in the Nosamu area of Ajegunle, Lagos. One of the girls, identified by police as Omole Taiwo, died after being taken to hospital; the other is receiving medical care and is in stable condition. The incident occurred on Thursday, November 5, between 9.30 pm and 10 pm, according to a statement issued by the Lagos State Police Command on Saturday.

The command said Assistant Superintendent of Police Omotayo Olajide discharged his firearm during a response to a reported clash between two rival groups, the Nosamu Boys and the Alayabiagba Boys. Police said the groups were reportedly fighting over toll collection and carrying cutlasses and other dangerous weapons. Both girls were taken to Ajeromi General Hospital. Taiwo was later transferred to the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital in Ikeja, where she died.

Olajide has been disarmed and detained, and the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department. The police said the investigation would establish what happened and determine any appropriate legal or disciplinary action. Commissioner of Police Tijani Fatai visited Taiwo’s family to offer condolences and said no officer found responsible would be protected.

The police account does not clarify whether Olajide intentionally fired at the rival groups, whether the girls were caught in the line of fire or whether the weapon discharged unintentionally. The incident recalls a fatal shooting in Ajegunle in April 2019, when 20-year-old Ada Ifeanyi was killed and Emmanuel Akomafuwa was injured. An officer involved in that case was later dismissed after an investigation found he had abused his authority and used his firearm unlawfully.

title: Police detain officer over fatal shooting of young girl in Lagos
summary: A Lagos police officer has been disarmed and detained after a girl was fatally shot during an operation in Ajegunle. Another child was injured.
body:
A Lagos police officer has been disarmed and detained after a young girl was fatally shot and another child injured during a police operation in the Nosamu area of Ajegunle. The incident occurred on Thursday night, November 5, 2026, as officers responded to a violent clash over toll collection between two rival groups, known as the Nosamu Boys and the Alayabiagba Boys.

Police spokesperson SP Abimbola Adebisi said the factions were reportedly armed with cutlasses and other dangerous weapons. During the operation to restore order, Assistant Superintendent of Police Omotayo Olajide discharged his firearm, and a bullet struck the two girls, according to the statement issued on Saturday.

Both children were taken to Ajeromi General Hospital for emergency treatment. Omole Taiwo was later transferred to Lagos State University Teaching Hospital in Ikeja, where she was pronounced dead. The second child remains in hospital and is reported to be in stable condition.

The police command said the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department for a thorough and impartial inquiry into the circumstances of the shooting. The investigation is intended to establish what happened and determine any appropriate legal or disciplinary measures. Commissioner of Police Tijani Fatai visited Taiwo’s family to offer condolences and said no officer found culpable would be shielded. The command expressed sorrow over the loss of life and urged anyone with relevant information to contact a nearby police station or its Public Relations Department.

title: Power minister explains recent nationwide outages
summary: Power Minister Joseph Tegbe said Egbin maintenance and gas constraints have reduced generation, prompting load shedding. Initial units could return within 48 to 72 hours.
body:
Power Minister Joseph Tegbe has attributed recent electricity outages in major Nigerian cities to planned maintenance at Egbin Power Station and constraints on gas supplies to some thermal plants. He said the issues had reduced the amount of electricity available on the national grid and that he was aware of the strain on households and businesses in four affected states, including Lagos and the Federal Capital Territory.

Grid operators have introduced load shedding in some areas to manage the shortfall, Tegbe said. He also cited sabotage of key transmission lines, which has restricted the use of alternative routes to supply some locations, particularly Lagos.

The minister said work was under way to return affected generating units to service in phases. The first units were expected to come back online within 48 to 72 hours. Tegbe said his team was also working with operators to improve gas supply and speed up repairs to damaged infrastructure, with further updates promised as electricity supply is restored.

The disruption has added pressure on households and businesses amid high temperatures and elevated petrol prices. Some consumers have increasingly turned to solar systems and inverters as alternatives. The outages also reflect persistent constraints on electricity delivery, including limited plant availability, gas supply problems, maintenance needs and transmission infrastructure challenges.

title: Afreximbank targets $1 billion investment deals at CANEX WKND 2026 in Lagos
summary: Afreximbank is seeking at least $1 billion in investor commitments at CANEX WKND 2026 in Lagos. Two cooperation agreements worth about $100 million have been signed.
body:
Afreximbank is targeting at least $1 billion in capital commitments from prospective investors at CANEX WKND 2026 in Lagos, as it seeks to expand investment in Africa’s creative economy. Kanayo Awani, the bank’s executive vice president for Intra-African Trade and Export Development, outlined the target while speaking to journalists on Friday at the CANEX Summit, held at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Theatre.

Awani said she expected the Lagos event to exceed the results of the previous gathering in Algiers, Algeria. There, Afreximbank facilitated about $540 million in trade and investment transactions in 2024. The bank had signed two cooperation agreements worth approximately $100 million on Thursday, with further commitments expected before the four-day programme ends on Sunday.

Awani said Nigeria’s market size and the opportunities in its creative industries supported a higher target. CANEX WKND is an Afreximbank initiative intended to promote investment, trade and commercial activity across Africa’s cultural and creative sectors.

The programme brings together activities spanning music, film, fashion, literature, spoken-word poetry, sports and other creative fields. Exhibitions, writing workshops, literary events and culinary showcases are among the activities, alongside a marketplace, book fairs and business-to-business meetings intended to connect creative businesses with investors and industry stakeholders. The initiative also aims to improve access to finance, international markets and distribution networks for the sector.

The investment effort comes as Afreximbank reports that its net income rose 24% to $813.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The bank has identified the creative economy as an area with potential to support employment, export earnings and economic diversification.

title: Tinubu mocks Obi over Anambra erosion
summary: Tinubu criticised Peter Obi over erosion in Anambra at an APC rally in Akwa Ibom, and also questioned Atiku Abubakar’s political loyalty and leadership.
body:
President Bola Tinubu criticised Peter Obi over the erosion crisis in Anambra State, where Obi served as governor, during an All Progressives Congress rally in Akwa Ibom State on Friday. Tinubu did not name Obi directly, but referred to a presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and accused him of avoiding the problem while in office.

Tinubu contrasted the Anambra situation with his own record in Lagos, saying he had confronted and “tamed” the Atlantic Ocean. He also praised Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno, saying Eno had confronted erosion in the state and was working for its people. The remarks were made to APC supporters and members at the rally.

The president also criticised African Democratic Congress presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar, questioning his political loyalty and leadership. Tinubu said Atiku had left the Peoples Democratic Party after a disagreement and joined the ADC, and argued that this raised doubts about his ability to lead. He also said the opposition lacked leadership and character.

Tinubu praised the APC as a united party with members he described as dependable and reliable, citing former party chairman Umar Ganduje among its leaders. His comments focused on the opposition candidates and parties as he addressed the party gathering.

title: Mbah inaugurates 68 development centre administrators to take projects, policies to more communities
summary: Enugu Governor Peter Mbah swore in 68 Development Centre appointees, urging them to connect communities with government programmes. He also outlined service and political priorities.
body:
Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah has sworn in 68 Development Centre administrators and members, urging them to strengthen grassroots governance and explain government policies and projects to residents. The ceremony took place on Thursday at the International Conference Centre in Enugu. Mbah said their oath of office carried a commitment to serve with integrity and described the centres as the tier of government closest to the people.

The appointees are expected to take state and local programmes closer to communities, especially women, families and rural residents, while complementing local governments’ statutory responsibilities. Mbah urged them to work with local government chairmen and explain how government interventions are intended to benefit residents, rather than simply announcing projects.

He cited Smart Green Schools and Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres as examples, saying the administrators should explain how the facilities could support maternal and child health, childhood immunisation and access to essential care. He also asked them to promote awareness of water and sanitation initiatives, including the campaign to make Enugu open-defecation-free. Mbah reaffirmed the administration’s 10,000-kilometre road development target and cited progress in tourism, transportation and gratuity payments to retired workers at state and local government levels.

Mbah said the administration would hold campaign and performance-assessment engagements at Development Centres to present its work in communities and wards. His Special Adviser on Political Matters, Frank Anioma, urged the appointees to mobilise grassroots support for the governor’s re-election bid. Responding for the appointees, Enugu North Administrator Kenechukwu Ikenegbu pledged sustained community engagement and support for the APC and its candidates in forthcoming elections. State Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice Osinachi Nnajieze conducted the swearing-in.

title: Ebonyi Youths Protest Political Violence, Intimidation Ahead Of 2027 Elections
summary: Hundreds of Ebonyi youths marched in Abakaliki, urging an end to political violence and intimidation ahead of the 2027 elections. They called for safe participation.
body:
Hundreds of young people from across Ebonyi State marched through Abakaliki, calling for an end to political violence, intimidation and harassment of opposition members ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group, Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy, said participants came from all 13 local government areas to press for a political environment where people can take part without fear.

The demonstrators carried placards calling for peaceful political debate and protection of freedom of speech. A spokesperson said the group would not accept efforts to undermine citizens’ rights to express themselves and assemble peacefully.

The group also raised concern about reported physical violence, harassment and voter intimidation directed at opposition figures in parts of the state. It said political thuggery and threats could harm the democratic process, and argued that citizens should be able to participate regardless of party affiliation.

The protesters asked security agencies and state institutions to intervene and help ensure a fair environment for all political parties. A youth coordinator said opposition parties should be able to campaign, present their programmes and engage voters without threats. The group described the march as part of a wider effort by young people to demand accountability and support peaceful political participation as the 2027 elections approach.

title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
summary: The US has reported 5,182 measles cases in 2026, the highest count since 1991. Officials have also reported at least eight related deaths.
body:
The United States has recorded 5,182 confirmed measles cases so far in 2026, according to figures released by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The total is the highest the agency has recorded since 1991, and more than twice the 2,289 cases reported during all of 2025. Measles is highly contagious but preventable through vaccination.

State health officials have reported at least eight deaths linked to measles, including deaths among very young children. The disease can cause fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash. In some cases, it leads to serious complications, including pneumonia and inflammation of the brain, which can cause lasting health problems or death.

Measles was declared eradicated in the United States in 2000, following the introduction of vaccination. The disease has returned in recent years amid falling vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr., who is known for skepticism about vaccines, has been accused of contributing to that distrust by spreading misinformation about the measles vaccine and playing down the risks of the disease.

Before a vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children in the United States each year. The disease continues to cause tens of thousands of deaths worldwide.

title: The 2027 elections: Upsetting the applecart?, By Jibrin Ibrahim
summary: A Federal High Court ruling invalidated the ADC leadership and its 2027 nominations, prompting Atiku Abubakar to condemn the decision. The case raises wider electoral concerns.
body:
A Federal High Court in Abuja has ruled against the African Democratic Congress leadership led by former Senate President David Mark, invalidating decisions made by its caretaker committee and directing the Independent National Electoral Commission not to recognise the party’s 2027 election nominations. The ruling, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu, upheld a challenge by former ADC deputy national chairman Nafiu Bala Gombe, who argued that he was entitled to lead the party after its national chairman resigned. The decision affects the party’s national officers, including National Secretary Rauf Aregbesola, and candidates selected under the Mark-led committee, among them presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar.

Atiku condemned the judgment, describing it as an attempt to weaken the ADC and obstruct his candidacy. In a statement issued by his campaign’s strategic communications director, he pointed to a large turnout at an ADC event in Sokoto shortly before the ruling and said the campaign would continue. The ADC has also questioned why a second case addressed the leadership dispute after Justice Musa Liman of the same court dismissed an earlier challenge. That ruling cited jurisdiction, standing and failure to exhaust internal party remedies, and resolved the substantive issues in favour of the defendants.

The dispute has prompted wider concerns about whether opposition parties can compete freely in the 2027 elections. The article argues that reports of restrictions on campaign access, attacks on candidates and limits on access to media, billboards and venues contribute to an uneven political environment. These claims are presented as part of a broader concern about the use of incumbency and the conditions under which the elections will be conducted.

It also highlights electoral rules and administration. Section 60(3) of the Electoral Act provides for electronic transmission of polling-unit results to IReV while retaining signed physical Form EC8A as the basis for collation when transmission fails. The article says uncertainty about how failure is determined could create disputes. It further raises concerns that a polling-unit form used to document places where elections did not occur may have been dropped from the 2027 guidelines, and questions INEC’s restoration of more than 20 state assembly constituencies and creation of over 450 polling units without National Assembly approval or stakeholder involvement. The article concludes that close public scrutiny will be important to the credibility of the polls.

title: How Plot To Kidnap NYSC Members, Disrupt 2027 Elections Was Uncovered — Amupitan
summary: INEC says intelligence led to arrests over an alleged plan to target NYSC election workers in 2027. The suspects have been charged as security preparations expand.
body:
The Independent National Electoral Commission says it uncovered and foiled a plot by suspected criminal kingpins to kidnap, intimidate and harass National Youth Service Corps members serving as ad-hoc staff in the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan disclosed the case during a meeting with commission staff in Lokoja, Kogi State, held as part of a readiness assessment for the North-Central Zone.

Amupitan said intelligence gathering led to the suspects’ arrest and that the Department of State Services had charged them to court. He warned that anyone threatening or attempting to harm electoral officials, NYSC members or other temporary election personnel would face the full weight of the law. He said the commission would not compromise the safety of staff deployed to conduct elections.

INEC is strengthening security coordination through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, or ICCES. Amupitan said the arrangement brings together the military, police, DSS, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Customs, Immigration, Correctional Services and Federal Road Safety Corps across the six North-Central states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The commission has also adopted an intelligence-led system called the ICCES Tentacle, intended to extend coordination from its national headquarters to local government areas and registration area centres. Election Risk Management tools are being used to identify vulnerable locations, and security assessments across North-Central states will be shared with relevant agencies to support early intervention and deployment. Amupitan identified risk mapping and mitigation, protection of electoral personnel, equipment and voters, and access to polling units as the framework’s three main pillars.

He said election security also covers cybersecurity and the protection of technology used in the process. Polling units within 500 metres of identified vulnerable locations will receive special attention. Amupitan said peaceful voting, effective logistics and efficient results management were essential to the 2027 elections, and reiterated INEC’s aim of keeping polling units safe for voters.

title: Troops arrest suspected terrorist in Plateau
summary: Troops arrested a suspected terrorist in Wase, Plateau State, and recovered ammunition, phones, suspected illicit drugs and cash. He remains in military custody.
body:
Troops of Operation Enduring Peace have arrested a man identified as Abubakar Ango during a stop-and-search operation in Kukawa village, Wase Local Government Area of Plateau State. Military sources said the arrest took place on Thursday as part of a routine security operation to identify and apprehend suspected criminals in the area.

The sources said troops recovered an AK-47 magazine, 7.62mm ammunition, two mobile phones, suspected illicit drugs and N30,000 in cash. The items were found with the suspect, according to the military sources.

They said preliminary questioning had reportedly linked Ango to a suspected terrorist syndicate allegedly led by a person identified as Kaura. Ango was in military custody for further investigation, which the sources said would seek to establish his level of involvement and identify other alleged members of the group.

The military urged residents to provide timely, credible information to security agencies and report suspicious movements to the appropriate authorities. It said public cooperation was important to ongoing efforts to address criminal activity in the state.

title: Tracking The Opposition
summary: Court rulings have put ADC nominations under pressure and limited a PDP faction’s leadership claim. Abia PDP leaders have pledged campaign support for Tinubu.
body:
Tracking the Opposition

A Federal High Court in Abuja on November 5 invalidated the leadership led by David Mark and decisions made under it, including Atiku Abubakar’s presidential nomination and other candidate nominations. The ADC has rejected the judgment and says it will appeal. Its campaign council announced plans to seek interim relief, but no appeal, stay application or order suspending the judgment had been independently verified in the material reviewed. The ruling leaves the party facing uncertainty over its presidential ticket and state candidates. Allegations by the ADC of interference by the APC remain unsubstantiated in the reporting reviewed.

A separate leadership dispute within the PDP also encountered a setback. On November 4, the Court of Appeal upheld the dismissal of a suit by the Wabara-led Board of Trustees seeking INEC recognition for the Turaki-led interim committee. The underlying decision concerned the plaintiffs’ legal standing; the appeal court also described the appeal as academic and an abuse of process. The faction says it plans to approach the Supreme Court. The decision constrains its claim to direct the party, but does not automatically invalidate every PDP nomination.

In Abia, Abraham Amah, identified as the PDP state chairman and deputy governorship candidate, announced support for Tinubu’s re-election at the November 5 inauguration of the APC presidential campaign council. Amah was assigned an interparty mobilisation role. The announcement creates competing political commitments within the state party organisation and could weaken PDP efforts to mobilise for its presidential candidate. It establishes an endorsement and campaign role, not a formal defection or evidence that party supporters will follow him.

Peter Obi, in a November 5 statement, said he was concerned the ADC judgment could restrict electoral choice and disrupt opposition preparations. His intervention does not establish a joint ticket or withdrawal agreement. The key developments to watch include any ADC court filings or interim orders, INEC’s response to the judgment and the Turaki faction’s planned Supreme Court filing. No new order resolving the Ogun, Kano or Niger nomination disputes was established in the material reviewed.

title: Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh
summary: NDC candidate Peter Ameh urged opposition parties not to celebrate the ADC court ruling. He said divisions could benefit the APC and called for credible elections.
body:
High Chief Peter Ameh, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Kogi East, has urged opposition parties not to treat the court judgment affecting the African Democratic Congress (ADC) as a political victory. The ruling sacked the David Mark-led ADC National Working Committee and nullified Atiku Abubakar’s candidacy, according to the account of the decision provided by Ameh.

Speaking in Abuja on Thursday, Ameh warned that celebrating the outcome could deepen divisions among opposition groups. He argued that the All Progressives Congress (APC) would benefit if opposition parties weakened one another, irrespective of their political affiliations. He also cautioned that a ruling seen as favouring one faction could later be used against another.

Ameh described the judgment as a warning rather than a win for any side. He urged opposition parties to focus on pressing for free, fair and credible elections instead of becoming consumed by disputes over party leadership and candidates.

He also criticised the APC-led administration, accusing it of failing to provide good governance over the past 11 years. Ameh called on opposition groups to work together to end the party’s rule, saying the APC was responsible for the country’s governance problems.

title: Gov Abiodun declares Ogun ready for state police
summary: Ogun Governor Dapo Abiodun says the state is ready for state police. Cash transfers for vulnerable residents are starting in Sagamu to help offset rising costs.
body:
Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun said his administration was ready to establish a state police force, arguing that the state’s expanding industrial and commercial activity required stronger security. He made the announcement at a town hall meeting in Sagamu on the proposed 2027 budget and the 2027–2029 Medium Term Expenditure Framework. Abiodun chairs the Nigeria Governors’ Forum committee on state police. He said the state had supported its existing security network with vehicles, equipment and allowances, and increased recruitment into Amotekun. Amotekun and the So-Safe Corps together have about 6,000 personnel, he said.

The governor also announced the immediate start of a cash transfer programme for vulnerable households facing higher food and transport costs. He said recipients already identified in the state database in Sagamu would begin receiving payment alerts, with the programme later extending across Remoland and the wider state. Abiodun attributed some of the economic pressure to disruptions in global oil and gas supply chains linked to the Israel-American-Iran conflict, which he said had contributed to higher oil and transport costs.

Abiodun also outlined plans to sink boreholes in all 236 wards and provide transformers and solar-powered streetlights. He said Remoland was central to the state’s development plans. At the meeting, Economic Adviser and Finance Commissioner Dapo Okubadejo said public participation and accountability were important to governance. He reported expenditure of N490 billion against a N703 billion estimate in 2024, or about 70 per cent, and about N700 billion against the N1.05 trillion 2025 budget, or 65 per cent. The N1.67 trillion 2026 budget, he said, was supporting work in infrastructure, education, youth empowerment and agriculture.

Local representatives raised infrastructure and development concerns. Sagamu Local Government Chairman Afolabi Odulate called for action on roads in Sagamu, Remo North and Ikenne, and raised concerns about Lagos encroaching into Ogun through border communities. The Akarigbo of Remoland, Oba Babatunde Ajayi, welcomed development projects but urged the creation of a team to monitor and maintain public facilities. He also called for federal tertiary institutions in Remoland and stronger inclusion of local residents in economic initiatives. Remo’s Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria chair, Adewale Kalejaye, urged greater collaboration on revenue generation and more funding for poverty, hunger and education programmes.

title: Ogun monarch confers chieftaincy titles on Adebutu, Iyabo Obasanjo
summary: Ogun monarch Oba Adedapo Tejuoso installed PDP figures Oladipupo Adebutu, Iyabo Obasanjo and others as Oke-Ona Egba titleholders. The ceremony was held in Abeokuta.
body:
The Osile of Oke-Ona Egba, Oba Adedapo Tejuoso, has installed Peoples Democratic Party governorship candidate Oladipupo Adebutu, his wife and several other party figures as traditional titleholders. The ceremony took place on Thursday at the monarch’s palace in Sapon, Abeokuta, and drew traditional rulers, political figures, community leaders and members of the Ogun State PDP leadership.

Adebutu received the title Lisa Aje of Oke-Ona Egba, while his wife, Adenike, was named Yeye Lisa Aje. Senator Iyabo Obasanjo was installed as Okanlomo Obinrin, and state PDP chairman Abayomi Tella received the title Fiwagbola. Alhaja Lateefat Sowunmi-Kolapo became Olu Nla Obinrin.

Other recipients were Dele Olaleye, named Sesogbayi; Ambassador Folake Marcus-Bello, named Oluomo Obinrin; and Chief Abiodun Ogunremi, named Otun Olu-Nla, all of Oke-Ona Egba. The monarch presented certificates and carried out traditional rites associated with the installations.

Tejuoso said the titles recognised people whose character, credibility and contributions had earned the traditional institution’s confidence. He described Adebutu as trustworthy and urged him and his wife to use the recognition to support development in Oke-Ona Egba and Ogun State. Adebutu called the honour a responsibility and a call to greater service, and pledged to contribute to development in Egbaland and the state.

The installation comes as Adebutu’s status as the PDP’s candidate for the 2027 Ogun governorship election faces uncertainty. He emerged as the party’s nominee after its governorship primary in May, but was omitted from the Independent National Electoral Commission’s list of candidates for the February 2027 election. His petition over the omission was rejected, while Adebutu has maintained that he remains the party’s duly nominated candidate.

title: Hotel accommodation: ‘This is not democracy, APC should allow parties to campaign without hindrance’ — NDC
summary: The NDC alleges Abuja hotels restricted access to venues for party meetings and events. It urged the APC to let parties campaign freely ahead of 2027.
body:
