The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of trying to limit opposition activity, alleging that hotels in Abuja have denied it access to venues for meetings and events. In a statement posted on X on Thursday, the party urged the APC to allow political parties to campaign without hindrance ahead of the 2027 general election.

The NDC said it had been turned away by several hotels despite meeting their requirements for using the facilities. It alleged that one hotel, whose name it did not disclose, cancelled venue agreements twice, including arrangements for the party’s second National Executive Committee meeting in June 2026. The party said the hotel had also recently rejected another request, citing instructions from an undisclosed authority.

The party separately accused another hotel of refusing to provide a venue for a meeting even though it had complied with the hotel’s conditions. It also said the unveiling of its National Campaign Council was nearly disrupted when the host venue asked it to collect a refund and said it would no longer provide the facilities. According to the NDC, it had already paid and insisted on using the venue, after which the hotel honoured the arrangement.

The NDC described the alleged incidents as undemocratic and said they risked frustrating opposition activities and restricting political participation. It called on Nigerians and supporters of democracy to condemn what it characterised as anti-democratic actions by the hotels. The statement was signed by the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, who reaffirmed the NDC’s commitment to serving Nigerians.

title: NGX plunges N3.28 trillion as Dangote Cement, Presco, UACN, HBM Nigeria, Tier 1 banks fall
summary: The NGX All-Share Index fell 1.98% as market value dropped about N3.28 trillion. Heavy losses in Dangote Cement and other large stocks drove the decline.
body:
Nigeria’s equities market shed about N3.28 trillion on Thursday, November 5, 2026, as selling in heavyweight stocks drove the benchmark lower. The NGX All-Share Index fell 5,052.22 points, or 1.98%, to 249,710.59 from 254,762.81 in the previous session. Market capitalisation declined to N162.13 trillion from N165.42 trillion.

Dangote Cement and Presco each fell by the maximum 10%. UACN lost 7.85% and HBM Nigeria declined 7.71%. Selling in First HoldCo, Nigerian Exchange Group, Nigerian Breweries, Stanbic IBTC, GTCO and UBA added to the downward pressure. Among those large-cap stocks, Stanbic IBTC fell 0.85% to N162.50, GTCO slipped 0.81% to N122.00 and UBA eased 0.24% to N42.00.

Dangote Cement was the largest single drag on market value. Its N149 decline accounted for roughly N2.5 trillion, or about three-quarters of the day’s total loss. The stock closed at N1,341, down from N1,490 on Wednesday. Despite the fall, it remained about 33% above its October 19 close of N1,008, following a 5.50% drop that day which removed N1.47 trillion from the market.

Market breadth weakened, with 36 stocks declining against 20 advancing, and all six sector indices finished lower. Industrial stocks recorded the sharpest sector decline. The year-to-date market return moderated to 60.47% from 63.72%, while the month-to-date return turned negative at about 1.8%.

Trading increased as prices fell: investors exchanged 856.28 million shares worth N74.09 billion in 33,540 deals. The market’s decline more than erased the N307.4 billion added in the previous sessions, when buying in Transcorp Power and banking stocks lifted prices. Continued selling in large-cap shares could keep the market volatile, while bargain-hunting in oversold heavyweights may offer support.

title: 2027: Keyamo faults opposition over ‘rig and die’ claim
summary: Festus Keyamo mocked the “rig and die” slogan ahead of 2027, saying it could weaken opposition fraud claims. Ovie Omo-Agege said it targeted election manipulators.
body:
Aviation and Aerospace Development Minister Festus Keyamo has criticised opposition politicians promoting the “rig and die” slogan ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. In a post on X on Thursday, he argued sarcastically that the phrase could make it harder for politicians to blame an electoral defeat on fraud if the vote was free and fair.

Keyamo said those who claimed an election had been rigged would, in effect, be challenged to show how many people they had killed on election day. He suggested that adopting the slogan would leave losing politicians unable to use allegations of rigging to explain their results.

The phrase was popularised by former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege, who used it at a campaign event in Uvwie Local Government Area of Delta State on October 23. Omo-Agege is seeking election to represent Delta Central Senatorial District under the Nigeria Democratic Congress. At the event, he threatened that people caught manipulating the 2027 election would be killed and said there would be no recourse to the courts.

Omo-Agege’s remarks drew criticism. His media aide, Godwin Anaughe, later said the warning was aimed at people who manipulate results or steal electoral materials, not voters or innocent citizens. Omo-Agege maintained that the slogan was intended as a warning against electoral malpractice and a call to defend the people’s mandate.

title: “Ba A Gudu Ba A Bar Gida”: Fifth Chukker, photography, cultural memory, and the responsibility of belonging, By Mudi Yahaya
summary: An exhibition in Kaduna presents Nina Fischer-Stephan’s photographs of Northern Nigeria and explores how archives, lived knowledge and memory shape belonging. Its title calls for care of home and the histories that help communities understand themselves.
body:
“Ba A Gudu Ba A Bar Gida,” an archival photography exhibition at the Fifth Chukker Polo and Country Club Resort in Kangimi, Kaduna, uses images by Nina Fischer-Stephan to explore belonging, historical memory and the responsibility to preserve cultural knowledge. Its Hausa title is understood as “One does not flee and abandon one’s home.” The exhibition’s framing treats home as more than buildings and familiar landscapes: it also depends on the knowledge through which people understand their relationships and imagine a shared future.

Fischer-Stephan was born in Munich in 1922 and moved to Ibadan in 1959 with her husband, Klaus Stephan, then an Africa correspondent for German television. For more than eleven years, his press passes afforded her access to Northern Nigeria’s royal courts, prominent figures and architectural heritage. The photographs document the region around the early years of independence, inviting viewers to consider how political change was experienced in everyday life—in homes, streets, clothing, work and encounters.

The exhibition presents the archive as a starting point for inquiry, not a complete account of the society it depicts. Photographs preserve traces of social life, but their meanings depend on context, research and engagement with people connected to the places and subjects shown. A building, market or garment may prompt questions about social organisation and local knowledge; appearance alone cannot settle those questions. The images should also be considered alongside Nigerian photographers and local practices of image-making, rather than treated as the beginning of Northern Nigeria’s photographic history.

The exhibition’s argument carries particular relevance amid insecurity, displacement, economic hardship and political uncertainty in Northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general elections. Its title is not presented as a judgement on people who leave for safety: belonging can persist through departure, memory and community ties. In Kaduna, the photographs can bring archival records into conversation with living knowledge, while recognising that memories may differ and require careful corroboration. The exhibition’s call is to preserve evidence, question inherited interpretations and leave future generations the means to understand the past more fully—without nostalgia or claims that exceed what the archive can support.

title: Police React To Viral Video On Alleged Officers Brutality In Osun
summary: Police in Zone 11 say officers shown in a video allegedly assaulting a suspect in Ede have been identified. An investigation is under way, with discipline promised if misconduct is established.
body:
The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 11, Bassey Ewah, has ordered an investigation after a video circulated on social media showing officers allegedly assaulting a suspect in Ede, Osun State. The incident reportedly took place on Wednesday, according to a statement issued on Thursday by the zone’s public relations officer, Ojedele Tunji.

Ewah said he viewed the footage with serious concern and stressed that the Nigeria Police Force does not condone brutality, intimidation or abuse of power. He said the officers involved had been identified and that steps had been initiated to investigate the incident thoroughly.

The AIG said police have the authority to enforce the law and maintain public order, but must carry out those duties professionally and with restraint. He also emphasised that officers are required to respect the fundamental rights and dignity of every person. Any officer found to have breached regulations or engaged in misconduct would face appropriate disciplinary measures under applicable laws and police regulations, the statement said.

Ewah urged the public to remain calm and avoid reaching conclusions before the investigation is complete. He said Zone 11, which serves Osun and Oyo states, remained committed to accountability, transparency and the protection of human rights, and that no officer was above the law.

title: Portfolio investments provide liquidity, pave way for deeper foreign capital – Oduwole
summary: Oduwole said portfolio inflows can introduce foreign investors to Nigeria and support deeper capital. She urged turning investment announcements into deployed funds.
body:
Portfolio investments can provide liquidity to Nigeria’s economy and help attract deeper, longer-term foreign capital, Industry, Trade and Investment Minister Jumoke Oduwole said. She described portfolio inflows as a way for investors to assess the Nigerian market before considering larger commitments in other sectors, arguing that their role is often underappreciated.

Oduwole said the government is promoting opportunities in the creative economy, environment, agribusiness and climate financing to attract international partnerships. She clarified that the $500 million associated with the Algiers engagement referred to business connections and potential partnerships between Nigerian private-sector companies and international investors. It was separate from the wider economic benefits of hosting investment events, she said, and should be viewed as a baseline for opportunities being pursued.

She also said investment announcements connected to President Bola Tinubu’s foreign trips had reached $50 billion as of 2025. These included about $8 billion in staged fertiliser investments and plans involving roughly $1.5 billion from Coca-Cola. Oduwole said the priority was to ensure announcements become actual investments.

Central Bank of Nigeria data showed portfolio inflows rose 45% to $6.51 billion in the second quarter of 2026, from $4.49 billion in the previous quarter. Such inflows reflect foreign participation in financial markets but are generally more exposed to changing market conditions than longer-term direct investment. The government has also outlined a wider investment pipeline: in October 2026, it unveiled 65 projects requiring a combined $78.5 billion. A Nigeria Deal Room, announced in June 2026, is intended to help turn opportunities into bankable transactions and address regulatory obstacles to implementation.

title: Six climate measures could save 1.6 million lives yearly – WHO
summary: Six climate and health interventions could avert 1.6 million deaths a year and cut emissions, according to WHO modelling. The measures could also deliver trillions in annual gains.
body:
Six climate and health interventions could prevent an estimated 1.6 million deaths each year and avoid 16.7 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually, according to a World Health Organisation report. The projected emissions reduction is equivalent to 31 per cent of annual global greenhouse gas emissions, excluding emissions from land use and forestry.

The measures are heat-health warning systems; climate-resilient drinking-water services; basic sanitation; hygiene and handwashing facilities; cleaner household fuels and technologies for cooking and heating; and more efficient fossil fuel pricing policies. The WHO says the interventions could produce $3.9 trillion in annual economic welfare benefits and $5.4 trillion in fiscal gains if implemented globally.

The report estimates that five of the interventions could return $24 in benefits for every dollar invested, with higher returns expected in low- and middle-income countries. Heat-health warning systems are projected to deliver particularly large returns—an estimated $835 for every dollar invested—because expanding existing systems is relatively inexpensive and could help prevent heat-related illness.

Efficient fossil fuel pricing policies are projected to generate the largest overall gains. Measures such as removing inefficient fossil fuel subsidies and appropriately taxing fossil fuels could prevent 1.2 million deaths a year, while producing $3 trillion in economic welfare benefits and $5.4 trillion in fiscal gains, the report says.

The WHO described the report as its first comprehensive assessment of the economic and fiscal returns from scaling up the six interventions. It argues that many health effects of climate change can be addressed with existing solutions, but governments need to put them into practice across health and other sectors. WHO Director-General Tedros Ghebreyesus urged governments to put health at the centre of climate action, particularly as countries prepare their commitments for the next round of international climate negotiations.

title: Como Record Stunning 9-1 Win Against Lens In Champions League
summary: Como beat Lens 9-1 away in the Champions League, matching the modern-era scoring record. Anastasios Douvikas scored a hat-trick for Cesc Fabregas’s side.
body:
Como recorded a 9-1 away victory over Lens in France on Wednesday, matching the record for the most goals scored by one team in a Champions League game in the competition’s modern era. The result also marked the heaviest defeat suffered by a French team in the tournament.

Anastasios Douvikas scored three times to lead Como’s attack. The Italian side is coached by Cesc Fabregas and has won three of its four matches in this season’s league phase.

Bayern Munich also scored nine goals in a Champions League match, beating Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in 2024. Liverpool and Real Madrid have each recorded 8-0 group-stage victories.

title: 2027: INEC urges Nigerians to protect electoral integrity
summary: INEC’s Abia commissioner urged Nigerians to counter misinformation and protect confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The commission is testing election technology.
body:
INEC urges Nigerians to protect electoral integrity ahead of 2027

The Independent National Electoral Commission has urged Nigerians to help protect electoral integrity and rebuild public confidence ahead of the 2027 general elections. Abia State Resident Electoral Commissioner Sylvia Agu made the call in Umuahia on Wednesday at a media retreat organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists in Abia State. The event focused on journalism in an era of disinformation.

Agu said false information could weaken trust in elections, and that confidence in the 2027 polls would be shaped both by what happens at polling stations and by the information voters receive and believe. She identified declining public confidence as a significant challenge, saying perceptions of electoral conduct and the credibility of claims shared with voters influence trust in the process.

She said INEC was working to strengthen election technology, including the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal, to support transparency. Agu described BVAS as a safeguard against electoral malpractice, including fictitious accreditation and voting. The commission is also prioritising cybersecurity, protection of voter and election data, and the reliability of its digital infrastructure, she said.

Agu said INEC was exploring the responsible use of artificial intelligence for planning, data analysis and operational efficiency, while keeping human judgement and oversight central. She also said the commission had been testing its equipment and information technology facilities in recent months to reduce the risk of technical failures. Preparation includes staff training and retraining, voter education, simulation exercises and knowledge sharing.

The preparations follow continuing debate over INEC’s technology during the 2023 elections, when the transmission of presidential results to the results portal was delayed. The commission attributed the delay to technical glitches, and the episode drew criticism and renewed calls for greater transparency and reliability. Agu said the commission was applying lessons from previous election cycles as it works to improve its systems and public confidence.

title: Obi vows to pursue kidnappers into their hideouts
summary: Peter Obi pledged to pursue kidnappers of schoolchildren and make security a priority. He also promised to focus on national unity, education, health and curbing corruption.
body:
Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, pledged to pursue kidnappers of schoolchildren into their hideouts if elected, saying his administration would not be intimidated by criminal groups. He made the commitment at the party’s presidential town hall meeting on Wednesday at the Metropolitan Hotel in Calabar, where he said Nigeria could no longer tolerate the current level of insecurity.

Obi said his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, had served as Minister of Defence and that securing the country would be a priority. He identified national unity as the first task of an NDC government, arguing that division would make it harder to confront insecurity. He said he had also conveyed that message during an earlier meeting with the Obong of Calabar.

The candidate pledged that an NDC administration would invest in education and healthcare, describing education as one of the most important areas of national development. He also presented the presidential ticket as a different approach to governance, saying he and Kwankwaso would work as partners to drive change.

On corruption, Obi said voters could assess the records of both candidates. He promised to intensify efforts against the misuse of public funds, saying government money should serve the public and support people’s welfare. Obi said the town hall was intended to hear from residents and other stakeholders, and invited participants to ask questions and make comments without restriction.

title: Nigerian stocks gain N307 billion as Transcorp Power, banks drive market rally
summary: Nigerian equities added N307.4 billion on Wednesday as Transcorp Power and major banks led gains. The All-Share Index rose 0.19%, with 27 stocks advancing.
body:
Nigerian stocks gained approximately N307.4 billion on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, as buying in Transcorp Power and major banking shares lifted the broader market. The NGX All-Share Index advanced 0.19% to 254,762.81 points, from 254,289.35 in the previous session, while market capitalisation rose to N165.42 trillion.

Transcorp Power led the session’s gainers, rising 9.97%. GTCO added 5.1%, UBA gained 2.68% and Zenith Bank rose 2.65%. Honeywell Flour increased 4.04% to N24.45, while Transcorp edged up 0.17% to N30.05. The Banking Index climbed 0.72% to 2,403.98 points, making banking the strongest-performing sector reported.

The advance came despite losses in several shares. Eterna fell 9.94% to N38.50, the session’s steepest decline, while Sovereign Trust Insurance and Learn Africa each lost nearly 10%. Overall market breadth was positive: 27 stocks advanced, compared with 23 that declined.

Investors traded 552.31 million shares worth N37.46 billion in 32,874 transactions. Share volume and transaction value increased, but the number of deals fell 15.88%. The session extended Tuesday’s N28.65 billion gain, which had recovered most of Monday’s losses. The market’s year-to-date return rose to 63.72%, and its month-to-date return reached 0.2%. Gains in major stocks supported the rally, while declines in other counters left the overall performance mixed.

title: Falana Tasks Lagos Legal Centre With Preserving Nigeria’s Legal History
summary: Femi Falana urged Lagos to preserve landmark judgments and promote compliance through its new legal study centre. He also called for greater attention to customary courts.
body:
Lagos State has opened the Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training in Alausa, Ikeja, with human rights lawyer Femi Falana urging the government to use it to preserve Nigeria’s legal history and encourage compliance with court judgments. The Centre was established by the Lagos State Ministry of Justice as a hub for research, professional training, policy development and capacity building for justice-sector practitioners and public officials.

Speaking at the opening on Wednesday, Falana said landmark decisions should be preserved so that important parts of the country’s legal history remain available to future generations. He cited the 1921 case of Amodu Tijani v Secretary, Southern Nigeria, which dealt with indigenous proprietary and usufructuary rights, as an example of a decision the Centre should document.

Falana also called for the Centre to give attention to customary courts. He said reforms since the return to democratic rule in 1999 had focused largely on superior courts, while customary courts had not received comparable attention. He argued that the Centre could help deepen public understanding of Nigeria’s legal system and strengthen respect for judicial decisions.

At the ceremony, Lagos Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice Lawal Pedro described the Centre as an investment in knowledge and the future of justice administration, rather than simply a new government facility. He said a justice system seeking to remain effective must continue to educate, assess and reform itself. The state presented the Centre as a means of developing legal expertise and preparing its justice institutions for emerging challenges.

title: Dangote Unveils Namibia Energy Project, Proposes 1.6mb Tank Farm
summary: Aliko Dangote unveiled plans for a petroleum storage and regional pipeline project in Walvis Bay. The proposed tank farm would hold at least 1.6 million barrels.
body:
Nigerian industrialist Aliko Dangote has unveiled plans for a petroleum storage and regional pipeline project in Walvis Bay, Namibia. The proposal is intended to expand fuel storage capacity and improve distribution across Southern Africa.

The proposed facility would store at least 1.6 million barrels of petrol and diesel. The plans were presented at an event attended by President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah and senior government officials.

The project is described as a major investment proposition, but the available information does not specify a construction timeline or other details about its implementation.

title: Elon Musk jokes about GOP election defeat after spending record sums on party
summary: Elon Musk joked that his election spending failed after Democrats won both chambers of Congress. He gave nearly $500 million to Republican political efforts.
body:
Elon Musk responded with a joke on Wednesday after Republicans lost control of Congress in the US midterm elections, despite his extensive financial support for the party. Democrats captured both the Senate and House of Representatives on Tuesday, in a result described as a rejection of President Donald Trump’s political agenda. On X, Musk suggested humorously that his supposed “election-interfering space lasers” had failed, adding a shrug emoji.

Musk contributed nearly half a billion dollars to Republican political efforts, making him the largest individual donor in a federal election cycle since unlimited election spending was allowed in 2010, according to campaign finance tracker OpenSecrets. Most of his donations went to the Republican-leaning America PAC and the Republican Senate Leadership Fund, a super PAC.

The Senate Leadership Fund used $158 million in donations from Musk in September to support Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate candidate in Texas. Paxton, an ally of Trump, was defeated by Democrat James Talarico. Talarico’s victory made him the first Democrat to win statewide office in Texas since 1994.

At a victory rally in Austin, Talarico described the race as a contest against powerful opponents, including Musk, Trump and the Washington establishment. The result in Texas came as Democrats also took control of both chambers of Congress, despite the scale of Musk’s financial backing for Republican candidates and political groups.

title: Brazil vs Nigeria: Five players who could decide crucial semi-final showdown
summary: Nigeria meet unbeaten Brazil in Wednesday’s U-17 Women’s World Cup semi-final. Five players could shape the contest and Nigeria’s bid to reach their first final.
body:
Nigeria’s Flamingos face one of their toughest tests at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup when they meet Brazil in Wednesday’s semi-final in Morocco. A place in the final would be a first for Nigeria at this level. Akeem Busari’s side have won four consecutive matches since losing their opener to Poland, including a 3-1 victory over defending champions DPR Korea. Brazil are unbeaten and have scored 17 goals in five games.

Goalkeeper Jane Ijirigho will be central to Nigeria’s effort to contain that attack. She has made 16 saves at the tournament, including important interventions against Puerto Rico and Mexico. Brazil’s threat comes from multiple players, so Ijirigho’s reflexes and communication with her defence may be as important as the saves themselves. Helena is among the forwards Nigeria must watch closely: she scored both goals in Brazil’s 2-1 quarter-final comeback against China PR, equalising 42 seconds into the second half before scoring again in the 87th minute.

Greise Kelly is another key danger for Nigeria. The Brazil forward has three goals and five assists, the most assists recorded by any player in the competition. Her eight direct goal contributions account for 47.06 per cent of Brazil’s goals, according to tournament statistics. Nigeria will need to restrict her space and disrupt her ability to create chances for teammates. Brazil’s attack also includes Marcela Bontorim, Nicolly Manuel and Pepe, adding to the challenge of defending them.

Nigeria will look to Oluebube Umejiaku and Oluwakemi Adegbuyi for a response. Umejiaku has scored three times and won the late penalty converted by Azeezat Oduntan in the quarter-final against Venezuela. Adegbuyi has scored twice, including against DPR Korea, and offers another threat in the final third. Brazil have conceded nine goals in five matches, leaving potential openings for Nigeria if they can attack quickly and use runs behind the defence. The Flamingos’ pressing and physical energy could help disrupt Brazil, but they will need to maintain defensive discipline. Strong performances from these five players could shape Nigeria’s chance of reaching a historic first final.

title: 2027: ‘Tomorrow is Here’ group rallies Nsukka voters for Mbah, Tinubu’s re-election
summary: The Tomorrow Is Here Movement says thousands joined a Nsukka Zone walk backing Peter Mbah, Bola Tinubu and APC candidates in 2027. Leaders cited development projects.
body:
The Tomorrow Is Here Movement (THM) says thousands of supporters took part in a walk across Enugu North Senatorial District, known as Nsukka Zone, to promote the re-election of Governor Peter Mbah and President Bola Tinubu and support other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. The group described the event as a sign of growing support for the party in the district.

The walk began at Opi in Nsukka and passed through Orba, Obollo-Afor and Obollo-Eke in Udenu Local Government Area, then Ogrute and Enugu-Ezike in Igboeze North, Ibagwa-Aka in Igboeze South and other communities in Nsukka Local Government Area. THM leader Chief Tony Okonkwo said the event had been planned for about 200 people but drew thousands. He attributed the turnout to public approval of the two administrations’ work.

Okonkwo pointed to road construction, education, healthcare, agriculture and transport as areas of progress. He cited the dual carriageway planned from 9th Mile through Igbo-Etiti, Nsukka and Udenu to Benue, Smart Green Schools, healthcare facilities and more than 50 compressed natural gas buses operating from Nsukka Central Terminal. He also referred to federal agricultural programmes, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and the appointment of Professor Simon Ortuanya as the University of Nigeria’s first indigenous vice-chancellor. These were presented by the movement as evidence supporting its call for voters to back the APC.

Igbo-Etiti council chairman Martins Ugwu-Amadieze said residents should reject appeals to tribal sentiment and argued that the party had shown commitment to the zone’s development. He said Mbah had acted on requests concerning the university vice-chancellorship and the proposed dualisation of the Penoks–Nike–Ugwogo–Ekwegbe–Opi–Nsukka road. Igboeze North chairman Chris Onyekachi linked increased development opportunities for state and local governments to Tinubu’s economic reforms, while Igboeze South chairman Ferdinand Ukwueze said government projects demonstrated the APC’s capacity to deliver. APC and THM officials, state legislators and local government representatives also attended.

title: Firefighters recover man’s body from Kwara river
summary: Firefighters recovered an unidentified man’s body from a river near Royal Valley Bridge in Ilorin on Tuesday. Police received the body as the cause of death remains unknown.
body:
The Kwara State Fire Service recovered the body of an unidentified man from a river near Royal Valley Bridge in the Kulende area of Ilorin on Tuesday. The man was estimated to be about 50 years old.

A passerby who saw the body floating in the river alerted a radio station, which then contacted the fire service. Firefighters mobilised to the scene at 3:44 pm and carried out the recovery operation.

The body was handed over to SUP Abdulganiu Garuba of the E-Division Police Station in Kulende for further action. The fire service said the circumstances of the incident and the cause of death had not been established, and that further investigation was expected to clarify what happened.

Chief Fire Officer Alabi Muhammed praised the passerby for reporting the discovery and the radio station for relaying the information to emergency responders. He urged residents to report emergencies and suspicious incidents promptly to the relevant authorities.

title: Security agencies rescue eight kidnap victims in Kaduna
summary: Joint security operations in Kaduna rescued eight people abducted in Chikun Local Government Area between October 31 and November 2. More personnel and vehicles are planned.
body:
Eight people, including an eight-year-old girl, have been rescued in coordinated security operations in Kaduna State, according to Commissioner of Police Muhammad Rabiu. The operations took place from October 31 to November 2 in Millennium City and Marabar Rido, both in Chikun Local Government Area, with the Kaduna State Government’s cooperation.

The rescued people were identified as Jamila Muhammad, 27; Talatu Yakubu, 40; Yunana Bawa, 30; Calista Bishop, 27; Chidinma Onuwere, 36; Eucharia Obi, 41; Godiya Victor, 50; and Miracle Alex, eight. Rabiu said the intelligence-led operations were part of continuing efforts to identify and disrupt networks responsible for repeated kidnappings in the area.

The rescue followed the release of Ahmad Zakka and members of his family from captivity on October 15. Rabiu said the successive operations reflected security agencies’ resolve to free abducted people and dismantle criminal networks. He credited the Office of the National Security Adviser with coordination, and cited operational support from the Police, intelligence from the Department of State Services and the Military’s involvement.

Rabiu said agencies were intensifying operations across Kaduna State and planned to deploy additional personnel and equipment, including 30 operational vans and eight armoured personnel carriers. He noted that difficult terrain in parts of the state can help criminal groups carry out attacks and evade security forces.

The commissioner urged residents, traditional rulers and community leaders to share credible information about suspected kidnappers and their activities, assuring the public that information would be treated confidentially. He also called on media organisations to avoid unverified reporting that could compromise operations or cause public alarm. Rabiu said the agencies and state government would continue their efforts to restore peace across the state.

title: EFCC Links Illegal Mining To Insecurity, Organised Crime, Vows To Target Financiers
summary: Nigeria’s EFCC says illegal mining can fuel insecurity and organised crime. It will target financiers and other beneficiaries, not only miners at extraction sites.
body:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has linked illegal mining and mineral theft to insecurity and organised crime in Nigeria. Chairman Ola Olukoyede said criminal networks exploit weaknesses in the sector, and warned that enforcement must target those financing and benefiting from illegal operations as well as miners at extraction sites.

Speaking at a public lecture and capacity-building workshop in Ilorin, Kwara State, Olukoyede said unregulated activity can create opportunities for extortion, smuggling, violence and territorial disputes. Proceeds from mineral theft may also finance other crimes, he said, making illegal mining more than a licensing issue.

The EFCC recorded 52 illegal mining cases between October 2023 and July 2026 and secured the forfeiture of 102 tonnes of solid minerals, Olukoyede said. He described investigations into networks involving local and international participants, with separate roles in financing operations, extracting and transporting minerals, arranging documentation and buying illegally obtained resources. The commission’s approach, he said, is to trace financial transactions and identify those who profit.

Olukoyede clarified that the EFCC does not regulate mining or issue licences. Its role is to investigate suspected corruption, fraud, money laundering, illicit financial flows and criminal proceeds. He warned that public officials who facilitate illegal mining, manipulate licences or launder proceeds would also face investigation.

He called for better coordination among mining regulators, financial intelligence institutions, law enforcement, customs and revenue agencies, saying fragmented information makes it harder to track criminal networks. He also urged host communities, traditional institutions, civil society and local leaders to report suspicious activity, and called on organised labour to advocate for lawful mining and decent working conditions. The EFCC, he said, will pursue financiers and facilitators, trace illicit proceeds, recover assets and prosecute suspects based on evidence.

title: Gambia Central Bank’s planned sack affects 57 Nigerians, NiDCOM kicks
summary: Nigeria’s diaspora commission says a Gambian central bank directive could affect 57 Nigerian bank workers. It urged the regulator to reconsider and consult stakeholders.
body:
Nigeria’s diaspora commission has opposed a Central Bank of The Gambia directive requiring banks to replace non-Gambian employees with Gambians. The commission’s chair and chief executive, Abike Dabiri-Erewa, said the measure could affect 57 Nigerian professionals. The directive, issued on September 16, gives banks until December 31, 2026, to make the changes.

The Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NIDCOM) said the affected Nigerians work at four Nigerian-owned banks and have valid residency and work permits. Dabiri-Erewa described the directive as deeply concerning, while acknowledging The Gambia’s right to promote employment for its citizens.

NIDCOM highlighted the banks’ role in the Gambian economy. It said they hold 37.2 per cent of total deposits, valued at GMD35.3 billion, and account for 32.6 per cent of loans, worth GMD7.67 billion. The banks also represent 37 per cent of industry assets, valued at GMD44.78 billion, and 34.5 per cent of investments in Central Bank bonds. The commission added that they provide 90 per cent of funding for the National Water and Electricity Company.

Dabiri-Erewa said employment policies should take account of existing contracts, valid work permits and ECOWAS protocols on free movement. She argued that removing qualified African professionals sits uneasily with efforts to encourage investment and regional cooperation across the continent.

NIDCOM called on the Gambian central bank to reverse the blanket directive and consult the Nigerian High Commission in Banjul and other stakeholders to reach an amicable resolution. It also urged Gambian authorities to uphold ECOWAS integration and the longstanding cordial relations between Nigeria and The Gambia.

title: Currency outside banks rises 104% in 3 yrs — CBN
summary: Currency held outside Nigeria’s banks reached N4.923 trillion in September 2026, up 103.8% in three years. Demand deposits rose 70.8%.
body:
Currency held outside Nigeria’s banking system rose 103.8 per cent over three years, reaching N4.923 trillion in September 2026 from N2.416 trillion in September 2023, according to Central Bank of Nigeria Money and Credit Statistics. The total was also 10.3 per cent higher than the N4.465 trillion recorded in September 2025.

The annual figures show currency outside banks increased by 66.2 per cent to N4.016 trillion in September 2024, then rose by 11.2 per cent to N4.465 trillion a year later. It climbed further to N4.923 trillion in September 2026. The continuing increase points to substantial demand for physical cash even as mobile banking, electronic transfers, point-of-sale terminals and other digital payment channels have expanded.

Demand deposits also grew over the period, rising 70.8 per cent to N39.124 trillion in September 2026 from N22.903 trillion in September 2023. They reached N31.842 trillion in September 2024, up 39 per cent from a year earlier, and N34.642 trillion in September 2025, an annual increase of 8.8 per cent. The latest figure represented a 12.9 per cent rise from September 2025. Demand deposits are funds in bank accounts generally accessible for payments and withdrawals on demand.

Economic and communications expert Clifford Egbomeade said the growth in both measures reflects the presence of formal bank balances alongside strong demand for cash in Nigeria’s payment system. He cautioned that the measures track different forms of monetary activity: demand deposits are account balances, while currency outside banks is cash held beyond the banking system. Their growth rates alone, he said, do not show whether higher cash holdings result from economic growth, inflation, informal transactions or changing payment preferences.

title: Leprosy mission partners Britain on tree planting
summary: The Leprosy Mission Nigeria and a British project partner planted 60 fruit and palm trees at a Minna leprosarium. Organisers said the effort supports climate resilience.
body:
The Leprosy Mission Nigeria (TLMN), working with a project partner from Great Britain, has planted 60 economic trees at a leprosarium in Minna, Niger State. The planting included 20 orange trees, 20 mango trees and 20 palm trees, according to the information provided by the mission.

Rev. Dr. Solomon Bityong, a TLMN project partner, said a healthy environment was essential to human survival and urged Nigerians to support similar efforts to address climate change. TLMN Minna Project Officer Habila Diko said the initiative was intended to bring environmental sustainability into the mission’s climate-smart agriculture and livelihood programmes.

Diko said the tree planting also formed part of The Leprosy Mission International’s broader commitment to promoting a clean and healthy environment. Community leader Bello Umar thanked the mission and said residents would care for and preserve the trees.

Hauwa Usman, an elderly community leader, said residents had often travelled to their farmlands to find shade during hot weather. She said the new trees could provide shade within their compounds as they grow.

title: APC Rally: Hard part of our economic reset over; next term is pure harvest – VP Shettima
summary: Vice President Kashim Shettima said the hardest phase of Nigeria’s economic reset is over, urging voters to renew the APC’s mandate in 2027. He cited Cross River projects.
body:
Vice President Kashim Shettima said the most difficult phase of the federal government’s economic reforms had passed, arguing that a second term under President Bola Tinubu would bring growth and tangible benefits to Nigerians. Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally in Calabar on Monday, he asked voters to renew the mandates of Tinubu and Shettima, and of Cross River Governor Bassey Otu and Deputy Governor Peter Odey, in the 2027 elections. Shettima said other parties lacked the capacity to change the economy’s direction, while also insisting that support for the government should not prevent citizens from questioning its performance.

He pointed to projects and proposals he said could support Cross River’s development. These included the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which he said would link coastal communities, ease transport, support tourism and attract investment. Shettima said the federal government had approved and backed the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port, describing it as a potential maritime gateway that could generate jobs and encourage industrial activity. He also said a proposal to locate the Gulf of Guinea Commission Secretariat in Calabar could bring diplomatic and commercial activity to the state.

Shettima said the federal government recognised Cross River’s coastal status and was prepared to help resolve a dispute over 46 oil wells. He linked a resolution to opportunities in maritime investment and the blue economy. On education, he cited the state’s participation in NELFUND education funding and said the initiative could ease pressure on parents and help young people continue their studies. He also referred to Project HOPE, describing its aims as improving foundational learning, teacher development, school management and access to education.

APC National Chairman Nentanwe Yilwatda and campaign council director general Abdulaziz Yari also called for support for Tinubu’s re-election. Otu praised the president’s leadership and said Cross River residents would back the APC ticket, pointing to policies in agriculture, education, industry and security. At a separate visit to the Obong of Calabar, Shettima paid homage to the traditional institution and outlined the party’s electoral aspirations. The Obong called for unity and peaceful coexistence, and praised the administration’s willingness to undertake difficult reforms.

title: [VIDEO] Tinubu’s Aide Refutes Claim President Visited Saudi Arabia To Get Northern Votes
summary: Ademola Oshodi said Tinubu’s Mecca visit was religious, not an effort to win northern support ahead of 2027. He cited Bauchi governor Bala Mohammed’s presence.
body:
Ademola Oshodi, Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Foreign Affairs and Protocol, has rejected claims that Tinubu travelled to Mecca to gain support among northerners before the 2027 general elections. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, Oshodi said the visit was strictly religious and reflected the President’s Muslim faith.

Oshodi pointed to the presence in Mecca of Bauchi State Governor Bala Mohammed, an opposition politician, saying he was there as a Muslim. The aide also urged other candidates in the 2027 presidential election to seek favour from God.

Tinubu arrived in Saudi Arabia on October 29 and performed the rites associated with Umrah. He said the purpose was to seek Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. After completing the rites, the President said he felt fulfilled and that God had granted him the wisdom to continue leading Nigerians.

Oshodi acknowledged that Nigerians are experiencing hardship, but said Tinubu is working to improve conditions. Tinubu is the All Progressives Congress presidential candidate for the 2027 elections.

title: Prosecutors seek retrial of mother accused of killing her three children
summary: Prosecutors plan to retry Lindsay Clancy after a jury deadlocked in her murder trial. The judge must first rule on a defense motion to dismiss.
body:
Prosecutors in Massachusetts say they intend to retry Lindsay Clancy, 36, after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict in her trial over the deaths of her three children. The deadlock resulted in a mistrial. Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague told the court that a retrial was planned but did not specify what charges Clancy would face.

The next step depends on a separate defense motion seeking dismissal of the charges. Judge William Sullivan is expected to rule at the next hearing, scheduled for November 16. He has set aside March 2027 as a possible retrial date if the case proceeds. Clancy’s lawyer, Kevin Reddington, indicated he would not oppose a retrial if the judge rejects the dismissal motion.

At trial, Clancy did not deny strangling Cora, five, Dawson, three, and Callan, eight months old, at the family home in Duxbury in January 2023. She pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, saying she heard a voice telling her to kill the children. Her lawyers argued that she was experiencing postpartum psychosis and therefore should not be held criminally responsible. Prosecutors disputed that account, arguing that the killings were planned and that Clancy understood the consequences of her actions.

The trial included more than 80 witnesses and drew attention to maternal mental health. The source material says medical experts estimate postpartum psychosis affects about one to two women in every 1,000 births. After the killings, Clancy cut her neck and wrists and jumped from a second-story window in what was described as an apparent suicide attempt. She was left paralyzed from the waist down and uses a wheelchair.

title: N1.3 billion worth of property saved from fire in Nasarawa
summary: Fire crews in Nasarawa say they saved N1.3bn in property across about 97 emergency calls since January. The incidents caused N800m in losses and one death.
body:
# N1.3 billion worth of property saved from fire in Nasarawa

Fire crews in Nasarawa State saved property valued at N1.3 billion during about 97 emergency calls received from January to the time of reporting, while assets worth N2.1 billion were exposed to fire hazards. The incidents caused estimated losses of N800 million and one death. Crews also rescued eight people from life-threatening situations, according to state Federal Fire Service Controller Eno Kelechi Nwachukwu.

Nwachukwu gave the figures at the launch of the 2026 National Fire Week Awareness Campaign at the Federal Secretariat in Lafia on Monday. The campaign’s theme is “Building a Fire Resilient Nigeria: One Community at a Time.” She called for a shift from responding to fires after they break out towards prevention led by communities, and said fire safety requires participation from government, businesses, institutions, families and individuals.

The Federal Fire Service plans to intensify public education on safe handling and storage of cooking gas, preventing illegal or improper electrical connections, avoiding indiscriminate refuse burning, and safely storing petroleum products and other combustible materials. Nwachukwu urged residents, business owners and market associations to take precautions and report emergencies promptly. Abigail Waya, head of the state civil service, was represented at the event by Belinda Oyigbenu Atinuke, who called for cooperation between federal and state fire services on information-sharing and emergency response. She also urged residents to switch off unused appliances and report fires before they spread.

In a keynote address, Abubakar Alhasan of the Federal University of Lafia’s Department of Geography and Environmental Management said electrical surges and overloaded cables accounted for 70 per cent of fire incidents, according to his assessment. Citing 2025 reports, he said 693 residential houses, 190 markets and 105 other premises were affected; he added that markets recorded the most deaths, with about 39. He also identified hazards including unsafe fuel storage, smoking, bush burning, gas-related fires and vehicle incidents, and cautioned against hiring unqualified electricians. The event included sessions on fire experiences and prevention, as well as awards recognising contributions to fire response and support for the service.

title: Adebutu Allays Supporters’ Fear Over Omission From INEC List For Ogun Gov Election
summary: Ladi Adebutu called his omission from INEC’s 2027 Ogun governorship candidate list a temporary setback. He urged supporters to stay focused.
body:
Peoples Democratic Party governorship candidate Ladi Adebutu has described his omission from the Independent National Electoral Commission’s list of candidates for the 2027 Ogun election as a temporary setback. Speaking in Abeokuta, he urged supporters and political associates not to lose confidence or be distracted as the party prepares for the election.

Adebutu was addressing an event at the PDP secretariat where defectors from the ruling All Progressives Congress and other parties were received. He said he had been a PDP member for 20 years and had stood as the party’s candidate in five consecutive election cycles. He also cited his involvement in organising and financing party registration in the state, saying he had registered as a member.

He questioned the basis for leaving his name off the list and said he had not left the PDP. Adebutu argued that participation in the party’s primaries was evidence of his membership, and said all Nigerians were entitled to take part in the democratic process. He accused political opponents of trying to slow his campaign and unsettle voters, but did not provide details of the process behind INEC’s omission.

Adebutu said the issue had slowed the party’s activities but would not stop them. He reported that his team had visited 12 of Ogun’s 20 local government areas and 140 of its 236 wards, with further visits planned. He said the campaign would continue and expressed confidence that he and the PDP would win.

title: INEC to ensure PWDs aren’t excluded from 2027 elections — Official
summary: INEC says it is strengthening accessibility measures ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 elections. A Gombe workshop focused on practical steps to reach voters with disabilities.
body:
The Independent National Electoral Commission says it is working to reduce physical, communication and procedural barriers that can prevent persons with disabilities from taking part in the 2027 general elections. Umar Gajiram, the Resident Electoral Commissioner in Gombe State, outlined the commitment through Administrative Secretary Fadimatu Bakari at a sensitisation workshop in Gombe on disability inclusion and electoral access.

Gajiram said electoral participation is a right for every Nigerian, regardless of disability. He pointed to measures including assistive materials, improved access at polling units, training for election officials and cooperation with disability organisations. He stressed that these steps must be properly communicated and used, and urged officials to consider disability access throughout their work. He also called on the commission’s Disability Desk Officer to stay in contact with disability groups and relay their concerns.

Bukar Maikwada, an assistant director for youth at INEC headquarters, said the workshop was intended to improve stakeholders’ understanding of inclusion and support the effective deployment of existing interventions. These include Braille ballot guides, written-instruction posters for deaf voters, magnifying glasses for people with visual impairment and albinism, and voter information in formats such as Braille, jingles, flyers and posters. Training, he said, would help officials decide where and when to provide the materials.

Maikwada said the commission’s work is guided by Section 54 of the Electoral Act, 2026, the Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act, 2018, and INEC’s framework on access and participation in elections. He called for coordination among election officials, disability organisations and their local clusters, including for voter education and mobilisation.

The workshop was also expected to help participants review previous elections, identify gaps and propose practical steps for national, state, local-government and grassroots implementation. Both officials emphasised that inclusion depends not only on making assistance available, but also on its effective delivery, communication and monitoring.

title: Nigerians, others to face 10-yr wait for UK permanent residency
summary: Most migrants, including many Nigerians, will face a 10-year wait for UK settlement under revised plans due next year. Care workers retain a five-year route.
body:
The UK government has revised its proposed immigration reforms, keeping plans to extend the standard wait for permanent settlement from five years to 10. The changes are expected to take effect next year and will also apply to migrants already living and working in Britain. Permanent settlement is formally known as indefinite leave to remain.

Hundreds of thousands of care workers will be exempt from the longer wait and retain a five-year route, subject to eligibility requirements. The concession is relevant to Nigerians employed in Britain’s health and social care sector, which relies on overseas workers to help fill staffing shortages.

The government initially proposed that lower-skilled foreign workers wait between 10 and 15 years before qualifying. The revised plans followed opposition from trade unions and Labour Party members, who raised concerns about the effects on low-paid foreign workers, particularly in care jobs.

Under the new arrangements, migrants earning at least £50,271 a year and certain skilled public-sector workers can apply after five years. Those earning more than £125,000 may qualify after three years. Refugees who entered Britain illegally, including people who arrived by small boats, could face substantially longer waits, potentially lasting decades. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the policy was intended to reward contributions to society while setting tougher conditions for people who break immigration rules.

The government estimates the reforms will reduce by 500,000 the number of migrants who arrived from 2021 and would otherwise have qualified for settlement by 2030. It still expects as many as 1.4 million migrants to qualify by then under the revised arrangements.

title: Alleged Terrorism Financing: Court Fixes Jan 2027 For Judgment In Case Against Mamu
summary: A Federal High Court in Abuja will deliver judgment on Jan. 27, 2027, in the terrorism-financing case against Tukur Mamu. Lawyers presented final arguments.
body:
A Federal High Court in Abuja has set January 27, 2027, for judgment in the Federal Government’s case against Tukur Mamu, who is accused of financing terrorism. Justice Mohammed Umar fixed the date after lawyers for both sides adopted their final written addresses and presented their arguments.

Mamu was initially charged with 10 counts related to terrorism financing. The prosecution later amended the charges to include additional alleged offences, including possession of firearms without a valid licence and money laundering. Mamu was arrested by Egyptian security officials at Cairo International Airport on September 7, 2022.

At the hearing, defence counsel Johnson Usman argued that the prosecution had not produced in court the licence for a rifle allegedly recovered from Mamu’s residence. He said the defence had requested the licence on three occasions and maintained that it was not expired when Mamu was arrested. Usman said the prosecution’s failure to produce it raised doubts and urged the court to resolve the matter in his client’s favour.

Federal Government lawyer David Kaswe disputed that account, saying the rifle and its licence had already been tendered as evidence. He also recalled that the court had approved the prosecution’s request to keep the rifle and other exhibits in a secure place. Kaswe adopted the government’s final written address, dated September 18 and filed on September 21.

Usman also thanked the Department of State Services for allowing Mamu’s family to see him in accordance with a court order. After hearing both sides, Justice Umar set the date for judgment.

title: Nasarawa SDP governorship candidate gifts 163 women leaders cars, cash, equipment
summary: SDP candidate Muhammad Adamu distributed vehicles, cash and equipment to women leaders across Nasarawa State. The programme was held on 31 October ahead of the 2027 election.
body:
Muhammad Adamu, the Social Democratic Party’s governorship candidate in Nasarawa State, has distributed vehicles, cash and household equipment to women leaders across the state. The programme, held on 31 October, covered leaders from all 13 local government areas and 147 electoral wards, according to his campaign. Adamu is seeking the governorship in the 2027 general election.

The campaign said the beneficiaries received cars, refrigerators, grinding machines, generators, solar-powered fans and cash. Adamu also confirmed the exercise in a post on his official Facebook page, describing it as an effort to support women’s economic empowerment and strengthen grassroots participation.

Each of the 13 local government women leaders received a Sharon car, a solar-powered fan and N200,000, the campaign said. The three zonal women leaders also received cars and solar-powered fans. The statement gave conflicting figures for the cash allocated to those leaders, so their individual amounts were not clear. The 147 ward women leaders received a refrigerator, grinding machine, generator, solar-powered table fan and N100,000 each. The campaign said the total cash distributed to ward leaders was N14.7 million.

The campaign presented the initiative as part of Adamu’s efforts to increase women’s political participation and economic independence. His recent community activities have also included commissioning two solar-powered boreholes in Keffi, at Angwan Lambu Phase II and near the High Court. Adamu said the projects were sponsored by his wife, Rukayya Adamu, to help meet water needs among Nasarawa State University students and residents of surrounding communities.

title: You Cannot Negotiate For TUC, Osifo Replies Ajearo As N70,000 Controversy Drags On
summary: Festus Osifo says the TUC was excluded from talks on a N70,000 transport allowance. He disputes the NLC’s authority to negotiate for other unions.
body:
Trade Union of Nigeria (TUC) President Festus Osifo has challenged Nigerian Labour Congress (NLC) President Joe Ajaero over who can negotiate workers’ pay and allowances with the Federal Government. The dispute follows an agreement on a N70,000 transportation allowance approved by President Bola Tinubu. Osifo said the TUC was not included in the negotiations and called the agreement an aberration.

Speaking on Monday, Osifo argued that neither union should negotiate on behalf of the other without its participation or consultation. He said the TUC and NLC must come together for negotiations, while acknowledging that the NLC has more affiliate unions. Osifo challenged Ajaero to produce an International Labour Organization regulation authorising one body to negotiate without the other.

Osifo also disputed Ajaero’s reliance on the Joint Public Sector Negotiating Council (JNC), saying the meeting that produced the allowance agreement was not a JNC meeting. He said the council has membership and quorum requirements, and that its members were not present. Osifo added that the labour minister and Ajaero were not council members.

He said the JNC should consider consequential adjustments after changes to the minimum wage. Osifo criticised the use of a questionnaire asking the council to apply N40,000 across the board—the difference between the previous N30,000 minimum wage and the new N70,000 figure. He said he had raised his objection directly with Ajaero, arguing that the approach had left federal workers earning very low salaries.

title: Sowore releases video of alleged attackers, alleges erased CCTV footage in Ekiti
summary: Omoyele Sowore released a video he says shows people involved in an attack on his team in Ado-Ekiti. He alleges restaurant CCTV was erased; police described the incident as an altercation.
body:
Omoyele Sowore has released a video that he says shows individuals involved in an attack on his team in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, on 30 October. The African Action Congress presidential candidate described the footage as a breakthrough but called for an independent investigation to establish who the people shown are and what roles they played.

The video appears to show men carrying cutlasses and sticks during a confrontation, while a person in a black suit is dragged. Bystanders can also be seen. The footage has not, in the supplied account, been independently verified as showing the people responsible for the incident.

Sowore also alleged that surveillance recordings from Tawakalitu Restaurant, where the incident occurred, were erased after police and State Security Service (SSS), also known as the Department of State Services (DSS), operatives took possession of the CCTV equipment. He said the equipment was returned to the restaurant without recordings. According to Sowore, restaurant management confirmed its return but declined to identify the officer who brought it back. He called on the police and SSS to release the footage and accused police officials of mishandling the investigation.

The allegations follow Sowore’s claim that suspected political thugs attacked him and members of his team. The Ekiti State Police Command described the event as an altercation at a restaurant. It said officers responded to information about the incident, rescued Sowore, who sustained minor injuries, and that the Commissioner of Police, Michael Falade, ordered a discreet investigation to establish what happened and identify those responsible.

Sowore said he had asked Falade, Ado-Ekiti Central Divisional Police Officer Mustapha Mohammed and the Rapid Response Squad commander for an update. He claimed they told him there was no complainant because he had not provided a written statement. Sowore challenged that explanation, saying police had intervened and, according to him, arrested suspects and recovered weapons, phones and other devices. He also called for the removal of the state Commissioner of Police and other officers he accused of mishandling the case.

title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest Formula One world champion at age 20
summary: Kimi Antonelli clinched the Formula One world championship with third place at the Mexico Grand Prix. At 20, he is the sport’s youngest champion.
body:
Kimi Antonelli secured the Formula One world championship by finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix, becoming the youngest driver to win the title. The Mercedes driver was 20 years and 68 days old when he clinched the crown.

Max Verstappen won the race, but Antonelli’s podium finish was enough to settle the championship. Antonelli’s achievement puts him more than three years ahead of Sebastian Vettel’s age when Vettel became champion in 2010.

Antonelli is also the first Italian to win the Formula One title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

title: Tinubu’s 2023 Electricity Pledge Taken Out Of Context, Says APC Campaign Council
summary: The APC campaign council says Tinubu’s 2023 electricity pledge was taken out of context. It cited metering, debt and grid initiatives as progress.
body:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has defended President Bola Tinubu’s 2023 promise to end estimated electricity billing and provide stable supply, saying recent commentary omitted part of his remarks. In a statement on Sunday, council spokesperson Dele Alake said Tinubu made the pledge while addressing members of the Organised Private Sector in Lagos before the general election.

Alake recalled Tinubu saying that people would have electricity and would no longer pay estimated bills. The candidate also said voters should not support him for a second term if he failed to keep the promise, unless he gave adequate reasons for not delivering. Alake argued that some accounts had left out that qualification, and said the pledge should be considered alongside actions taken by the administration since it assumed office in 2023.

Among those actions, Alake cited Tinubu’s signing of the Electricity Act 2023 on June 9, which he said opened electricity generation, transmission and distribution to state governments. He named Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger as states that have established electricity regulatory agencies. He also said the Presidential Metering Initiative was launched to tackle a backlog of more than seven million unmetered customers, with over 1.5 million metered under the programme in the last three years.

Alake said the government was addressing more than ₦6 trillion in legacy debts accumulated between 2015 and 2025 through a ₦4 trillion bond programme. Its first two tranches, he said, raised more than ₦1.2 trillion towards verified obligations to 21 generation companies and gas suppliers. He also pointed to investments in substations, grid expansion and renewable energy, including plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre and build an East-West super grid. The government has also adjusted tariffs towards cost-reflective levels, while putting measures in place to protect low-income households, he said.

Alake acknowledged that resolving the power sector crisis remained ongoing. He said Tinubu would present his record in the sector and explain what remained to be done as he sought a second term.

title: Toluwanisings’ death and social media prosecutors, By Festus Adedayo
summary: Gospel musician Toluwanisings, 34, died after collapsing at his Ibadan home on 14 October. Reports of delayed hospital care and a family burial dispute drew online scrutiny.
body:
Gospel musician Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, known as Toluwanisings, died on 14 October after collapsing on the staircase of his home in Ibadan, Oyo State. The 34-year-old had recently returned from a worship concert titled In His Presence. His death prompted public concern about the emergency care he received and a dispute over his burial arrangements.

Accounts described in the commentary say he was taken to about seven or eight hospitals in Ibadan, including the University College Hospital, but was either turned away or faced administrative obstacles. The commentary presents his experience as an example of wider concerns about emergency treatment in Nigeria, including allegations that hospitals delay or refuse care. It argues that the focus on the musician’s personal life after his death diverted attention from questions about access to urgent medical help.

The debate also widened into a disagreement over where Toluwanisings should be buried. His widow was said to favour a quiet burial in a modern cemetery, while his father and other relatives reportedly wanted him buried at his newly completed home in Ibadan or beside his late mother in Ikirun, Osun State. The dispute unfolded publicly on social media, alongside claims about his relationship with his family and how he used his money. The account also notes that he left a wife and two young daughters.

The commentary compares the public scrutiny after Toluwanisings’ death with the controversy surrounding singer Mohbad, who died in 2023. In both cases, it says, disputes involving relatives and the handling of the deceased’s remains became prominent in public discussion. It calls for attention to the circumstances of Toluwanisings’ death and criticises the online airing of family conflict, while raising broader questions about emergency hospital care and the treatment of a person’s memory after death.

title: Movie director Michael Mann accidentally shoots self
summary: Director Michael Mann suffered a superficial injury when a gun accidentally discharged at a Los Angeles range. Police said the incident was accidental.
body:
Film director Michael Mann suffered a superficial injury after a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered at a Los Angeles gun range on Saturday, according to a statement from his representative. Mann was treated and was being released, the statement said.

The Los Angeles Police Department said officers responded to a “shots fired” incident at about 4:00 p.m. local time. The shooting was determined to be accidental. Mann is 83 and is described as an experienced target shooter.

Mann is known for films including “Thief,” “The Last of the Mohicans,” “Public Enemies,” “The Insider” and “Ali.” He is perhaps best known for “Heat,” the crime thriller starring Robert De Niro as a master criminal and Al Pacino as a police officer. Its final scene follows the two characters, both armed, near an airport runway.

title: CAF picks Nigeria’s Samson Adamu as new General Secretary
summary: CAF has appointed Nigerian Samson Adamu as its General Secretary after a competitive recruitment process. He had served in an acting capacity since March.
body:
The Confederation of African Football has appointed Nigerian Samson Adamu as its General Secretary following a recruitment process that included advertising the role and interviewing several candidates. CAF announced the appointment on Sunday.

Adamu had been serving as acting General Secretary since March, after Veron Mosengo-Omba resigned. Mosengo-Omba later became president of the football federation in the Democratic Republic of Congo. CAF President Patrice Motsepe said the appointment followed a competitive selection process.

Adamu has worked at CAF for eight years. He joined in 2018 as Director of Competitions and later became Director of Tournaments and Events. In those roles, he contributed to the delivery of major continental competitions, including the Africa Cup of Nations. He is also a graduate of the FIFA Master programme in International Management, Law and Humanities of Sport.

In his new position, Adamu is expected to oversee CAF’s day-to-day administration and support the organisation’s strategic priorities. He is the son of Amos Adamu, a former Director of Sports in Nigeria’s then Ministry of Sports and a former FIFA Executive Committee member.

Adamu joins a succession of CAF General Secretaries that has included three members of Egypt’s Fahmy family. Mourad Fahmy held the post from 1961 to 1982, followed by his son Mustapha Fahmy from 1982 to 2010. Amr Fahmy, Mourad’s grandson, served from 2017 to 2019.

title: Decoupling Sovereignty Index (5): How decoupling reinforces itself, By Max Amuchie
summary: The DSI’s Convergence Indicator examines whether weaknesses across money, land and public authority reinforce one another. It also defines a possible Event Horizon.
body:
The Decoupling Sovereignty Index (DSI) uses its Convergence Indicator to examine whether separate weaknesses in state authority are beginning to reinforce one another. The framework distinguishes a territory with several serious but contained problems from one where conditions across its Money, Land and Mind vectors combine to sustain an alternative order. Multiple high indicator scores alone are not enough to establish that such a system has formed; analysts must identify how the conditions interact and support that assessment with evidence and explicit rules.

The source describes a possible cycle in which an armed organisation’s economic extraction finances recruitment, weapons and territorial expansion. Control of territory can then allow the group to regulate movement, influence production and impose rules, creating further opportunities to extract resources. Residents’ compliance may reflect fear, dependence or a lack of alternatives rather than voluntary support, but it can still help the organisation maintain control. In this account, economic power, territorial authority and effects on public behaviour can reinforce one another.

The DSI calls a critical condition in which a Shadow Order is resilient and embedded enough to resist reversal through ordinary state intervention an Event Horizon. This is presented as an analytical concept, not a fixed threshold that applies identically everywhere. It does not mean recovery is impossible, nor does durability demonstrate popular legitimacy: coercion, economic dependence and the absence of credible alternatives may help sustain an order. The framework argues that addressing one symptom at a time may be inadequate when the underlying relationships remain intact.

Two designated indicator combinations illustrate the approach. M6 and L6 are associated with agricultural sovereignty collapse, where economic pressures and territorial insecurity can disrupt farming, transport and livelihoods. L7, L3 and MD5 are identified as a signal of human sovereignty collapse: conditions that constrain people’s ability to move, sustain ordinary life and exercise agency. The latter concerns people’s practical circumstances and does not replace or negate the state’s legal sovereignty. In both cases, the DSI’s focus is on the interaction among conditions, not simply on whether a particular problem exists.

title: Masussuka’s killing highlights Nigeria’s extremism, terrorism problem
summary: The killing of cleric Yahaya Masussuka has renewed concern over religious hostility and extremist rhetoric in Nigeria. Ansaru claimed responsibility; no evidence links Izala.
body:
Islamic cleric Yahaya Masussuka was shot dead outside his home in Katsina State on the evening of 26 October. His friend, Adamu Abubakar, was also killed. Police said two people on a motorcycle carried out the attack. Ansaru, a breakaway faction of Boko Haram, later claimed responsibility, saying it targeted Masussuka over his rejection of hadiths and support for peaceful coexistence among people of different faiths. The claim has not been independently established in the supplied material.

Some of Masussuka’s supporters initially blamed scholars from rival religious movements, citing earlier threats and online disputes. But there is no established evidence connecting those groups or the Izala movement to the killing. Some Izala scholars have rejected the accusations. Masussuka’s teachings, described as “Quran-only,” drew opposition, though he said he rejected only hadiths he believed contradicted the Quran or justified violence. Amnesty International Nigeria condemned the killing and called for an investigation; President Bola Tinubu also condemned it and directed security agencies to investigate.

The reaction to the killing has drawn attention to how theological disputes can become a source of hostility. In research on Muslim identities and conflict in northern Nigeria, the late academic Abdul Mustapha examined how rival claims to religious authenticity have intensified divisions and, at times, violence. The practice of declaring another Muslim an unbeliever, known as takfirism, has also been used by violent Sunni jihadists to portray religious opponents as illegitimate. Ibrahim Makari, an imam at the National Mosque in Abuja, warned that declaring someone an unbeliever can be a “gate to assassination.”

Religious intimidation is not confined to Muslim communities or northern Nigeria. In 2022, Christian student Deborah Samuel was killed by fellow students after being accused of blasphemy, and Christian Rhoda Jatau was later arrested and charged after sharing a message condemning the killing. Traditional religious practitioners have also reported threats and discrimination. In Delta State, a court ruled that the harassment of traditional worshippers was unconstitutional after a shrine and artefacts were destroyed in 2024.

Auwal Rafsanjani of the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre said extremist ideas that promote hatred and justify violence can create a path to terrorism, while noting that not all extremists are terrorists. He called for religious and traditional leaders to counter extremist narratives and protect young people from recruitment. He also said governments should distinguish criminal violence from peaceful religious belief and lawful dissent, and not use counterterrorism as a pretext for persecution or restrictions on fundamental freedoms.

title: Meet the CEOs leading Nigeria’s seven listed oil and gas companies
summary: Seven companies on the Nigerian Exchange have a combined market value of about N16.7 trillion. Their leaders bring experience in engineering, law, finance and operations.
body:
Nigeria’s seven listed oil and gas companies have a combined market capitalisation of about N16.7 trillion, with executives steering businesses across exploration, production, refining, distribution and related services. Their leaders have varied career paths, from engineering and corporate law to banking and marketing, as indigenous firms take a larger role in the sector.

At Seplat Energy, Engr. Effiong Okon became chief executive on August 1, 2026, bringing more than 35 years of energy-sector experience, including senior roles at Shell. Seplat has reported an estimated 157 billion cubic feet of gas and 19 million barrels of oil in place at its Aku-01 exploration well. Adegbite Falade, a former Shell and Oando executive, has led Aradel Holdings since 2021. The company reported a 154.3% rise in profit before tax to N764.71 billion for the nine months to September 2026, alongside revenue of N3.95 trillion.

Oando Plc is led by Wale Tinubu, whose background is in law and petroleum law. He co-founded Ocean and Oil Limited in 1994; the group adopted the Oando name in 2003 and expanded across the oil and gas value chain. Wilfried Konde leads Total Nigeria Plc after a career in audit, finance and corporate affairs at TotalEnergies across several countries. The company, listed on the Nigerian Exchange in 1979, recorded pre-tax profit of N8.02 billion in the nine months to September 2026.
