Ikechukwu Emmanuel Oraekwuotu, whose career spans banking and financial services, leads Conoil Plc. He joined its board in 2014 and later assumed its acting leadership role.

At Eterna Plc, Jude Nwaulune became managing director and chief executive in May 2026 after roles in retail operations and logistics. The company reported revenue of N365.56 billion for the nine months to September 2026, up from N212.84 billion in the same period a year earlier. Henry Alakhume took over as acting group managing director of Japaul Gold & Ventures in February 2026, following Akinloye Daniel Oladapo’s resignation. Alakhume had been the company’s chief operating officer. Japaul reported profit before tax of N1.50 billion for the nine months to September 2026, a 202.3% increase on the corresponding period of 2025.

title: U-17 WWC: Five key players to watch as Flamingos face Venezuela in quarterfinal
summary: Nigeria face Venezuela for a place in the U-17 Women’s World Cup semi-finals. Umejiaku, Adegbuyi, Bravo, Suárez and Ijirigho could shape the contest.
body:
Nigeria’s Flamingos meet Venezuela in the quarterfinal of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, with a place in the semi-finals at stake. After losing their opening match to Poland, Akeem Busari’s side recovered with wins over Puerto Rico, defending champions DPR Korea and Mexico. Venezuela also arrive with momentum after beating Germany 1-0 in the round of 16.

Nigeria forward Umejiaku has scored against Poland, DPR Korea and Mexico, and assisted Precious Oscar’s stoppage-time goal in the 2-0 win over Puerto Rico. Her movement and ability to create chances could help Nigeria break down a Venezuelan defence that held Germany scoreless. Adegbuyi offers another threat: she scored against Puerto Rico and opened the scoring in Nigeria’s 3-1 victory over DPR Korea.

Venezuela’s Diana Bravo scored the fifth-minute goal that eliminated Germany, who had won all three of their group matches. The early strike helped her team settle into a disciplined defensive performance. Nigeria will also need to track Suárez, who scored a stoppage-time winner in Venezuela’s 3-2 group-stage victory over Zambia. Her goal showed she can make the most of an opportunity late in a close match.

Goalkeeper Jane Ijirigho was important to Nigeria’s 2-1 round-of-16 win over Mexico. She saved an effort from captain Citlalli Reyes and tipped Kemberly Garcia’s long-range shot onto the crossbar. The 1.92-metre goalkeeper has been identified by FIFA as the tournament’s tallest player. Nigeria will need her reach and composure if Venezuela create chances, but progress will also depend on the whole team: the Flamingos must be patient in attack, organised at the back and alert throughout the match.

title: Photos: Sanwo-Olu walks runway alongside models at Lagos Fashion Week
summary: Lagos Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu joined models on the runway at Lagos Fashion Week in an outfit by designer Ugo Monye. The event runs through Sunday.
body:
Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu made a surprise appearance on the runway at the 2026 Lagos Fashion Week, walking alongside models in an ensemble by Nigerian designer Ugo Monye. The governor said he had stepped away from his usual governance work to support Monye and the event’s role in promoting fashion, creativity and culture in Lagos.

Sanwo-Olu wore regal off-white attire combining a traditional caftan with a kimono-inspired design, paired with a beige fedora. He drew applause as he walked across the runway, giving peace signs and nodding to spectators.

This year’s event, themed “CRAFTED: Heritage”, began last Wednesday at the Federal Palace Hotel in Lagos and is scheduled to conclude on Sunday. The annual gathering brings together designers, models, industry professionals and fashion enthusiasts to celebrate African creativity, craftsmanship and heritage.

title: Lagos Real Estate: Goania Project MD reveals costs developers underestimate
summary: Lagos developers may underestimate title, approval, infrastructure and community costs, says Goania Project MD Godfrey C. Aniebo. He also calls for better-planned, affordable housing.
body:
Property developers in Lagos can overlook major costs before construction and sales begin, according to Tpl. Godfrey C. Aniebo, Managing Director and Co-founder of Goania Project Limited, a town planning consultancy. He says thorough preparation is essential in a market shaped by complex land arrangements, rising development expenses and growing housing demand.

One early risk is land-title verification. Developers need to budget for processes such as excision, Certificates of Occupancy, e-GIS searches and title validation; buying unverified family land can lead to costly disputes. Planning approvals also involve expenses for EPPPS submissions, professional services, environmental assessments, drainage studies and traffic impact assessments. Delays or costs that are not included in budgets from the outset can create pressure later.

Site conditions and relationships with host communities can add further costs. In areas such as Ibeju-Lekki, sand-filling and drainage require particular attention, while unresolved community obligations or informal demands can lead to disputes. Aniebo also points to penalties for breaches of planning, environmental and building rules, inflation in materials, diesel and labour, and post-sale responsibilities involving buyer disputes, documentation and estate management. He recommends checking titles, approvals, infrastructure budgets and community agreements before marketing or sales begin.

Aniebo argues that Lagos needs more properly planned, affordable housing, not simply more homes. He says developments should include functional smaller apartments for a wider range of incomes, while streamlined approvals, shared infrastructure, locally sourced materials and faster construction methods could help manage costs. Secure titles and affordable mortgage financing are also important to access to housing.

He further stresses that new developments should be planned as complete neighbourhoods, with transport links, drainage, utilities and community facilities considered alongside housing. In high-demand areas, he warns, increasing density without matching infrastructure can affect residents’ quality of life. He calls for area-based planning, stronger development control and protection of drainage corridors, wetlands and green space, arguing that development costs and urban impacts need to be addressed before projects proceed.

title: DEZNY’s journey from school performances to AMVCA
summary: Digital creator DEZNY has earned a 2026 AMVCA nomination after years of building his craft, from school performances to online storytelling.
body:
Digital content creator Destiny Osarewinda, known as DEZNY, has been nominated for Best Digital Content Creator at the 2026 Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. The recognition follows years of developing work for online audiences, where he has built a following of more than two million across social media platforms.

DEZNY’s interest in performance began with church and school productions. Since around 2015, he has taken on different parts of content production, including writing, filming and editing. During secondary school, he established YEC TV to give young people opportunities to explore acting, music and dance. The initiative also gave him experience organising creative activities and collaborating with performers.

He later expanded his work to YouTube and other social platforms, developing stories around relatable situations. One example is Marriage List, which took more than a month of preparation before filming. DEZNY wrote the story in full and researched cultural elements featured in it, including Umu’Ada and traditional beads, asking questions to learn about practices he did not know well.

His creative interests also include music: he plays instruments and has taken part in choirs. Those experiences have informed his use of rhythm and emotional expression in storytelling. His background also includes military school training.

The nomination reflects growing recognition of digital creators in African entertainment. Social platforms have enabled independent storytellers to reach audiences beyond conventional film and television. For DEZNY, the recognition follows a gradual progression from early performances and youth-focused creative work to a substantial online audience, built through continued production and experimentation.

title: Financial Impact Of Funds Stolen Will Be Fully Covered, Says Binance
summary: Binance says it has bought tokens to replace 90% of the $6.3 billion stolen in a hack and set aside over $6.34 billion to cover losses. Withdrawals may resume Sunday.
body:
Binance said Saturday it had used company funds to buy tokens to replace 90 per cent of the $6.3 billion stolen in a major hacking attack. The cryptocurrency platform said its commitment was to cover the full financial impact of the theft and that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds for that purpose.

The remaining 10 per cent of tokens may take longer to source, Binance said, because they are less liquid and may not be available in the required amounts. The company described the incident on Friday as a complex attack involving several points of breach.

Investigators have pointed to hackers linked to North Korea as responsible for the attack. Prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell after news of the cyberattack. Binance suspended user withdrawals following the incident, but said in its latest update that they were on track to resume Sunday.

The incident has unfolded amid wider concerns expressed by observers about whether increasingly capable artificial intelligence models could threaten cryptography and information-technology security protocols. U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday that the United States was looking into the hack. The FBI said it was working with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity and was prepared to investigate.
