title: CIBN honours 755 leaders at fellowship investiture
summary: CIBN is set to honour 755 leaders and professionals at its 2026 Fellowship Investiture in Lagos. The programme includes three categories of awards.
body:
The Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) is set to honour 755 leaders and professionals at its 2026 Fellowship Investiture in Lagos tomorrow. The awardees come from banking, government, the private sector and academia. The Institute says the honours recognise contributions to banking, the economy, and the promotion of ethics and professionalism.

The programme will include 18 honorary fellowships, the election of 460 Associates as Fellows, and the induction of 277 senior management staff from banks and academics as Honorary Senior Members. Among those named for recognition are Lagos State Deputy Chief of Staff Sam Egube; Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation Managing Director and Chief Executive Thompson Oludare Sunday; and Bank of Sierra Leone Governor Ibrahim Stevens.

Other awardees include Famfa Oil Limited Vice Chairman Folorunsho Alakija, Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria Managing Director and Chief Executive Olubunmi Kuku, Dangote Cement Plc Chairman Emmanuel Ikazoboh, and Quest Merchant Bank Managing Director and Chief Executive Afolabi Olorode. Ogun State Secretary to the Government Tokunbo Talabi and Summit Bank Limited Managing Director and Chief Executive Siraju Salisu are also listed.

The keynote address, titled “Bank Recapitalisation: Leveraging New Bank Capital for Nigeria’s Industrial Transformation,” will be delivered by Nigerian Economic Summit Group Chief Executive Tayo Aduloju. Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning Doris Uzoka-Anite are expected to attend as special guests of honour.

title: Osimhen welcomes second child with partner Stefanie
summary: Victor Osimhen and partner Stefanie Kim Ladewig have welcomed their second child, a daughter named Liora Audrey. Galatasaray announced the birth.
body:
Nigeria and Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen and his partner, Stefanie Kim Ladewig, have welcomed their second child, a daughter named Liora Audrey. The Turkish club announced the birth and congratulated the couple, wishing the newborn a long, healthy and happy life.

The announcement came about two weeks after Ladewig, a model, escaped injury in a three-vehicle crash in Istanbul while eight months pregnant. The accident occurred on 13 October in the Mithatpasa neighbourhood of Kemerburgaz, in the city’s Eyupsultan district.

Reports said Ladewig was driving an SUV when it collided with a light commercial vehicle and then veered into another SUV travelling in the opposite direction. The vehicles were damaged, but no injuries were reported. Ladewig was taken to a private hospital in the Maslak area for precautionary checks because of her pregnancy and was later discharged.

Osimhen, 27, is a member of Nigeria’s Super Eagles and plays for Galatasaray in the Turkish Süper Lig. The birth adds to his family life as he continues his professional football career in Türkiye.

title: LASCOPA takes action against Ikeja Electric, resolves 528 consumer complaints
summary: LASCOPA says it resolved 528 of 556 complaints against Ikeja Electric from January to September 2026. Refunds and credit adjustments totalled N26.24 million.
body:
The Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency says it resolved 528 of 556 complaints against Ikeja Electric Distribution Company between January and September 2026. The agency’s latest update puts the resolution rate at about 95%, with 28 complaints still ongoing. It also says its interventions secured credit adjustments and refunds totalling N26,243,758.75 for affected consumers.

LASCOPA General Manager and Chief Executive Officer Afolabi Solebo said the agency was committed to fairness, accountability, transparency and improved service delivery in the electricity distribution sector. The agency said its mediation work is intended to help consumers obtain redress and encourage electricity providers to respond to grievances.

Yusuf Musiliu, head of the agency’s Complaints and Mediation Department, said LASCOPA receives and analyses complaints submitted through online and offline channels. Its monthly stakeholders’ parley with Ikeja Electric gives company representatives and affected consumers a regular forum to discuss unresolved cases and seek mutually acceptable agreements. The meetings take place on the last Thursday of each month, according to the agency.

LASCOPA advised consumers to use established complaint procedures rather than resort to self-help. It urged residents raising concerns about estimated bills, excessive charges, overbilling, electricity supply or other service practices to submit supporting evidence, such as bills and payment receipts, to assist investigations and speed up resolution. The agency said its consumer-protection work is carried out under the Lagos State Consumer Protection Law 2025, as amended, and encouraged residents to report grievances promptly.

title: Beyond the battlefield: Crisis communication as a national security imperative, By Mukhtar Ya’u Madobi
summary: A Kaduna symposium urged coordinated crisis messaging to counter deepfakes and disinformation. Participants also called for safeguards for public trust and fundamental rights.
body:
More than 150 representatives of security agencies, emergency services, government, academia and the media gathered in Kaduna for the Second National Symposium on Crisis Communication. Organised by the Centre for Crisis Communication on 27 and 28 October, the event focused on inter-agency cooperation, public trust and cyber threats. Participants argued that coordination between institutions must extend beyond operations to the information they release during emergencies.

Centre chairman Major General Chris Olukolade (rtd) warned that delays or conflicting official accounts can give rumours and manipulated claims room to spread. He cited figures indicating Nigeria had about 109 million internet users at the end of 2025 and estimated cybercrime losses of ₦1.1 trillion between 2017 and 2023. Brigadier General Murtala Abu, representing the Chief of Defence Staff, said cooperation in the field is incomplete without coordinated public communication. He also highlighted the risk that AI-generated audio, images and video could be used to deceive the public.

Participants raised concerns that deepfakes and organised disinformation could affect national security and public confidence, particularly ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kaduna State Commissioner for Information and Culture Ahmed Maiyaki, representing Governor Uba Sani, stressed the role of credible information in building trust. Speakers also recognised that some details may need to be withheld to protect operations, while warning that unexplained silence can fuel speculation.

The symposium’s communiqué proposed an Integrated National Crisis Information Architecture, supported by shared procedures for information exchange and public messaging. It also recommended tools to detect disinformation and deepfakes, improved digital literacy, and regulatory safeguards that protect security while respecting freedom of expression, fundamental rights and due process. The Centre unveiled the Nigerian Journal of Crisis Communication as a platform for research and practical guidance. Participants’ proposals, organisers said, will matter only if institutions put them into practice during future emergencies, sharing verified information promptly and communicating clearly without compromising sensitive operations.

title: ‘X-Men,’ ‘Star Trek’ Star Patrick Stewart Dies At 86
summary: Actor Patrick Stewart, known for “Star Trek” and “X-Men,” has died at 86. He died at home in Los Angeles after a brief journey with two conditions.
body:
Actor Patrick Stewart, best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in “X-Men” films, has died at 86. A statement said he died at his home in Los Angeles, with his wife, Sunny, by his side, after a brief period with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.

Born in Yorkshire in northern England, Stewart began his career on British stages with the Royal Shakespeare Company. He later moved across the Atlantic and built an acclaimed career in American theatre and film.

His performances ranged across genres. A statement described his voice and talent as closely associated with memorable roles, including his work in the Marvel films and as the captain of the Starship Enterprise.

title: Tinubu defends borrowing plans, says investments ‘ll expand opportunities for future generations
summary: President Bola Tinubu defended new loans from international institutions and banks amid opposition criticism. He said the investments would expand opportunities for future generations.
body:
President Bola Tinubu has responded to criticism, particularly from opposition leaders, over new loans Nigeria has accessed from international institutions and banks.

In an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” Tinubu defended the borrowing plans, saying the investments would expand opportunities for future generations.

The account provided no details about the loans’ amounts, terms or the specific projects they are intended to support.

title: Samson Adamu makes history as CAF confirms Nigerian as General Secretary
summary: Samson Adamu has been confirmed as CAF General Secretary, becoming the first Nigerian to hold the post in the organisation’s 70-year history. The NFF welcomed his appointment.
body:
Samson Adamu has been confirmed as the substantive General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), becoming the first Nigerian to hold the position in the organisation’s 70-year history. The confirmation was announced on Thursday, and the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) congratulated him on his appointment.

Emmanuel Ikpeme, the NFF’s acting general secretary, called the confirmation good news for Nigerian football administration. He said the federation was confident Adamu would succeed and described him as knowledgeable, committed to developing his expertise and experienced across football administration.

Ikpeme said the NFF was pleased with the appointment and would provide the necessary support to Adamu as a member association under CAF. He also wished him success in the role.

Adamu joined CAF, the governing body of African football, as director of competitions and later became director of tournaments and events. On 29 March, he took over as acting general secretary after Veron Mosengo-Omba resigned. His confirmation makes his interim role permanent and gives Nigeria its first holder of the post in CAF’s history.

title: [VIDEO] Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia
summary: Bola Tinubu arrived in Jeddah on Thursday night for Umrah after departing Abuja earlier that day. He is expected to return to Nigeria next week.
body:
President Bola Tinubu arrived in Saudi Arabia on Thursday night to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage to the Holy City. He landed at King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah after departing Abuja for Makkah on Thursday afternoon.

Tinubu was received at the airport by Nigeria’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and Saudi Arabia’s head of Royal Protocol, Ahmad bin Thafir.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, presidential media aide Bayo Onanuga said the trip would provide an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion and prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability and continued progress. Tinubu is to perform the religious rites associated with Umrah and seek Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people.

The President is expected to return to Nigeria next week.

title: Police nab masquerades for extorting residents in A’Ibom
summary: Police in Akwa Ibom arrested two Ekpo masquerade participants over alleged extortion and assaults in Ikot Ekpene. Investigators are seeking others linked to the case.
body:
Police in Akwa Ibom State have arrested two Ekpo masquerade participants over allegations of extorting and assaulting residents in Ikot Ekpene. The command said the suspects were detained at about 6 p.m. on Monday, October 26, along the Ukana/Abak highway during an operational show of force. The arrest was announced in a statement released by police spokesperson Timfom John on Thursday.

The suspects were identified as Ine Isong, 29, of Ukana Ikot Esoh Village, and Emmanuel Ekpenyong, 20, of Ikono Local Government Area. Police said they were allegedly found with Ekpo masquerade costumes and attire, as well as machetes, spears and arrows.

According to preliminary reports cited by police, the suspects and other people allegedly involved had been terrorising residents and demanding money from members of the public. The statement also said some people, particularly women, were reportedly assaulted. Police said investigations were continuing to establish what happened and identify others who may be connected to the alleged offences.

Commissioner of Police Baba Azare warned against using cultural practices or masquerade activities to intimidate, extort or harm people. He said the command respected lawful cultural traditions but would act against individuals or groups that took the law into their own hands or threatened residents’ safety.

title: [VIDEO] ‘Four-Year Presidency Is A Gamble,’ Okorocha Faults Obi’s One-Term Promise
summary: Rochas Okorocha called Peter Obi’s proposed four-year presidency a gamble. He urged South-East strategic alliances and backed Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.
body:
Former Imo State governor Rochas Okorocha has criticised Peter Obi’s proposed four-year presidency, calling it a gamble. Obi is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress.

Speaking in a television interview on Thursday, Okorocha said the South-East must learn to be strategic in its alliances. He did not provide further details about what alliances he had in mind.

Okorocha also voiced support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. The former lawmaker representing Imo West said Tinubu had done no wrong to any Igbo man.

title: Inter, AC Milan unveil new stadium plans to replace San Siro
summary: Inter and AC Milan unveiled plans for a 71,500-seat stadium to replace San Siro, with construction due to start in 2028. The €1.2 billion venue is planned to open in 2031/32.
body:
Inter and AC Milan have unveiled plans for a shared stadium to replace San Siro, with the new venue expected to open from the 2031/32 season. Named Generali Stadium after its sponsor, the project is scheduled to begin construction in 2028 and is expected to cost the clubs €1.2 billion.

The stadium will hold 71,500 spectators, compared with San Siro’s current capacity of 75,000. Its design, developed by architect Norman Foster and stadium specialist David Manica, is intended to bring fans closer to the pitch. Stands behind the goals will have a steep 37-degree incline, while the overall structure will sit low before rising at either end.

The roof will cover the stands while leaving the pitch exposed. Manica said the design team focused on proximity to the field and acoustics, with the roof intended to amplify crowd noise. He described the project as an effort to carry forward the atmosphere associated with San Siro, rather than simply reproduce its physical form. The venue is also designed to host American football, rugby and concerts.

The clubs paid €197 million to acquire the existing stadium and its adjacent parking areas, where they plan to build their new home. San Siro, also known as Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, opened in 1926 and is Italy’s largest stadium. Despite renovations over the decades, the clubs say the venue no longer meets their needs or those of spectators. It is expected to be largely demolished as construction of the new stadium nears completion.

title: APC youth support group urges unity, warns against divisions ahead of 2027 elections
summary: An APC youth support group has backed National Youth Leader Dayo Israel and urged members to resolve disputes through party channels. It called for unity ahead of 2027.
body:
The All Progressives Congress National Young Stakeholders Forum has urged members of the party’s youth wing to respect internal procedures and avoid actions that could deepen divisions ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group also expressed support for National Youth Leader Dayo Israel and called on party youths to focus on mobilising for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

At a press conference in Abuja on Thursday, the forum’s National Publicity Secretary, Shehu Attah, said disagreements should be handled by the appropriate party authorities. He cautioned against factional manoeuvres and efforts to establish competing centres of authority, saying such actions could cast doubt on the recognised youth leadership. The forum did not name the people or groups it said were challenging Israel’s office.

The appeal follows public scrutiny of a video Israel posted and later deleted, which showed seven new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado vehicles reportedly allocated to youth leaders for campaign activities. The vehicles prompted questions about resources for political mobilisation. Remi Tinubu had also disclosed that utility vehicles, campaign materials and footwear were being provided for APC youth leaders.

The forum passed a vote of confidence in Israel, describing his office as a link between the party leadership and young members. Attah credited him with initiatives including the APC Youth House, the Nest Resource Centre and Renewed Hope Conversations programmes at tertiary institutions. He also said more than 100 party youths and youth leaders had taken part in overseas training and capacity-building programmes over the past two years.

The group commended Israel’s role in facilitating campaign vehicles for selected youth leaders and the earlier distribution of buses to other party members. Attah said the initiatives had improved morale and addressed calls for greater recognition, while warning that factional disputes could discourage young people seeking a place in the party. The forum urged members to let recognised party structures operate as preparations for the 2027 elections advance.

title: No confusion, Osun will vote Accord candidates, Tinubu for president — Adeleke
summary: Ademola Adeleke says Osun voters should back Bola Tinubu for president in 2027 and Accord candidates for assembly seats. He urged full campaign loyalty.
body:
Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has said voters should support Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election while choosing Accord Party candidates for the National and State Assembly elections. He said the split in support would not confuse voters, despite the “Rainbow Coalition” effort to mobilise backing for Tinubu’s re-election, led by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike.

Adeleke made the remarks on Thursday in Ede while inaugurating a campaign committee for the re-election of Osun West Senator Lere Oyewumi. The governor was represented by his deputy, Kola Adewusi. Adeleke praised Oyewumi, the Senate’s Deputy Minority Leader, and urged committee members to work fully behind his campaign.

Oyewumi credited Adeleke’s leadership and performance with strengthening Accord’s acceptance in Osun. He said the governor’s re-election reflected public support and would help the party’s candidates. Oyewumi also pledged further development in Osun West, including better roads, schools and hospitals, access to clean water and solar streetlights.

Campaign committee Director-General Adesoye Oyetunde praised Oyewumi’s record, saying roads had been tarred in eight of the district’s 10 local government areas, with work launched in the other two. He also cited classroom construction, healthcare support and farm inputs for constituents. Adeleke joined Accord after leaving the Peoples Democratic Party in December 2025. He won re-election on the Accord platform in August, defeating the All Progressives Congress candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, and has also voiced support for Tinubu’s second-term bid.

title: 2027: Makinde visits South-east, speaks on Peter Obi, Igbo’s votes
summary: Seyi Makinde urged South-east voters to look beyond ethnic and religious loyalties in 2027. He outlined his agenda and said his manifesto was due on 4 November 2026.
body:
Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde urged voters in the South-east not to make their choices in the 2027 election on ethnic or religious grounds. Speaking at an Allied Peoples Movement (APM) town hall in Enugu on Thursday, he said the challenges facing Nigeria affected people regardless of their identity.

Makinde, the APM’s presidential candidate, acknowledged that Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate and a former Anambra governor, had strong ties to the region. He said his team had been discouraged from visiting because the South-east was considered Obi’s territory, but that he had come to present his Reset Agenda for Nigeria. He called on voters to reject divisions based on religion or ethnicity.

Makinde said he had held town hall meetings across the country’s six geopolitical zones before releasing his manifesto, arguing that the meetings helped him understand people’s needs. He described the Enugu gathering as the final one and said the manifesto would be prepared over the weekend and launched on 4 November 2026. He outlined four pillars for his agenda: the economy, security, education and socio-political issues. He also promised to govern sincerely, work to rebuild trust between leaders and citizens, and provide an environment in which businesses could thrive. He said youth skills training would support job creation and help reduce unemployment.

At the meeting, South-east campaign coordinator Okechukwu Obiechina said bad leadership had contributed to hardship, including difficulties meeting food, fuel and school-fee costs. APM National Chairman Yusuf Dantalle criticised President Bola Tinubu’s record since his 2023 election and called on him to step aside from the 2027 race. Dantalle also described Makinde, whom he identified as 58, as a candidate representing the youth population. APM vice-presidential candidate Lawal Daura said the party intended to address national challenges through a 16-point agenda and reform the system for the benefit of Nigerians.

title: RCIM share disposal records good progress as investor demand remains robust
summary: RCIM has transferred about 5.2 billion FirstHoldCo shares to investors in a secondary-market disposal. Further transfers await approvals and execution steps.
body:
First HoldCo Plc and RC Investment Management Limited (RCIM) say they have made significant progress in transferring a large block of FirstHoldCo shares held by RCIM as an independent Bridge Holder. The disposal is an orderly transfer of existing shares through the Nigerian Exchange (NGX), rather than a new share issue.

RCIM acquired approximately 10.43 billion FirstHoldCo shares on the NGX in July 2025 under a Central Bank of Nigeria-approved shareholder divestment arrangement. About 5.2 billion shares have since been crossed to subscribers. Further transfers are expected once the required regulatory approvals are secured and the remaining execution processes are completed.

The companies said the large trading volumes in FirstHoldCo shares reflect, to a substantial extent, the transfer of RCIM’s holding to investors. They described subscriptions and the absorption of the sizeable block as evidence of continued investor confidence, citing the group’s financial performance, fundamentals and long-term growth prospects.

The statement also pointed to shareholder returns. On a total shareholder return basis, First HoldCo ranks first among the FUGAZ banking groups, with returns of more than 200% from the beginning of January 2026 to date, it said. The disposal is intended to complete the divestment programme in an orderly manner and broaden FirstHoldCo’s investor base.

title: 2027: Kaduna APC rally won’t erase poverty, insecurity – PRP
summary: The PRP criticised the APC’s Kaduna rally, saying it would not distract from poverty and insecurity. It also called for action over a cleric’s killing.
body:
The Peoples Redemption Party has criticised the All Progressives Congress over its rally in Kaduna, saying campaign events cannot divert attention from poverty and insecurity. In a statement issued in Abuja, PRP National Chairman Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed described the gathering as an expensive effort to project support for the ruling party ahead of the 2027 general elections. He questioned the alleged spending on the event, but the statement did not provide evidence for the amount or establish how it was funded.

Baba-Ahmed said economic hardship and security concerns would remain central to public debate, and argued that political gatherings could not substitute for a record of effective government. He said Nigerians should not interpret the rally as proof that they were satisfied with the APC’s performance. The criticism comes as parties begin positioning themselves ahead of the next general election, when the Tinubu administration’s record is expected to feature in political debate.

The PRP chairman also raised concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s health and called for close medical scrutiny and management. The statement offered no medical evidence to support those concerns. Baba-Ahmed further alleged that attacks and abductions continued during the rally, including abductions from homes in Kaduna metropolis, while police were deployed to protect billboards at the event.

He condemned the killing of Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka at his home in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, and called for those responsible to be arrested and prosecuted. Baba-Ahmed said citizens had a right to expect protection regardless of their political views, and urged the government to prioritise security and welfare. He maintained that a credible election in 2027 would end the APC’s leadership, while saying Nigerians would continue to demand safety and dignified living conditions in the meantime.

title: Seplat discovers 157 billion cubic feet of gas, 19 million barrels of oil in Nigeria
summary: Seplat estimates Aku-01 holds 157 Bcf of gas and 19 million barrels of oil in place. It plans further evaluation and another exploration well in 2027.
body:
Seplat Energy has reported an estimated 157 billion cubic feet of natural gas and 19 million barrels of oil in place at its Aku-01 exploration well in Nigeria. The company disclosed the find on October 29 in unaudited results for the nine months to September 30, 2026. The discovery occurred after the period ended.

The oil was unexpected: Seplat said its original exploration programme anticipated natural gas, but not crude oil. Preliminary assessments indicate substantial hydrocarbon resources, though further work is needed to establish how much can be commercially recovered. Seplat is working to complete the well for potential future production and plans to connect it to existing infrastructure to support early development.

The discovery has lowered exploration uncertainty across four nearby prospects in the licence area, the company said. Seplat plans to drill a second exploration well in the Aku area in 2027. It holds a 40% operated interest in Petroleum Prospecting Licence 2A25, where Aku-01 is located.

For the nine-month period, Seplat’s combined working-interest production averaged 144,999 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 7% from a year earlier. Average crude oil and condensate output rose about 1.4% to 103,173 barrels per day, while natural gas production increased 11.6% to 194.9 million standard cubic feet per day. Natural gas liquids output more than doubled, reaching 8,222 barrels per day.

Revenue rose to N3.78 trillion from N3.36 trillion in the same period of 2025. Pre-tax profit increased 52.75% to N1.34 trillion, compared with N878.99 billion a year earlier. Seplat declared a third-quarter dividend of 19 US cents per share, comprising a 5-cent core dividend and a 14-cent special dividend. That brought dividends declared for the first nine months of 2026 to 40 US cents per share.

title: Ondo govt appoints committee for Fasoranti’s burial
summary: Ondo State named a committee led by Kayode Ajulo to coordinate Reuben Fasoranti’s state burial with his family and Afenifere. His family set Dec. 17 for the funeral.
body:
The Ondo State Government has appointed a committee to coordinate a state burial for Reuben Fasoranti, the late Afenifere leader who died on 20 October at the age of 100. The committee is to work with his family and Afenifere’s leadership to arrange a dignified farewell. The government has not announced a date or detailed programme for the state burial; the family has scheduled the funeral service and interment for 17 December.

Kayode Ajulo, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, will chair the committee, with Eniola Olushola as secretary. Its other members are Gbenga Fasua, Gbenga Atiba, Kosemani Kolawole, Bakkita Bello, Idowu Otetubi, Modupe Martins, George Asonja, Muyiwa Ogunyemi, Stephen Abitogun and Adetunji Gbenga.

The committee’s formation was announced in a statement by Ebenezer Adeniyan, the governor’s Chief Press Secretary. The statement said the government approved the state burial in recognition of Fasoranti’s contributions to Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria. Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa believes the late elder statesman should be honoured for his years of service, wisdom and selfless leadership, it added.

Fasoranti was an educationist and a prominent figure in progressive politics and the struggle for democracy. His political career was associated with Obafemi Awolowo’s tradition, including the defunct Action Group and later the Unity Party of Nigeria. He served as commissioner for finance in the government of Ondo State Governor Adekunle Ajasin from 1979 to 1983, and later became one of the leading figures in Afenifere.

Separately, on Wednesday, the Senate considered a motion by Adeniyi Adegbonmire, who represents Ondo Central, urging the federal government to name an educational institution after Fasoranti in recognition of his contributions to education and national development.

title: Carrick not surprised he’s still Man Utd manager
summary: Michael Carrick said he was not surprised to remain Manchester United manager and needs no assurances, despite an eight-game winless run. United face Chelsea on Saturday.
body:
Michael Carrick said he was not surprised to remain Manchester United manager despite mounting pressure over the club’s results. Speaking ahead of Saturday’s away match against Chelsea, he said his focus was on improving the team and that he did not need assurances from the club’s leadership about his future.

United have gone eight games without a win. Their 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday left them one point above the Premier League relegation zone. The club have won two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, while seven points from their first eight league games marks their worst start to a league campaign in 40 years.

Carrick’s position has drawn scrutiny during the run of poor results. Bruno Fernandes was left out of the starting line-up against Bournemouth after criticising Carrick’s tactics following a 4-1 defeat by Como. Carrick described the decision to bench the United captain as one made for that game and said Fernandes remained committed to the club.

Carrick received applause from supporters as he left the pitch after the Bournemouth match, while players were booed. Former United captain Gary Neville said earlier on Thursday that sometimes a manager needs to be sacked for their own good. Carrick said he would not walk away, adding that he understood the responsibility of the role and cared about what supporters saw from the team. He said the players were hurting over their results but remained hungry to improve.

title: Minister demands results from colleges of education under dual mandate
summary: Education Minister Tunji Alausa urged colleges to show measurable gains under the dual mandate. Eligible colleges can offer the NCE and approved education degrees.
body:
Education Minister Tunji Alausa has urged provosts of colleges of education to demonstrate results under the dual-mandate policy, with stronger accountability and improved teacher preparation. He said the reform could strengthen colleges and widen opportunities for academic and professional advancement, but would require strategic leadership and cooperation among stakeholders.

Alausa’s remarks were delivered by Dr Cecilia Uba, the Federal Ministry of Education’s Director of Colleges of Education, at the National Commission for Colleges of Education Teacher Education Leadership and Impact Award ceremony in Abuja on Thursday. The event, held in partnership with Gosima Group, was part of the commission’s retreat and workshop on implementing the dual mandate and its strategic plan. The policy allows eligible colleges to offer both the Nigeria Certificate in Education and approved bachelor’s degree programmes in education.

The minister reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to working with the NCCE, provosts and other stakeholders to improve the quality and relevance of teacher education. He also said award recipients should treat the recognition as a call to greater responsibility, innovation and service. NCCE Executive Secretary Dr Angela Ajala urged colleges to improve performance, strengthen teacher preparation, support research and adopt digital innovation, while pursuing academic excellence and financial sustainability.

Former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim said teacher education was important to national development and called for modern facilities, sustainable funding and stronger professional development. Gosima Group President and Group Managing Director Dr Gideon Chidiebere Osi said the company planned to expand scholarships for deserving students through its charitable foundation. He said its partnership with the NCCE would support educational leadership and teacher education through scholarships, mentorship and youth leadership development.

title: Police Foil Kidnap Plot In Kano, Arrest Two Suspects
summary: Kano police say they arrested two suspects over a threat to kidnap a village head in Gezawa. Investigations are continuing ahead of a court arraignment.
body:
Police in Kano State say they have foiled an attempted kidnapping in Gezawa Local Government Area and arrested two suspects accused of threatening to abduct the village head of Bangare, Mallam Idris. The suspects were arrested by officers attached to the Gezawa Division during intelligence-led operations.

According to a statement from police spokesperson CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, Idris reported the threat on October 26, 2026. He told police he had received a threatening phone call from an unidentified caller on October 24 at about 9:33 p.m.

The command said officers acted after receiving the report and arrested the suspects following sustained follow-up and intelligence-led work. Police said the suspects had confessed to the crime, while investigations continued ahead of their arraignment in court.

Kano State Commissioner of Police CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori commended the officers for their response and reiterated the command’s zero-tolerance stance on criminal activity. He said the operation reflected the Inspector-General of Police’s emphasis on intelligence-led and technology-driven policing, professionalism and proactive crime prevention. The command urged residents to stay vigilant and report suspicious people or movements to the nearest police station.

title: 2027: Abia CP warns politicians against violence, intimidation
summary: Abia police chief Wilfred Afolabi urged parties to avoid violence and notify police before rallies. INEC pledged neutrality and advised candidates to challenge results in court.
body:
Abia State Commissioner of Police Wilfred Afolabi has urged political parties and their supporters to avoid violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and property damage ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also asked parties to notify police in writing before holding rallies, processions and other political activities so security arrangements can be made.

Afolabi spoke at a peace accord signing in Umuahia attended by the Independent National Electoral Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioner, Prof. Sylvia Agu, representatives of security agencies, registered political parties and campaign teams. The accord was read to participants after the police command’s legal officer reviewed relevant electoral laws. Party representatives then signed, pledging to pursue their political ambitions peacefully.

The police commissioner said the command was committed to providing professional and impartial security for all candidates, parties and supporters. He said police had strengthened security through intelligence gathering and analysis, crime mapping, a revamped Cybercrime Unit and improved operational response. Afolabi also acknowledged Governor Alex Otti’s directive on security for campaigns and related activities, and pledged continued cooperation with INEC, security agencies and political stakeholders to protect lives and property.

Agu said INEC would serve all candidates equally and provide a level playing field. She urged candidates to maintain peace before, during and after the election, and to accept the outcome of a free, fair and credible poll. Those dissatisfied with the results, she said, should seek redress through the courts rather than resort to violence or undermine the electoral process. Agu said the accord was intended to prevent conflict by committing signatories to peaceful conduct throughout the election period.

title: Ethiopia receives Russian fighter jets, air defence systems
summary: Ethiopia says it has received 12 Russian Su-35 jets and expects four S-400 systems. The deliveries come amid renewed fighting in Tigray.
body:
Ethiopia has received 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets and expects four S-400 air-defence systems, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said. The deliveries are intended to strengthen the country’s military capabilities as fighting intensifies in the northern Tigray region. The S-400 systems are expected but have not been reported as delivered.

Abiy said the aircraft were supplied under an earlier agreement with the Russian government and arrived a year ahead of schedule. He described the delivery as a milestone in efforts to strengthen national security, and said the jets would support Ethiopia’s sovereignty as well as regional security and stability. He also said Ethiopia had become the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to possess this type of advanced combat technology.

The announcement coincided with the start of a two-day Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, which Abiy is attending. The gathering is described as an effort by Russian President Vladimir Putin to expand Russia’s presence in Africa. Abiy has called Putin a close friend of Ethiopia.

The military deliveries come amid renewed clashes between Ethiopian government forces and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front. TPLF forces had taken control of Mekelle and Alula Aba Nega Airport, but government and allied forces retook Mekelle on Sunday after the group said it had temporarily left the regional capital to operate elsewhere. Eritrean troops crossed into Tigray in early October, adding to tensions and concerns about a wider regional conflict.

title: Argentine football fan jailed for threatening Di Maria over return
summary: A Rosario court sentenced Sergio Di Vanni to 7.5 years for threats aimed at deterring Angel Di Maria’s return to Argentina. Di Maria joined Rosario Central in 2025.
body:
A court in Rosario sentenced football supporter Sergio Di Vanni to seven and a half years in prison on Wednesday for directing threats at Angel Di Maria’s family. The court found the 45-year-old guilty of ordering intimidation intended to dissuade the former Argentina international from returning from abroad to play for Rosario Central, his boyhood club.

The threats took place in March 2024, when Di Maria was playing for Benfica and considering a return to Argentina. They included gunshots fired near a gated community where he owns a property, as well as a pig’s head marked by a bullet wound left outside an estate agency run by his sister. A message threatening his daughter was also reported.

Prosecutors identified 25-year-old Belen Gutierrez as one of the people involved. She was sentenced to three and a half years in prison in June after reaching a plea agreement. A third suspect remains in pre-trial detention. Prosecutors alleged the threats were carried out in exchange for four million pesos, equivalent to $2,600, and linked the campaign to an internal power struggle among supporters of Newell’s Old Boys. Di Vanni’s sentence also covers separate offences connected to his involvement in the supporters’ group.

Rosario Central and Newell’s Old Boys are the city’s two major clubs and fierce rivals. Di Maria initially dropped plans to return to Argentina because of concerns for his family’s safety, but later changed his mind and joined Rosario Central in 2025. He has spent the past two seasons at the club, which won the Argentine title at the end of 2025.

title: Naira holds the N1350/$ baseline despite attractive US yields
summary: The naira settled at N1,349 per dollar as the Fed held rates, keeping US yields attractive and limiting portfolio inflows. Oil receipts and CBN intervention support the currency.
body:
The naira settled at N1,349 per dollar in midweek trading after the US Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged and signalled that borrowing costs could remain high. The decision supports the appeal of US assets, with Treasury yields near 5%, and the dollar index trading around 102.25 in early European hours on Thursday.

High US yields have helped constrain foreign portfolio investment into Nigerian bonds and other local assets, limiting one potential source of foreign exchange. At the same time, attractive nominal returns in Nigeria’s bond market may encourage risk-conscious investors to keep their holdings in naira, rather than convert them into dollars. The balance between those forces is one factor shaping the exchange rate.

Oil earnings provide another source of support. Nigerian crude was reported at about $115 a barrel, and higher export revenues could help the Central Bank of Nigeria build gross reserves and strengthen its capacity to manage external shocks. The CBN has also supplied foreign exchange directly to dealer banks to address backlogs and support liquidity in the market.

The exchange rate is expected to move within a N1,340–1,370 per dollar range in the near term, with CBN intervention and oil inflows providing support. Traders are also watching the next CBN Monetary Policy Committee meeting for signs of whether Nigerian rates could be cut, which might narrow the positive real-rate gap with the United States.

In the US, policymakers said they would rely on incoming data when deciding their next steps. Market attention is focused on the September personal consumption expenditures inflation report, due Friday. If inflation rises again and prompts the Fed to resume rate increases, outflows from Nigerian local debt could intensify, adding pressure to the naira.

title: Tinubu To Induct Five Helicopters Acquired By NAF
summary: President Bola Tinubu is expected to induct five new Nigerian Air Force helicopters in Abuja. He is also set to commission the reconstructed hangar housing them.
body:
President Bola Tinubu is expected to induct five helicopters acquired by the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) at a ceremony in Abuja. He is also expected to commission the service’s newly reconstructed hangar, where the aircraft are housed.

The helicopters comprise two H-125s manufactured by Airbus Helicopters and three AW-109 Trekker Bs made by Italy’s Leonardo Helicopters. The induction is scheduled to take place at the hangar on the presidential wing of Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport.

The NAF received the aircraft in stages. The two H-125 helicopters had been delivered earlier, while the three AW-109 Trekker Bs arrived in Lagos as part of a separate batch of 10 helicopters acquired by the Federal Government. The other seven aircraft in that batch are expected to be delivered before the end of 2026.

The acquisition is part of the Federal Government’s investment in strengthening the air force’s operational capabilities. It also comes amid broader efforts to modernise and re-equip the Armed Forces to respond to evolving security threats and sustain operations against insecurity.

title: Tell Nigerians your real destination, APM challenges Tinubu
summary: The APM urged President Bola Tinubu to disclose his destination and stay in Nigeria to address hardship. It also questioned his 2027 electoral prospects.
body:
Tell Nigerians your real destination, APM challenges Tinubu

The Allied People’s Movement (APM) has called on President Bola Tinubu to disclose his actual destination and remain in Nigeria to address the difficulties facing citizens. The party questioned whether the announced lesser Hajj pilgrimage was the full purpose of his trip, arguing that the country’s problems required attention at home.

In a statement, APM National Publicity Secretary Abubakar Yusuf said the pilgrimage should be devoted to prayer and supplication, not used as a cover for other activities. He accused Tinubu’s administration of worsening hardship and said the President should focus on resolving what he described as burdens placed on ordinary Nigerians.

Yusuf also invoked the expression “Andrew, check out,” urging Tinubu not to leave the country. The party’s appeal tied its criticism of the proposed trip to its broader contention that the President should address domestic challenges rather than depart while citizens face hardship.

Looking ahead to the 2027 presidential election, Yusuf said Tinubu could struggle to win at least 25 per cent of votes in 12 selected states. He expressed confidence that the APM’s presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, would defeat the President, describing Makinde as a hardworking and energetic contender. Yusuf also said Makinde could challenge Tinubu’s political strength in the South-West and elsewhere in the South.

title: Akpabio alleges payment for social media attacks on Tinubu
summary: Senate President Godswill Akpabio urged northern youths to campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election. He alleged some online critics are paid.
body:
Senate President Godswill Akpabio has urged young people in northern Nigeria to build grassroots support for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 election. He made the appeal on Wednesday during a visit to his office by the Arewa Revival Project, a group with members from the 19 northern states. The group presented Akpabio with an award for his contributions to nation-building.

Akpabio alleged that some people criticising Tinubu and his supporters on social media were being paid, while the young people he addressed were not. He encouraged them to convene youth groups and engage people directly, saying they should challenge what he described as propaganda and explain the case for continuity in government. The allegation was not accompanied by evidence in the account of his remarks.

He defended the administration’s economic policies, including tax reforms, and said the government was seeking to move Nigeria away from reliance on crude oil. Akpabio praised Tinubu’s handling of challenges and said he and members of the National Assembly had given the President a pass mark and endorsed him for a second term. The 2027 election is expected to include Tinubu seeking re-election, with opposition parties aiming to challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress.

Akpabio also addressed insecurity and the proposed creation of state police. He said the constitutional amendment process was nearing completion and claimed about 30 state assemblies had endorsed the proposal. He predicted a decentralised policing system could be established within a month, while expressing confidence that the country would overcome its security challenges. Earlier, Arewa Revival Project coordinator Mustafa Ibrahim said the award recognised Akpabio’s national contributions and the National Assembly’s work under his leadership.

title: Katsina APC declares Funtua campaign peaceful amid reports of attacks in Malumfashi
summary: Katsina APC said its Funtua campaign launch was peaceful, while reports described attacks on supporters travelling through Malumfashi. Injury and damage totals remain unclear.
body:
The All Progressives Congress in Katsina State described Wednesday’s Tinubu–Dikko 2027 campaign launch in Funtua as peaceful, saying no clashes, injuries or property losses were recorded at the Funtua Township Stadium. The party’s state chairman, Bishir Saulawa, thanked Governor Dikko Radda, security agencies, party members and other stakeholders for their conduct at the event.

Separate reports described attacks on supporters travelling to Funtua through Malumfashi Local Government Area. Some supporters alleged that groups of youths threw stones and bottles and used other weapons. Those affected reported injuries and lost belongings, while some vehicles had damaged windscreens. Stones were also reported around the Malumfashi town roundabout, near the road linking Bakori Local Government Area.

The reported incidents were along the route to the campaign, not necessarily at the stadium. The APC chairman’s statement did not address the allegations or clarify whether his account covered supporters travelling to the event. The number of people injured, the extent of the damage and who carried out the attacks have not been established.

At the launch, Radda urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu and APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. He identified security, infrastructure, education, healthcare and economic opportunities as priorities, and called on candidates and supporters to campaign peacefully and respect voters’ choices. Deputy Governor Faruk Jobe, former governors Aminu Masari and Ibrahim Shema, lawmakers and other party stakeholders attended. Saulawa presented party flags and banners to candidates for three Senate seats, 15 House of Representatives seats and 34 State Assembly seats.

title: Spain Begins Three-Day Mourning After Latest Train Tragedy Kills 68
summary: Spain began three days of mourning after a train collision killed 68 people and injured scores. Investigators face questions about a reported rail-control failure.
body:
Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday after a collision between two high-speed trains in Castilla-La Mancha killed 68 people and injured scores. The crash happened on Wednesday morning on the line connecting Madrid and Seville, when a Renfe train struck the back of a stationary train operated by Iryo. Emergency crews searched the wreckage overnight, using cranes to move twisted metal as they looked for further victims.

Passengers described severe impacts and chaotic scenes inside the Renfe train. One survivor said he woke to find himself thrown into the air; another, who suffered head injuries, said a last-minute seat change may have saved his life. In the nearby village of Urda, a school was opened for relatives seeking information. Red Cross teams provided support, while Civil Guard offices in Madrid, Toledo, Cordoba and Seville collected DNA samples to help identify missing people. Blood donation points were also established in Castilla-La Mancha and Madrid.

Transport Minister Oscar Puente said an automatic control system had failed along 69 kilometres of track, leading to trains being stopped. He said the control centre then resumed traffic despite circumstances he described as inexplicable. According to Puente, the Renfe train travelled 25 kilometres before hitting the Iryo, and the control centre had time to identify and address the error. The cause of the collision has not been established in the supplied account.

The disaster has renewed scrutiny of rail safety in Spain. In January, a derailment in Andalusia led to two high-speed trains colliding after one crossed onto an adjacent track; 46 people died. That investigation remains ongoing, and the government has faced criticism over its management of the rail network. Families of those killed and missing now face a difficult process of identification and grief, with support workers warning that people will respond to the loss in different ways.

title: 2027: Fubara urges Rivers monarchs to remain neutral
summary: Rivers Governor Siminalayi Fubara urged traditional rulers to promote fairness and peace ahead of the 2027 elections. He also addressed their welfare requests.
body:
Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara has urged traditional rulers to remain fair and promote peace as political activity increases ahead of the 2027 general elections. He made the appeal while opening the 126th, 127th and 128th combined quarterly meeting of the Rivers State Council of Traditional Rulers in Port Harcourt on Wednesday.

Fubara said traditional leaders’ roles in administering justice and ensuring fairness made it important for them to avoid conduct that could divide communities or trigger crises. He asked them to honour the oaths and constitution they accepted before taking their stools, and to put Rivers State’s interests above personal sentiments. He said prioritising the state’s interests was also a principle he applied in governing.

Addressing requests for improved welfare, Fubara said delays in meeting some past requests were due to the council’s inability to organise its own affairs, rather than a failure by the state government. He also said stipends paid to traditional rulers by local government councils were a statutory benefit under the constitution, which a governor could not change through a verbal announcement. Fubara said he would fulfil his promises to the rulers before leaving office next year.

Earlier, council chairman and Paramount Ruler of Apara Kingdom, Chike Amadi Worlu Wodo, thanked the state government for maintaining cordial relations with the traditional institution. He said rulers were well placed to help resolve disputes because of their proximity to communities, including conflicts over chieftaincy, family matters and land ownership.

title: ALTON urges states to scrap telecoms right-of-way fees
summary: ALTON says right-of-way fees can make up 50–60% of fibre costs in some states and wants free access, especially in underserved rural areas. It also seeks targeted incentives.
body:
The Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON) has called on state governments to abolish right-of-way charges for telecommunications infrastructure. The association says the fees can account for as much as 60 per cent of fibre-optic deployment costs in some states, making it harder to extend networks to underserved communities. Right-of-way charges are fees for permission to install infrastructure on public or private land and roads.

ALTON Chairman Gbenga Adebayo made the appeal on Tuesday at the 2026 Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja. He said that in some states the charges represent 50 to 60 per cent of the cost of deploying a kilometre of fibre. That expense, he argued, can make projects difficult to justify in places where expected revenue is unlikely to cover construction costs.

Adebayo urged lawmakers to establish free access for telecommunications infrastructure, particularly in rural communities and other areas with limited commercial prospects. He also called for incentives for operators investing where deployment costs exceed likely returns. The Universal Service Provision Fund, which is intended to support areas lacking coverage, could be used more strategically, he said. Adebayo rejected the view that operators were unwilling to invest in rural areas, pointing instead to the economics of building networks there.

He also called for more investment in fibre-optic cables, telecommunications sites and network capacity, saying infrastructure is needed to improve service quality and support emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. At the same summit, Senate ICT and Cybersecurity Committee Chairman Shuaib Salisu said the National Digital Economy and E-Government Bill had reached its third reading and that lawmakers were working on cybersecurity reforms and reviewing the Data Protection Act. He also pointed to the government’s planned 90,000-kilometre fibre network as a way to extend connectivity to underserved communities. Salisu urged businesses to engage lawmakers early so legislation reflects industry conditions and investment needs.

title: CBD COP17: Why African countries struggle to mobilise biodiversity funding – AfDB official
summary: African governments need to embed biodiversity in national investment plans and fund implementation, an AfDB official said at CBD COP17. Fragmented finance and competing priorities remain barriers.
body:
African governments should make biodiversity conservation a central part of national investment priorities and provide resources to carry out commitments, African Development Bank (AfDB) official Arona Soumare said during a discussion on the sidelines of CBD COP17 in Yerevan, Armenia. Soumare, the bank’s Chief Climate Change and Green Growth Officer, said countries often approach development financiers for other priorities, with biodiversity treated as an additional element rather than a main investment objective.

The panel, organised by the World Wide Fund for Nature, examined findings from Africa’s seventh national reports on progress and gaps in delivering the Global Biodiversity Framework. Soumare said governments needed to move beyond commitments under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and show their intent through concrete funding and investment decisions. He said the bank had received many biodiversity project proposals from external organisations, while strong proposals led by African governments were less common.

Soumare described the fragmentation of funding across development sectors as a major obstacle. The AfDB works with countries through Country Strategy Papers, which set out national development priorities and help shape the bank’s investment portfolios. He said biodiversity should be integrated into those priorities alongside areas such as infrastructure, food security and livelihoods, rather than handled separately. Madagascar, he said, offered an example of how country allocations could support private-sector initiatives for national parks and help attract further finance.

He called for financing that could serve both large conservation programmes and smaller community-led projects. While the bank offers funding opportunities to grassroots organisations, available resources do not meet demand: Soumare said a call for proposals might receive enough funding for only three of every 10 applications. He also pointed to blended finance, green banks, green credit lines and nature-related bonds as ways to channel more investment into conservation.

Daniel Mukubi, of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, also identified inadequate financing as a constraint. He said conservation competes with urgent needs including food security, energy, infrastructure and poverty reduction. Regional cooperation, he added, can help build institutional capacity. He cited training for technical experts in geographic information systems and biodiversity mapping, which could support planning for the global goal of conserving at least 30 per cent of land, inland waters and coastal and marine areas by 2030.

title: Solid Minerals: FG Inaugurates Nigeria-US Committee On Strategic Cooperation
summary: Nigeria has inaugurated a committee to advance its minerals partnership with the US. Minister Dele Alake denied claims that Nigeria sold $700 billion in minerals.
body:
The Federal Government has inaugurated the Nigeria-United States Committee on Strategic Cooperation in the Solid Minerals Sector in Abuja, weeks after the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding on developing Nigeria’s mining industry. The committee is intended to advance the partnership and identify ways to turn the agreement into practical outcomes.

Solid Minerals Development Minister Dele Alake rejected claims that Nigeria had sold $700 billion worth of solid minerals to the United States. He said Nigeria had not sold its mineral assets and described the agreement as a government-to-government framework intended to connect American investors with Nigerian businesses.

The memorandum was signed in September on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Alake signed for Nigeria with US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau at the Nigerian Mission House in New York. The stated areas of cooperation include attracting investment, sharing technology, expanding local processing and creating jobs.

Alake said the government wants mineral resources to generate more value within Nigeria and contribute to the country’s effort to reduce its dependence on oil. Local processing, he said, is now a key requirement for investors seeking mineral titles. He also said the partnership could bring together Nigeria’s resources with US capital and technology to support the mining sector.

The minister called on the committee to work diligently, identify viable investment opportunities and produce measurable results in support of President Bola Tinubu’s $1 trillion economy target. At the signing, Alake said implementation of the agreement would support the administration’s economic diversification agenda and promote industrial growth. Landau was quoted as supporting a US partnership with Nigeria.

title: AU accredits Nigeria’s counter-terrorism centre for West Africa
summary: The AU accredited Nigeria’s counter-terrorism centre as a regional hub for West Africa and the Sahel. Its renewable three-year mandate includes training and threat analysis.
body:
The African Union has accredited Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) as an African Union Regional Centre of Excellence in Counter Terrorism for West Africa and the Sahel. The designation expands the centre’s role in supporting AU member states through specialised training, joint threat analysis, research, technical assistance and exchanges of lessons learned.

The accreditation was announced on October 27, 2026, at the conclusion of the African Lessons Learned Forum in Abuja. The Acting Director of the African Union Counter Terrorism Centre, Dr Idriss Mounir Lallali, said the recognition followed an assessment of the NCTC’s governance, institutional capacity, training programmes, analytical capabilities, coordination mechanisms and adherence to human rights and the rule of law. The accreditation will initially run for three years and may be renewed.

The process began with a memorandum of understanding between the AU and the NCTC in September 2025. A technical assessment mission in Abuja in December that year produced a roadmap setting out the institutional requirements for accreditation. The NCTC subsequently strengthened its governance structures, training curricula, operational procedures, analytical and coordination functions, and human-rights safeguards.

The centre operates under Nigeria’s Office of the National Security Adviser. Its regional role reflects President Bola Tinubu’s vision, announced at a high-level African counter-terrorism meeting in Abuja in April 2024, to develop the NCTC as a hub for intelligence sharing, operational coordination, training and capacity building.

National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, represented at the event by NCTC National Coordinator Major General Adamu Garba Laka, described the accreditation as both recognition of Nigeria’s progress and a responsibility to contribute further to collective African security. Ribadu said the Federal Government and the Office of the National Security Adviser would support the expanded mandate through staffing, sustainable resources and institutional partnerships, while maintaining compliance with accreditation standards.
